What we covered in the first week: letters of the Elif and Khâ groups; “My religion is Islam” (Camiye Gidiyorum 1, pp. 11–16); “The pillars of Islam” (pp. 17–24); “I get to know our Prophet (s.a.s.)” (pp. 37–42); “My religion recommends kind words and good conduct” (pp. 25–30).
At home:
• Read these pages of the book together; your child should be able to name the five pillars of Islam in order (declaration of faith, prayer, fasting, zakat, hajj).
• Make greeting people with salam a habit, at home and outside.
• Next lesson: Saturday 12 September at 11:00. Please remind your child to bring the book, notebook and pen.

2026-09-12|odev.t:
Revision at home (7–11 September):
• Elifbâ: revise the letters of the Elif and Khâ groups briefly every day; have your child write the letters in the notebook and say their names.
• Camiye Gidiyorum 1: read “My religion is Islam” (pp. 11–16) and “The pillars of Islam” (pp. 17–24) together; your child should be able to name the five pillars of Islam in order (declaration of faith, prayer, fasting, zakat, hajj).
• Read “I get to know our Prophet (s.a.s.)” (pp. 37–42) and the section on greeting (pp. 25–30); make greeting people with salam a habit at home.
Preparing for the weekend lessons (12–13 September): the letters of the Shîn and Ayn groups; “Our holy book is the Qur’an” (pp. 31–36), “I perform ablution (wudu) and purify myself” (pp. 55–58), “The childhood of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.)” (pp. 71–76), “I share my joy” (pp. 43–47). Please do not forget the book, notebook and pen; the lesson starts at 11:00.

Revision at home (14–18 September):
• Elifbâ: revise the letters of the Shîn and Ayn groups briefly every day; your child should be able to say a letter’s name when they see it.
• Camiye Gidiyorum 1: read “Our holy book is the Qur’an” (pp. 31–36) and “I perform ablution (wudu) and purify myself” (pp. 55–58) together; practise the steps of ablution together at home.
• Briefly recall the sections “The childhood of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.)” (pp. 71–76) and “I share my joy” (pp. 43–47).
Preparing for the weekend lessons (19–20 September): the letters of the Lâm group (Lâm, Mîm, Nûn, Vâv, He, Ye) — with these six letters all 28 letters are complete — and, on Sunday, a revision of all the letters; “Allah is our Creator” (pp. 49–54), “I perform ablution (wudu) and purify myself” (pp. 55–58), “The youth of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.)” (pp. 107–112), “I love my family” (pp. 59–63). Please do not forget the book, notebook and pen; the lesson starts at 11.00.

Revision at home (21–25 September):
• Elifbâ: this week all 28 letters were completed. Revise the letters in mixed order for 5–10 minutes every day; your child should be able to say a letter’s name when they see it.
• Camiye Gidiyorum 1: read “Allah is our Creator” (pp. 49–54) and “I perform ablution (wudu) and purify myself” (pp. 55–58) together; practise the steps of ablution at home.
• Briefly recall “The youth of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.)” (pp. 107–112) and “I love my family” (pp. 59–63).
Preparing for the weekend lessons (26–27 September): on Saturday we will study how letters are written at the beginning of a word, and on Sunday in the middle of a word; we are now moving from recognising the letters to writing them. You may also take a quick look at “Our tree of faith” (pp. 85–90), “Learning and reading the Qur’an is an act of worship” (pp. 65–70), “Muhammad (s.a.s.) becomes a prophet” (pp. 181–186) and “We celebrate together” (pp. 77–83). plan.Öğrenci, Elif grubu harflerini şekil ve: The student distinguishes the letters of the Elif group by shape and by sound.
plan.Elif, Bâ, Tâ, Se, Cîm ve Hâ harfleri kar: The letters Elif, Bâ, Tâ, Se, Cîm and Hâ are introduced with cards. The teacher shows the points of articulation (mahreç), and the students pronounce the letters by repeating them, first in chorus and then one by one.
plan.Öğrenci, İslam dininin Allah tarafından: The student explains that the religion of Islam was sent by Allah through the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) and that a person who follows this religion is called a ‘Muslim’. • The student lists the three basic dimensions of Islam (belief, worship and good character) and gives an example from daily life for each. • The student recites from memory and writes the meaning of the Declaration of Oneness (kalimat at-tawhid) in Turkish and its French version. • The student correctly matches the names Muslim, Christian and Jew with the corresponding religion (Islam, Christianity, Judaism). • The student expresses in their own sentences how important it is to relate to people of other religions in a spirit of mutual help and respect. • The student puts into practice saying the Basmala before a meal and Alhamdulillah after it as a concrete way of thanking Allah.
plan.Birinci ünite, \"Benim dinim İslam'dır\": Under the title “My religion is Islam”, the first unit aims to give children aged 7 and over a sense of the basic identity and outlook of Islam. First, they learn that Islam is a religion sent through the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) and that a person who follows it is called a “Muslim”. It is stressed that belief, worship and good character together make up the three basic dimensions of Islam. Through concrete examples and fill-in-the-blank activities, the children grasp that believing in Allah makes a person honest, trustworthy and kind in speech. The unit then opens a comparative perspective by comparing Christianity, Judaism and Islam with regard to their places of worship. The importance of living with people of other religions in respect is emphasised.
plan.Mutlu bir anımı defterime çiziyorum. / G: I draw a happy memory in my notebook. / I draw good behaviours in my notebook. / I think about how to thank my Lord.
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'ın beş şartını (kelime-i: The student lists the five pillars of Islam (the Shahadah, prayer, fasting, almsgiving and pilgrimage) in the correct order. • The student recites from memory and writes the Shahadah (kalimat ash-shahadah) and the Declaration of Oneness (kalimat at-tawhid) together with their Turkish meanings. • The student memorises the Basmala and explains in their own sentences what it means to begin every task with the Basmala. • The student describes how many times a day the prayer is performed and its basic elements such as ablution and the qibla, and explains that prayer is described as ‘the pillar of religion’. • The student distinguishes the basic meaning of fasting, almsgiving and pilgrimage and what each contributes to a Muslim’s life, giving examples. • The student reads or sings aloud in class the hadith on the five pillars of Islam and the Basmala song.
plan.Bu ünite, \"İslam'ın Şartları\" başlığı: Under the title “The pillars of Islam”, this unit introduces children over the age of seven to the five basic pillars of Islam step by step and with concrete examples. First the Shahadah, which is the essence and summary of Islam, is taken up; it is taught that bearing witness to the oneness of Allah, and that the Prophet Muhammad is His servant and messenger, is the foundation of Muslim identity. The relationship between the Declaration of Oneness and the Shahadah is then drawn out, and it is stressed that these words place both meaning and responsibility on the one who says them and create a bond of brotherhood among Muslims. To connect with daily life, the meaning of the Basmala and the importance of beginning every task with it are dwelt upon.
plan.Kelime-i Şehadet'i Türkçe ya da Fransızc: Reciting the Shahadah from memory to a friend, in Turkish or in French. / Writing the Shahadah from memory in the notebook, in its Turkish, French and Arabic readings. / Finding the letters in the flower picture that contains the texts of the Declaration of Oneness and the Shahadah and writing them in the answer box.
plan.Öğrenci, Hı grubu harflerini doğru mahre: The student reads the letters of the Khâ group with the correct point of articulation (mahreç).
plan.Hı, Dâl, Zel, Râ, Ze ve Sîn harfleri ağı: The letters Hı, Dâl, Zel, Râ, Ze and Sîn are practised while the movement of the mouth is demonstrated. A quick recognition game is played with letter cards, and similar sounds are compared with short examples.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) doğduğ: The student explains Mecca, the city where the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) was born, and the main features of the Jahiliyya period (idol worship, slavery, injustice). • The student lists in chronological order the important events of the Prophet’s childhood (the death of his father, his wet nurse, the deaths of his mother and grandfather, his uncle’s protection). • The student states why the Prophet Muhammad was given the nickname ‘Muhammad al-Amin’ (the Trustworthy). • The student lists at least five examples of the Prophet Muhammad’s exemplary behaviour, such as honesty, helpfulness, patience and love of animals. • The student gets to know the Prophet Muhammad’s family life (his marriage to Khadija, his children) and gives concrete examples of the Prophet’s love for children. • The student compares the Prophet Muhammad’s exemplary behaviour with their own daily life and makes a self-assessment.
plan.Bu ünite, çocukları Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a: This unit centres on introducing children to the life of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.). First, the social and religious situation of pre-Islamic Arabia, especially Mecca, is outlined through the idol worship and social injustice of the Jahiliyya period, so that the child understands the setting into which the Prophet was born. Then, in chronological order, we learn that the Prophet Muhammad lost his father before he was born and his mother and grandfather at a very young age, that he grew up in the desert with his wet nurse Halima, and that he finally came under the protection of his uncle Abu Talib. In the rest of the unit the Prophet’s moral character comes to the fore: the honesty and trustworthiness that earned him the nickname ‘Muhammad al-Amin’ from his community are described.
plan.Mekke'nin nerede olduğunu ve Cahiliye dö: Talking and discussing with a classmate where Mecca is and why the Jahiliyya period is regarded as a bad time. / Discussing with a classmate why it is sad that the Kaaba was full of idols. / Listing the names that appear in the reading text (Abdullah, Amina, Halima, Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib, etc.) in the correct order.
plan.Öğrenci, günlük hayatta kullanılan farkl: The student recognises different forms of greeting used in daily life (Turkish, French) and explains them in their own words. • The student says the meaning of the Islamic greeting “As-salamu alaykum” (a wish for peace, safety and health) and explains with examples that the greeting increases love between people. • The student states, on the basis of verse 86 of Surah an-Nisa, the duty to answer a greeting with a better one or at least with the same. • The student recites the Tahiyyat prayer in Arabic together with the class and tells at which point of worship it is recited (at every sitting of the prayer: the first and the last sitting). • The student explains the place of hospitality in Islam, drawing on the story, and states that treating guests kindly is a religious value. • The student describes the Prophet Muhammad’s efforts towards people with what they learnt from the hymn and states the importance of feeling respect and love for the Prophet.
plan.Bu ünitede çocuklara güzel söz ve davran: In this unit children are taught the religious and human value of kind words and behaviour, especially of greeting one another. The unit begins by introducing different forms of greeting used in daily life; then the meaning and importance of Islam’s basic greeting, “as-salamu alaykum / wa alaykumu s-salam”, is explored in depth. By stressing that the greeting is not just a word but means wishing the other person health, safety and peace, the unit helps children discover how greeting strengthens love and bonds between people. Through the story titled “The Unwelcome Guest”, hospitality and treating guests kindly are taught as a religious value.
plan.Farklı selamlama sözcükleri arasından en: Let us choose the greeting we like best from among the different greeting words and circle it. / Let us write our favourite greeting in our notebook and explain to our friends why we chose it. / Let us talk with a classmate about the forms of greeting used in our families and act them out in front of the class.
plan.Öğrenci, Şîn grubu harflerini kalın ve i: The student recognises the letters of the Shîn group, paying attention to the difference between heavy and light sounds.
plan.Sâd, Dâd, Tı ve Zı kalın (isti'lâ) harfl: Sâd, Dâd, Tı and Zı are introduced as heavy (isti‘lâ) letters and Shîn as a light letter; it is also shown that Zı is pronounced with the tongue between the teeth. The students read the letters in order, in mixed order and from the card the teacher points to.
plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in Allah tarafın: The student explains that the Holy Qur’an is a sacred book sent by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad through revelation. • The student reads verse 2 of Surah al-Baqara and its meaning, and expresses in their own sentences the Qur’an’s quality of ‘guidance’. • The student lists in at least three points the rules of respect that must be shown to the Qur’an (keeping it in a state of ablution, not putting it on the floor, not tearing its pages, etc.). • Starting from the ‘prescription’ metaphor, the student explains in their own words that it is important not just to read the Qur’an but to put it into practice. • The student tells the Qur’an apart from other books with examples.
plan.Dördüncü ünite, çocukları Kur'an-ı Kerim: The fourth unit begins by introducing children to what the Holy Qur’an is and why it is a special book. That the Qur’an was sent by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad through revelation, that it shows people the right way and that it contains no doubt is reinforced with the second verse of Surah al-Baqara. The unit then moves to a fictional story seen through a child’s eyes in order to make the abstract concept concrete: the bookshelf at home, the father’s habit of reading the Qur’an and the discovery of how the Qur’an differs from other books are brought together with the child’s own experience. In the next stage the unit moves from cognitive to behavioural learning and teaches the rules of respect to be shown to the Qur’an.
plan.Kutsal kitabın diğer kitaplardan farkını: Discussing and assessing as a class how the holy book differs from other books. / Finding out about the pupils in class who read the Qur’an and introducing them to their friends. / Doing a personal piece of research about how much one loves the Holy Qur’an. / Hymn: ‘A Sun Rose in 571’ (optional)
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'da temizliğin bedensel, k: The student lists the three dimensions of cleanliness in Islam: cleanliness of the body, of clothing and of the heart.
plan.Öğrenci, Mâide Suresi 6. ayetinin abdest: The student explains that verse 6 of Surah al-Ma’ida contains the command to perform ablution.
plan.Öğrenci, 'Temizlik imandandır.' hadisini: The student memorises the hadith ‘Cleanliness is part of faith.’ and expresses its meaning in their own sentences.
plan.Sekizinci ünite, \"Abdest alıyorum, temi: Under the title “I perform ablution, I purify myself”, the eighth unit presents the understanding of cleanliness in Islam to the child from a holistic point of view. The unit opens with verse 6 of Surah al-Ma’ida and shows, in the language of the Qur’an, that performing ablution before the prayer is a religious obligation. It then stresses that cleanliness is not only a bodily act but also covers clothing, daily habits and the inner world (cleanliness of the heart). Within the principle “Islam is the religion of cleanliness”, the child is made aware that negative feelings such as pride and selfishness are also a kind of spiritual impurity. The topic is reinforced by memorising the hadith of our Prophet, “Cleanliness is half of faith.” (Muslim, Tahara 1).
plan.Hangi ibadetlerden önce temizlenilmesi g: Discussing with a classmate before which acts of worship one must be clean, and giving examples. / Finding five examples of how the heart can become dirty and discussing them with a classmate. / Discussing what needs to be paid attention to in the behaviours shown in the pictures.
plan.Öğrenci, Ayn grubu harflerini duyduğunda: The student correctly matches the letters of the Ayn group when hearing and seeing them.
plan.Ayn ile Ğayn'ın boğaz, Fe'nin dudak-diş,: The points of articulation are practised: the throat for Ayn and Ghayn, the lip and teeth for Fe, and the back of the tongue for Kâf and Kef. The large form of each letter is shown on the board, and the students raise the matching card when they hear the letter.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) hayatı: The student lists in chronological order the main events in the life of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) (birth, wet nurse, the deaths of his mother and grandfather, the protection of Abu Talib, the journey to Damascus). • The student explains the role of his uncle Abu Talib in the Prophet Muhammad’s life and the love and protection he showed his nephew. • The student tells the story of Bahira in their own sentences and defines the idea of the ‘awaited prophet’ in a way suited to their age. • The student explains new concepts such as caravan, guide, Torah and Gospel by using them in context. • The student compares similarities and differences between the Prophet’s childhood and their own childhood experiences. • The student performs the hymn ‘I Learned a Lesson from the Masnavi’ together with the class and expresses in their own words the spiritual submission the hymn conveys.
plan.Bu ünite, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) doğum: This unit introduces children, in chronological order, to the Prophet Muhammad’s (s.a.s.) life journey from his birth to his youth. The students first follow on a timeline the events from his birth in the year 571 to his early childhood with his wet nurse Halima, the death of his mother and the care of his grandfather; then they learn about his move to his uncle Abu Talib’s home in 578 and the first trading journey to Damascus in 583. The fact that our Prophet, although he grew up an orphan, was loved and protected like their own child by his uncle Abu Talib and his wife Fatima is treated in the context of the importance of love and family ties.
plan.Zaman çizelgesi etkinliği: Kendi hayatım: Timeline activity: Let us add the important events in our own lives (birth, starting primary school, going to the mosque) to the timeline by writing them next to the dates given. / Family sharing: Share in class the games you play with your brothers and sisters and the moments when you are happiest with your family. / Comparison discussion: Let us compare our Prophet’s childhood with our own; are there similarities?
plan.Öğrenci, kendi yaşamındaki kişisel ve di: The student lists by name the personal and religious special days in their own life (birthday, Eids, blessed nights, etc.). • The student explains with examples the practices carried out on Islamic special days such as Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, the Night of Destiny and Mosques Day (sharing the sacrificial meat, fasting, handing out sweets, etc.). • The student states the importance, from an Islamic point of view, of sharing joy and special days with others. • The student correctly uses the basic concepts about Islam, the Prophet Muhammad, the Shahadah, the Basmala and the Qur’an in matching and fill-in-the-blank activities. • The student recalls basic biographical information such as the family of the Prophet Muhammad (his mother Amina, his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, his wet nurse Halima) and his birthplace. • The student understands that Islam is a universal religion belonging to all people and not specific to one nation, and tells true and false statements apart.
plan.6. ünite, \"Sevincimi paylaşıyorum\" baş: Under the title “I share my joy”, unit 6 aims to teach children the beauty of sharing joys and special days with others. First, the children are helped to notice which days are important in their own lives: besides personal celebrations such as birthdays and starting school, religious special days such as Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, the Mawlid night, the Mi‘raj night, the Night of Destiny and Mosques Day are treated in this framework. The children learn what is done on these days through concrete examples: cutting a cake, handing out sacrificial meat, fasting, introducing Islam to guests and sharing sweets.
plan.En sevdiğimiz özel günde neler yaptığımı: Telling our friends orally what we do on our favourite special day. / Choosing three of the important days of the year and writing down the features of each in the notebook. / Writing in the notebook with whom and how we spend the important days mentioned during the year.
plan.Öğrenci, Lâm grubu harflerini mahreçleri: The student pronounces the letters of the Lâm group, paying attention to their points of articulation.
plan.Lâm, Mîm, Nûn, Vâv, He ve Ye harfleri du: Lâm, Mîm, Nûn, Vâv, He and Ye are introduced with the movements of the lips, the tongue and the throat. The students repeat the letters through a row chain, a card game and listening in pairs.
plan.Öğrenci, Allah'ın kâinattaki canlıları v: The student explains that Allah created the living things and beings in the universe out of nothing. • The student tells the difference between ‘creating’ and ‘manufacturing’ with at least three examples. • The student memorises Surah al-Ikhlas in Arabic and expresses its meaning in their own sentences. • The student names Allah’s names as-Sami‘, al-Basir, al-‘Alim, ar-Rahim and al-Wadud and explains the meaning of each. • The student defines the concept of tawhid as ‘Allah is One and unique’.
plan.Yedinci ünite, \"Yaratıcımız Allah'tır\": Under the title “Allah is our Creator”, the seventh unit introduces children to Allah’s existence, oneness and attributes through concrete observations and stories. The unit opens with a zoo trip by two children called Elif and Alperen; through the variety of insects, birds and other living creatures, attention is drawn to the universe created by Allah, and this thought is reinforced with verse 29 of Surah al-Baqara. Then it is taught that ‘creating’ belongs to Allah alone: the basic difference between bringing something into being from nothing and making things out of existing materials (manufacturing) is explained with examples. At the centre of the unit are Surah al-Ikhlas and Allah’s names as-Sami‘, al-Basir, al-‘Alim, ar-Rahim and al-Wadud.
plan.İhlas Suresi'ni kendi sözcükleriyle açık: An activity of explaining Surah al-Ikhlas in one’s own words is carried out. / The things Allah has created and the things people have manufactured are written in the notebook as a comparison table with five examples and talked over with a friend. / Whom we trust most and why is shared with a friend. / Singing a hymn that expresses love of the Prophet (optional)
plan.Öğrenci, kibir ve bencillik gibi olumsuz: The student explains with examples that negative feelings such as pride and selfishness can make the heart unclean.
plan.Öğrenci, abdestin adımlarını doğru sıray: The student performs the steps of ablution in the correct order.
plan.Öğrenci, namazdan önce neden temizlenilm: The student explains, with its religious basis, why one must be clean before the prayer.
plan.Sekizinci ünite, \"Abdest alıyorum, temi: Under the title “I perform ablution, I purify myself”, the eighth unit presents the understanding of cleanliness in Islam to the child from a holistic point of view. The unit opens with verse 6 of Surah al-Ma’ida and shows, in the language of the Qur’an, that performing ablution before the prayer is a religious obligation. It then stresses that cleanliness is not only a bodily act but also covers clothing, daily habits and the inner world (cleanliness of the heart). Within the principle “Islam is the religion of cleanliness”, the child is made aware that negative feelings such as pride and selfishness are also a kind of spiritual impurity. In this lesson the steps of ablution are practised; the idea that feelings such as pride and selfishness can make the heart unclean is treated with examples.
plan.Beden temizliğine dair beş örnek bulma v: Finding five examples of bodily cleanliness and sharing them with a classmate. / Assessing as a class what is understood from the hadith ‘Cleanliness is half of faith.’ (Muslim, Tahara 1). / Thinking about how acts of worship would be performed without water and sharing our thoughts.
plan.Öğrenci, öğrendiği harfleri karışık sıra: The student recognises, without a mistake, the letters learnt, in mixed order.
plan.Öğrenilen bütün harfler karışık kartlarl: All the letters learnt are revised with mixed cards. Each student is given a short turn at recognition, and the letters they find difficult are worked on again together with the class.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed'in gençlik dönemin: The student explains, with at least three concrete events, the basic virtues the Prophet Muhammad showed in his youth, such as honesty, trustworthiness and a talent for reconciling people. • The student defines in their own sentences the purpose for which the Hilf al-Fudul (the Alliance of the Virtuous) was founded and the Prophet Muhammad’s role in it. • The student puts the chronological stages of the marriage of the Prophet Muhammad and Khadija in the correct order. • The student tells about the peaceful solution the Prophet Muhammad proposed in the episode of replacing the Black Stone and explains the importance of this solution for reconciliation. • The student expresses the importance of working and having a profession, giving an example from the Prophet Muhammad’s trading life. • The student lists the names of the five daily prayers by singing the hymn ‘While Worshipping’ with the class.
plan.Bu ünite, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) gençl: This unit introduces children to the youth of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) around four main events. First an injustice that took place in Mecca is treated: when a merchant from Yemen (from the Zubayd tribe) was wronged by al-‘As ibn Wa’il, the young Muhammad and his virtuous friends took action, which shows how the idea of the Hilf al-Fudul (the Alliance of the Virtuous) was born. Then it is treated how the Prophet Muhammad joined trading caravans, met different people and gained experience, and how with his honest and trustworthy character he became a model in business life. In the third stage, the steps of his marriage to Khadija are discussed. The fourth event is the peaceful solution in the replacing of the Black Stone.
plan.'Erdemli' kelimesinin anlamı, anlatılan: The meaning of the word ‘virtuous’ is explained from the story of injustice that is told; how virtuous behaviour can be reflected in the classroom is discussed. / Each pupil writes their own dream profession on a sticky note (post-it); the class does the activity ‘Let Us Make Our Profession Map’. / An activity of putting in the correct order the four stages of the marriage of the Prophet Muhammad and Khadija (the trading journey, the conveying of her admiration, asking permission from the elders of the family, fixing the ages).
plan.Öğrenci, çekirdek aile ve geniş aile kav: The student defines the concepts of nuclear family and extended family and illustrates the difference between the two with their own family. • The student builds a family diagram by correctly using basic kinship terms such as paternal aunt, uncle and grandfather. • The student explains that getting along well with brothers, sisters and relatives is a command of Islam. • The student lists the hadith ‘Always treat people well’ and the hadith about kindness to parents. • The student comes up with peaceful ways of solving disagreements between brothers and sisters. • The student expresses their sense of responsibility and gratitude towards their parents with concrete everyday examples.
plan.Dokuzuncu ünite \"Ailemi Seviyorum\" baş: Under the title “I Love My Family”, the ninth unit introduces the child to the concept of the family, relationships within the family and family ties from an Islamic point of view. With the opening text told through the eyes of a child named Elif, the nuclear family made up of mother, father and brothers and sisters is made concrete, and the contribution of everyday moments together, such as breakfast in the morning, to family happiness is stressed. Then, through the extended family of a child named Enes, who lives both in Germany and in Turkey, the concept of kinship and its terms (paternal aunt, uncle, grandfather, etc.) are treated in a comic-strip format. The religious-education side of the unit is formed by two hadiths: ‘Always treat people well’ and the hadiths about kindness to parents.
plan.Sıra arkadaşına kendi ailesini tanıtma (: Introducing one’s own family (mother, father, brothers and sisters, close relatives) to a classmate. / Drawing Elif’s family tree in the notebook. / Drawing one’s own family tree in the notebook.
plan.Öğrenci, harflerin kelime başındaki şeki: The student recognises the shapes of the letters at the beginning of a word.
plan.Harflerin kelime başındaki şekilleri tah: The shapes of the letters at the beginning of a word are shown on the board with coloured examples. The students match the isolated and initial forms of the same letter, and then read short syllable examples.
plan.Öğrenci, imanın ne anlama geldiğini günl: The student explains what faith means with examples from daily life. • The student lists in order, and memorises, the basic articles of faith of Islam (the six articles). • Using the metaphor of the tree of faith, the student defines the branch that stands for each article of faith and explains its meaning. • The student expresses, with examples, how the articles of faith in Allah, the angels and the books are related to daily worship and learning. • The student explains in their own sentences how faith in the prophets, the hereafter and destiny contributes to a person’s responsible behaviour. • The student sings the hymn ‘My Body Burns Without Stopping, O Allah’ together with classmates.
plan.13. ünite olan \"İman Ağacımız\", çocukl: Unit 13, “Our Tree of Faith”, aims to let children discover the basic beliefs of Islam. The unit opens with a line of questioning that, through concrete examples from daily life (such as putting on a seat belt, listening in the mosque, helping a friend), lets children sense what faith means. Then the six articles of faith — faith in Allah, the angels, the books, the prophets, the hereafter and destiny — are pictured through the metaphor of a tree: each branch of a strong tree with deep roots stands for one article. The first three articles (faith in Allah, the angels and the books) are made concrete in the context of worship and prayer practice, the duties of the angels and learning the Qur’an. Faith in the prophets, the hereafter and destiny is linked to responsible behaviour.
plan.Günlük yaşam cümlelerini 'iman' kelimesi: An activity of matching sentences from daily life with the meaning of the word ‘faith’ is done. / Reciting the six articles of faith from memory with a classmate. / Writing the articles of faith in the notebook from memory.
plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in insanlara reh: The student explains that the Holy Qur’an was sent to guide people, and that reading it, learning it and living by it are counted as worship. • The student recites the hadith which says that those who learn the Qur’an and teach it are the best of people, and expresses its meaning in their own sentences. • The student lists the three basic areas the Qur’an guides us in (belief, worship, supplication/good character) and gives at least one example for each. • The student recognises the concepts of khatm (completing the whole Qur’an), mukabele (reading the Qur’an in turns) and reading with the meaning, and tells them apart. • The student lists the moral values the Qur’an teaches (respect for the neighbour, honour for parents, helping the poor, loving people). • The student explains the importance of reading the Qur’an both in its original Arabic and through its translated meaning.
plan.Onuncu ünite, \"Kur'an öğrenmek ve okuma: Under the title “Learning and reading the Qur’an is an act of worship”, the tenth unit aims to make children love the Holy Qur’an as a divine book that guides humanity, and to take it to heart. First, through the question of why the Qur’an was sent, children are helped to grasp that reading it, learning it, understanding it and putting it into practice are each an act of worship. Through the hadiths of our Prophet (s.a.s.) it is explained that those who learn the Qur’an and teach it are the best of people, and that a believer who reads the Qur’an is likened to a fruit with a pleasant scent. Then the three basic areas of guidance the Qur’an offers people are listed: belief, worship, and supplication/good character.
plan.Dört resimdeki numaralar uygun yerlere y: The numbers in the four pictures are placed in the right spots to complete the sentences ‘Our Lord has sent us the Holy Qur’an so that we read / understand / learn / live it.’ / What comes to our minds and what we feel while reading the hadiths is shared with the class. / What the Holy Qur’an teaches us (belief, worship, good character, love) is summarised with a classmate; examples are given and shared with the class.
plan.Öğrenci, harflerin kelime ortasındaki şe: The student correctly tells apart the shapes of the letters in the middle of a word.
plan.Harflerin kelime ortasında iki taraftan: How letters join on both sides in the middle of a word is shown with example words. The students choose the right letter shape for the gaps on the board and read short words by spelling them out.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) peygam: The student lists, with at least three examples, the main social problems that existed in Meccan society before the prophethood of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.). • The student explains in their own sentences why the Prophet Muhammad withdrew to the Cave of Hira. • The student tells that the first revelation came through Jibril (as) with the command ‘Read!’. • The student briefly defines the concepts ‘revelation’, ‘Lord’ and ‘Jibril’. • The student reads the meaning of the first five verses of Surah al-‘Alaq and states the importance of these verses. • The student sings the hymn ‘Take Our Greetings’ in class and recognises the holy places mentioned in the hymn.
plan.Bu ünite, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) peyga: This unit teaches the child, step by step, how the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) received the task of prophethood, that is, the starting point of Islam. First, the problems of the Meccan society in which our Prophet grew up are treated; bitter realities such as poverty, orphanhood, injustice towards women and children, and slavery are laid out with concrete examples. Then the young Prophet Muhammad, deeply troubled by this corrupt social order, is described withdrawing into solitude and reflecting for long periods in the Cave of Hira. At the centre of the unit is the moment the first revelation came: the first five verses of Surah al-‘Alaq, brought by Jibril with the command ‘Read!’, are studied.
plan.Konuşma balonlarını okuyarak sınıfça tar: Read the speech bubbles and discuss as a class: In what kind of society did our Prophet grow up? What would someone who saw these problems feel, and what would they do? / Imagine together as a class, and talk about, what might have gone through the mind of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) as he went up to the Cave of Hira. / Put in the correct order the jumbled sentences about how the revelation came.
plan.Öğrenci, Ramazan Bayramı'nın İslam'daki: The student explains the meaning of Eid al-Fitr in Islam and the hadith ‘Eid is a day of joy’. • Starting from the Prophet’s treatment of an orphan child, the student expresses, with examples, the importance of sharing and compassion at Eid. • The student links the values of sharing, trust, solidarity and love to concrete situations from daily life and describes what would result if these values were missing. • The student reinforces basic knowledge about the oneness of Allah, the Qur’an, ablution and the Prophet’s family by telling true from false. • By singing the hymn ‘Bismillah’ together in class, the student grasps the importance of the Basmala in Islamic life.
plan.12. Ünite \"Birlikte Kutluyoruz\" başlığ: Unit 12, titled “We Celebrate Together”, begins by conveying to the child, through a concrete story, the meaning of the joy of Eid in Islam and the value of sharing. The account of the Prophet embracing an orphan child on the day of Eid and making him happy shows how love, compassion and solidarity are lived in practice. Then the concepts of sharing, trust, solidarity and love are brought into daily life with the question “What would happen if it were missing?”; values education is deepened with concrete scenarios such as helping those in need, prayer, rejoicing together and giving gifts. The unit also contains the closing assessment of Part 2: earlier topics are reinforced with sentence-matching and true/false questions.
plan.Hikâyeye uygun bir başlık bul. / Paylaşm: Find a suitable title for the story. / Sharing: Think about and write what would happen if people in need were forgotten at Eid. / Trust: Think about what it would mean if we did not pray for one another when starting school.
plan.Öğrenci, harflerin kelime sonundaki şeki: The student recognises the shapes of the letters at the end of a word within reading.
plan.Harflerin kelime sonundaki bağlı ve yalı: The joined and isolated appearances of letters at the end of a word are compared. The students mark the final letter in example words and have the teacher check it by reading one-to-one.
plan.Öğrenci, imanın birinci şartının Allah'a: The student states that the first article of faith is faith in Allah. • The student explains that a person who believes in Allah and the hereafter lives a more meaningful life in this world. • The student memorises the Amantu prayer in Arabic and says the meaning of the word ‘amantu’. • The student knows that the Amantu sums up the articles of faith and lists these articles. • The student tells apart the basic similarities and differences between the ways Islam, Judaism and Christianity believe in the Creator. • The student says the meaning of the expression ‘Ar-rizqu ‘alallah’ and explains with an example the belief that provision comes from Allah.
plan.19. ünite, imanın birinci şartı olan All: Unit 19 focuses on faith in Allah, the first article of faith, and first brings the topic close to the child through a story. The fact that the Prophet’s uncle Abu Talib did not believe is presented as a sad example, while through a dialogue between Ali and one of his neighbours the message is given that a person who believes in Allah and the hereafter lives a more meaningful and happier life in this world. It is explained that the believer, by doing good, will find peace in the hereafter, and will strengthen their Muslim identity by reciting the Shahadah and reading the Qur’an. Then the Amantu prayer, which gathers all the articles of faith in a concise form, is memorised in Arabic and the meaning of the word ‘amantu’ is explained.
plan.Hz. Ali ile komşusu arasındaki hikâye dr: The story of Ali and his neighbour is acted out using drama. / The students write the question ‘Why do I believe in Allah?’ in their notebooks. / An activity of putting the articles of faith in order is done.
plan.Öğrenci, beş vakit namazın isimlerini ve: The student lists the names and daily times of the five daily prayers. • The student explains what the qibla means and where the Kaaba is located. • The student correctly says the number of rak‘as of the five daily prayers (distinguishing sunnah and fard). • The student memorises, and expresses in their own sentences, the six conditions that must be fulfilled before beginning the prayer (purity from ritual impurity, purity from filth, covering the awra, facing the qibla, the time, the intention). • The student recognises in the correct order the basic pillars within the prayer (the opening takbir, standing, recitation, bowing, prostration, the final sitting). • The student gives examples of the rules to be observed in the prayer (performing ablution, keeping quiet, etc.).
plan.Bu ünite, 7 yaş ve üzeri çocuklara namaz: This unit introduces the prayer to children aged 7 and over in a comprehensive and gradual way. First the names and times of the five daily prayers are taught through a concrete example (the Diyanet prayer-times chart on our mosque’s website), aiming to link them with the child’s daily life. Then, with the help of a geographical map, it is explained that the direction faced in prayer is the qibla, and that the qibla is the Kaaba, whose foundations were raised by Abraham and Ishmael about 4,000 years ago. Through the eyes of a child named Alperen, it is stressed that Muslims all over the world pray facing the same qibla, so that a sense of belonging to the ummah is felt.
plan.Camimizin web sitesindeki Marche-en-Fame: Looking at the Marche-en-Famenne Diyanet prayer-times chart on our mosque’s website, finding the prayer times for one’s own birthday and writing them in the notebook. / Finding a title for Alperen’s story and cooperating with the class by marking on a world map the places where prayer is performed. / Finding the direction of the qibla in the classroom.
plan.Öğrenci, bitişen harfleri kelime içinde: The student correctly follows the joining letters within a word.
plan.Sağından ve solundan bağlanabilen harfle: Letters that can join on their right and on their left are practised with example words. The students connect the letters with a line, and then read aloud the syllables and words that result.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed'in ilk vahyi alışı: The student explains in their own sentences the role of support and trust that Khadija played when the Prophet Muhammad received the first revelation. • The student lists names such as Ali and Umar among the first Muslims and recognises the main feature of each one’s story of coming to Islam. • The student expresses with examples the difficulties the Prophet Muhammad met in the process of conveying Islam (the pressure of Abu Lahab, the first reaction of society). • The student states that the Hijra took place in the year 622 and that the Prophet was welcomed in Medina with a hymn. • The student explains which historical event the hymn ‘Tala‘a al-Badru‘ is linked to and recognises the hymn. • The student relates the courage and determination the first Muslims showed in protecting their beliefs to their own life with suitable examples.
plan.Bu ünite, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) peyga: This unit introduces the child, through stories and dialogues, to the Prophet Muhammad’s (s.a.s.) mission of prophethood and the process of conveying Islam. First, bringing out Khadija’s role as a ‘confidante’, it describes those troubled moments when our Prophet received the first revelation, the deep trust his wife showed him, and Khadija’s taking him to Waraqa ibn Nawfal, her cousin. Then, after the mission of prophethood had been announced, it is explained how hard a process it was to invite people to Islam, how Ali, while still a small child, was one of the first young people to accept Islam, and how the house of al-Arqam became the first meeting place of the Muslims.
plan.Metinde verilen paragrafı okuyarak ilk M: An activity of reading the paragraph given in the text and identifying and listing the qualities of the first Muslims (strength, determination, patience). / An activity of finding a suitable title for the story that tells how Umar came to Islam.
plan.Öğrenci, hata yapmanın insan doğasının b: The student explains that making mistakes is part of human nature. • The student expresses the importance of apologising in Islam, basing it on the teachings of the Qur’an and the Prophet. • The student defines in their own sentences the harm that arrogant behaviour does to social relations. • The student recalls the meaning of verse 37 of Surah al-Isra and links the prohibition of arrogance to this verse. • The student gives an example of a concrete situation in their own daily life that calls for an apology and explains how they would behave in it.
plan.On beşinci ünite, \"Dinim, hatamı düzelt: Under the title “My religion asks me to put my mistakes right”, the fifteenth unit conveys to children the teachings of Islam on admitting mistakes and apologising. The unit opens with an illustration showing a dialogue between a girl wearing a headscarf and a child in a wheelchair; in this way everyday communication between different people and the feeling of empathy are made visible. Children are taught that every person can make mistakes from time to time and that this is a natural fact. It is stressed that what really matters is noticing the mistake, feeling regret and apologising. That Islam does not approve of arrogance and pride is explained by linking it to verse 37 of Surah al-Isra.
plan.Özür dilemeyi gerektiren bir davranışı b: An activity of writing on a piece of paper a behaviour that calls for an apology and sharing it with the class. / A scenario: while lining up at break time you knock a friend’s bag to the ground; assessing and discussing the situation of going to pick up the spilled things and apologising.
plan.Öğrenci, bitişmeyen harfleri kelime için: The student correctly identifies the non-joining letters within a word.
plan.Sağından bağlandığı hâlde solundan bağla: Letters that join on their right but do not join on their left are introduced with simple examples. The students colour the non-joining letters and explain why a break occurs in the word.
plan.Öğrenci, dört büyük ilahî kitabın (Kur'a: The student lists the names of the four great divine books (the Holy Qur’an, the Gospel, the Torah, the Psalms) and the prophet to whom each was revealed. • The student explains to which nation and in which city or place each holy book was sent down. • The student recognises the French equivalents of the four holy books (le Coran, l’Évangile, la Torah, les Psaumes) and matches them correctly. • The student states that believing in the holy books is one of the articles of faith. • The student explains in their own sentences the wisdom of Allah’s sending more than one holy book. • The student explains the importance of a sense of responsibility and duty in religious education, giving examples from the stories of Esma and Enes.
plan.22. Ünite, \"Kutsal Kitapları Tanıyalım\: Under the title “Let Us Discover the Holy Books”, Unit 22 systematically introduces children to the four great divine books. The unit begins with an opening picture in which children from different nations study these books together, and first it is explained that the Holy Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) in Mecca and Medina and addresses all of humanity. Then it is taught that the Gospel was revealed to Jesus in Jerusalem, the Torah to Moses on Mount Sinai and the Psalms to David in Jerusalem, and that each of them was sent to the Children of Israel. The French equivalents (le Coran, l’Évangile, la Torah, les Psaumes) are given. The unit is completed by touching on responsibility and a sense of duty through the stories of Esma and Enes.
plan.Sıra arkadaşıyla kutsal kitaplarla ilgil: Asking and answering questions about the holy books with a classmate (for example: ‘To which prophet was the Psalms revealed?’). / Writing in the notebook the French names of the prophets mentioned in the book (e.g. Abraham, Moïse, Jésus, David). / Writing in the notebook the features of the four holy books in our own sentences.
plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in temel özellik: The student lists the main features of the Holy Qur’an (its language, number of pages, number of surahs and verses). • The student defines the concepts mushaf, surah, verse, juz’ and basmala and uses them in the right contexts. • The student points out and explains the elements on a real page of the Qur’an (the juz’ number, the beginning of a surah, the basmala, the pause marks, the juz’ rosette). • The student tells the difference between a translation of the meaning of the Qur’an and the Qur’an itself, and gives examples of translation differences between meanings. • The student explains that fasting is one of the pillars of Islam and how it is practised in the month of Ramadan. • The student gives concrete examples of the importance of behaving respectfully towards the Qur’an.
plan.16. Ünite, \"Kur'an'la Buluşuyoruz\" baş: Under the title “Meeting the Qur’an”, Unit 16 aims to introduce children to the Holy Qur’an and to help them feel love for it. First it is stressed that the Qur’an is the most sacred book, that its reading is begun by saying the Basmala and that it is also recited in the prayer; the child is expected to handle it with care and to ask Allah for help in understanding it. Then concrete information about the basic structure of the Qur’an is presented: it is taught that it is a book of about 600 pages, written in Arabic, called the mushaf, made up of 114 surahs and 6236 verses, that all the surahs except Surah at-Tawba begin with the basmala, and that the last twenty pages make up one single juz’.
plan.Karışık sıralanmış Kur'an ile ilgili cüm: Putting jumbled sentences about the Qur’an in order and writing them in the notebook. / Telling a classmate the new things learnt about the Holy Qur’an. / Asking a classmate questions about the topic learnt.
plan.Öğrenci, harf şekillerini kelimedeki kon: The student sorts the letter shapes according to their position in the word.
plan.Başta, ortada ve sonda yazılışlar karışı: The initial, medial and final forms are revised with a mixed worksheet. The students say the position of the letter, and the teacher makes a short individual reading check.
plan.Öğrenci, işlenen konulardaki temel kavra: The student recalls and gives examples of the basic concepts in the topics covered.
plan.Bu bölüme kadar işlenen konuların soru-c: Reinforcing the topics covered up to this section with questions and answers, a short written exercise and group work.
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'daki iki dinî bayramı (Ra: The student recognises by name the two religious festivals in Islam (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha) and explains which act of worship each is related to. • The student lists in at least five points the behaviours that should be carried out on the days of Eid (getting up early, performing ablution, the Eid prayer, visiting elders, helping one another, etc.). • The student tells apart the festivals of different religions (Easter, Christmas, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha) according to their religion and, giving examples, compares what they have in common and how they differ. • The student understands that congratulating friends of other faiths on their festivals is an expression of respect and tolerance, and applies this attitude in daily life. • The student sings the hymn ‘The Roads of the Kaaba’ in class and expresses in their own sentences the basic religious feelings and concepts in it (longing for the Kaaba, the transience of the world). • By answering the assessment questions of the unit (matching, fill-in-the-blank, multiple choice), the student shows their knowledge of the articles of faith, the prayer, the Qur’an and the Prophet Muhammad.
plan.18. ünite \"Bayramlaşıyoruz\" başlığını: Unit 18 is titled “We Exchange Our Eid Greetings” and introduces the child to the two religious festivals in Islam, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, both in their meaning and in their practical behaviour. The unit begins by treating what the festivals are and why they are important; then it gives the student, point by point, concrete Eid behaviours such as getting up early on the morning of Eid, performing ablution, going to the Eid prayer, kissing the hands of elders, offering hospitality to guests, phoning relatives far away, making up after quarrels and helping the poor. A striking aspect of the unit is the comparison of the festivals of different religions. Congratulating friends of other faiths is regarded as an expression of respect.
plan.Bildiğimiz bayramları sıra arkadaşımıza: Share the festivals we know orally with a classmate. / Share the religious festivals in writing with a classmate and discuss them. / Tell a classmate about the festivals of friends who are not Muslim.
plan.Öğrenci, lâmelifi kelime içinde tanır ve: The student recognises the lâm-elif within a word and reads it correctly.
plan.Lâmelifin Lâm ve Elif harflerinin birleş: It is shown that the lâm-elif is the combination of the letters Lâm and Elif. The students mark the examples that contain the lâm-elif on the board and practise short words by repeated reading.
plan.Öğrenci, iyilik yapan kişilere teşekkür: The student explains why it is important to thank people who do good and to say ‘Allah razı olsun’ (may Allah be pleased with you). • The student lists, with examples, at least three different everyday situations in which the expression ‘Allah razı olsun’ can be used. • The student expresses in their own sentences what supplication (dua) means and how close Allah is to people. • The student writes a short, sincere prayer for their family or a friend. • The student reads the hadith about the brotherhood of Muslims and explains with concrete examples what it corresponds to in their own life.
plan.20. ünite, \"Allah'a dua ediyorum ve şük: Under the title “I pray to Allah and I thank Him”, Unit 20 introduces children to the concepts of gratitude, thanks and supplication with concrete examples from everyday life. The unit opens with a child named Amina going to the supermarket with her mother; through this story children are helped to feel that thanking the people around us is a good behaviour. Then the meaning of the expression “Allah razı olsun” is explored in depth, and how to use it in many everyday situations such as gifts, meals, help and friendship is taught. When the definition and importance of supplication are treated, it is stressed that Allah is the closest of all beings to people. The unit is completed with the hadith about the brotherhood of Muslims.
plan.Bilinen duaları sınıf arkadaşlarıyla pay: Sharing the prayers we know with classmates. / Writing a prayer for the family and sharing it in class. / Writing a prayer for a favourite friend and sharing it with that friend.
plan.Öğrenci, hemzeyi farklı yazılışlarda tan: The student recognises the hamza in its different written forms and pronounces it.
plan.Hemzenin yazılış yerleri ve okuma sesi b: Where the hamza is written and how it sounds are introduced with simple examples. The students repeat syllables with hamza after the teacher and pick out the hamza from cards.
plan.Öğrenci, Allah'ın insanlara doğru yolu g: The student explains that Allah sent prophets and books to show people the right way. • The student says the concepts prophet, messenger, nabi and rasul, and that faith in the prophets is one of the six articles of faith. • The student knows how the abbreviations “Hz.”, “s.a.s.”, “a.s.” and “r.a.” are read and what they mean. • The student names the ulu al-‘azm (great) prophets — Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) — in order, each with one characteristic.
plan.Allah, insanları yarattığı için onları s: Because Allah created people, He loved them, chose prophets from among them to show the right way and sent them knowledge through Jibril; and so that it would not be forgotten, He also sent books. Prophets are also called messenger, nabi or rasul; faith in them is one of the six articles of faith. “Hz.” is an expression of respect, “s.a.s.” is used only for the Prophet Muhammad, “a.s.” for prophets and angels, and “r.a.” for prophets and the Companions. The great prophets called ulu al-‘azm are, in order, Noah; Abraham, to whom ten scrolls were given; Moses, on whom the Torah was sent down; Jesus, to whom the Gospel was given; and Muhammad (s.a.s.), the last prophet, to whom the Qur’an was given.
plan.Ekrana yansıtılan beş büyük peygamberin: Memorising the names of the five great prophets shown on the screen by repeating them in order all together.
plan.\"Hz., s.a.s., a.s., r.a.\" kısaltmaları: Showing the abbreviations “Hz., s.a.s., a.s., r.a.” on the board and matching them orally with their meanings.
plan.\"Neden Allah peygamber göndermiş?\" sor: Discussing as a class the question “Why did Allah send prophets?” and summarising the answers.
plan.Ülü'l-azm beş büyük peygamberin adları:: The names of the five great ulu al-‘azm prophets: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, Muhammad (s.a.s.).
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'da din kardeşliği ve yard: The student explains in their own sentences that brotherhood in faith and mutual help are a basic value in Islam. • The student expresses, with concrete examples, that respect and compassion should be shown to people who work hard and to those in need. • The student defines zakat as one of the five pillars of Islam and says that wealthy Muslims give a certain proportion of their property/money to the poor. • The student tells apart negative behaviours such as arrogance, stinginess and oppressing the orphan, basing this on verses of the Qur’an. • The student memorises the hadith ‘Whoever relieves a fellow believer of a hardship, Allah will relieve him of a hardship’ and explains its meaning. • The student sings Yunus Emre’s hymn ‘I Asked the Yellow Flower’ together with the class and expresses the theme of brotherhood in the hymn.
plan.21. ünite, İslam'ın dostluk, kardeşlik v: Unit 21 conveys the principles of friendship, brotherhood and mutual help in Islam to children aged 7+ through concrete stories and quotations from the Qur’an and hadith. With an opening illustration in which children of different backgrounds are together, the unit makes the universal side of brotherhood in faith visible. In the story “Is It Really Funny?”, respect for labour and the wrongness of mocking are treated through Enes and Kaya meeting an elderly woman who collects rubbish; a father–son dialogue reinforces this message. Then ways of helping children in need are explored, and the principle “relieve the hardship of your believing brother” is grounded in the hadith. The unit also reminds us that zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam.
plan.Hikâyede kimin yerinde olmak istemezdin?: In the story, whose place would you not want to be in? Tell a friend. / What would you do if you were in Enes’s place? Tell a friend. / Discuss with a friend why the children who earn their living from rubbish, and their families, are in need.
plan.Öğrenci, üstünlü harfleri kısa sesle doğ: The student correctly reads letters with fatha as a short sound.
plan.Üstün harekesinin harfe kısa a veya e se: It is shown with examples that the fatha gives the letter a short a or e sound. The students reinforce this by reading the letters with fatha first in chorus and then one by one.
plan.Öğrenci, meleklerin en az beş özelliğini: The student names at least five characteristics of the angels (created from light, never committing sin, obeying Allah, doing good deeds, not being seen with the eye). • The student puts the names of the four great angels (Jibril, Azrail, Mikail, Israfil) in the right order with the memory aid ‘CAMİ’. • Starting from Murat’s story, the student explains that faith in destiny does not rule out working, and that a person must do what they can. • The student states that faith in the angels and in destiny are two of the six articles of faith.
plan.25. ünite, 'Meleklere ve kadere iman edi: Under the title ‘I believe in the angels and in destiny’, Unit 25 introduces two of the basic articles of faith to the child in age-appropriate language. First the angels are treated: that they were created from light, cannot be seen with the eye, never commit sin and always obey Allah’s commands is told in short sentences. The names of the four great angels — Jibril, Azrail, Mikail and Israfil — are taught in a memorable way by linking them with the letters of the word ‘CAMİ’. The unit then moves on to destiny; instead of an abstract definition, this concept is made concrete through the story of a pupil called Murat choosing a school and passing an exam: it is stressed that for one’s destiny to be good, a person must also do what they can.
plan.Sınıf sohbeti: 'Melek gibi insan deyince: Class chat: we talk with our classmate about the question ‘Who comes to our mind when we say a person is like an angel?’
plan.Murat'ın hikâyesini dinledikten sonra 'K: After listening to Murat’s story, we discuss as a class the question ‘What can we do so that our destiny is good?’
plan.Öğrenci, esreli harfleri üstünlü harfler: The student reads letters with kasra, telling them apart from letters with fatha.
plan.Esre harekesinin harfe kısa i sesi verdi: It is explained that the kasra gives the letter a short i sound. The students read letters with kasra paying attention to the movement of the lips and chin, and then make a comparison with the fatha.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) 571 yı: The student tells that the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) was born in Mecca in 571 and why his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib chose this name for him. • The student lists the Prophet Muhammad’s growing up with his wet nurse Halima, losing his mother Amina at the age of six and his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib at the age of eight, and coming under the protection of his uncle Abu Talib. • The student explains the qualities that shepherding in his childhood gave him, such as attention, responsibility and organisation. • The student summarises his meeting with the monk Bahira in Busra on his first trading journey with his uncle at the age of twelve.
plan.Hz. Muhammed (s.a.s.) 571 yılında Mekke': The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) was born in Mecca in 571 as the son of Amina and Abdullah of the Quraysh tribe; his father had died before his birth. His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib gave him the name Muhammad ‘so that everyone in the heavens and on earth would praise him’. Because of Mecca’s harsh climate he was given to his wet nurse Halima and grew up with her until the age of four. At six he lost his mother Amina, and at eight his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, who loved him; after that he came under the protection of his uncle Abu Talib, played with his cousins and grazed his uncle’s sheep. On his first trading journey with his uncle, at the age of twelve, the monk Bahira in Busra noticed in him the signs of the awaited prophet and warned Abu Talib not to take him to Damascus.
plan.Hz. Muhammed'in doğumundan on iki yaşına: Telling in order, on the timeline on the screen, what the Prophet Muhammad lived through from his birth to the age of twelve.
plan.\"Yetimlere nasıl destek olabiliriz?\" s: Answering the question “How can we support orphans?” as a class by brainstorming.
plan.Koyun otlatmanın kazandırdığı özellikler: Listing on the board, with oral examples, the qualities that shepherding gives (attention, responsibility, order).
plan.Öğrenci, ötreli harfleri doğru dudak har: The student pronounces letters with damma with the right movement of the lips.
plan.Ötre harekesinin harfe kısa u sesi verdi: It is shown that the damma gives the letter a short u sound. The students pronounce the letters with damma with a lip-rounding exercise and read from mixed cards.
plan.Öğrenci, hadisin Hz. Peygamber'in (s.a.s: The student explains that the hadith consists of the sayings, actions and approvals of the Prophet (s.a.s.). • The student expresses in their own sentences the difference between the Qur’an and the hadith (the Qur’an lays down the general principles, the hadiths give the details). • Starting from Enes’s story, the student explains with an example that the hadiths give guidance for daily life. • The student matches one verse–hadith example each on prayer, supplication and fasting and shares its meaning in class. • The student knows that brushing the teeth is a sunnah of the Prophet (s.a.s.) and links it to a present-day behaviour.
plan.28. ünite, 'Hadislerle Buluşuyoruz' başl: Unit 28 introduces the concept of the hadith to children under the title ‘Meeting the Hadiths’. The unit opens with a story in which Enes, who avoids brushing his teeth, goes to the dentist and, through the miswak, remembers the sunnah of the Prophet (s.a.s.). Through this story it is taught that a hadith is a saying of the Prophet, that the Qur’an lays down general principles and that the hadiths give the details of these principles. Then one verse and one hadith each on prayer, supplication and fasting are matched, showing how the Qur’an and the hadith complete each other. The unit ends with the hymn ‘Candan İçeru’.
plan.Enes'in hikâyesini dinledikten sonra 'Pe: After listening to Enes’s story, we discuss with our classmate the question ‘Why is what our Prophet did in religious matters important?’
plan.Sınıfça bugüne kadar öğrendiğimiz hadisl: As a class we recall the hadiths we have learnt so far and write them on the board, and we talk about their meanings together.
plan.'Candan İçeru' ilahisini sınıfta hep bir: We sing the hymn ‘Candan İçeru’ together in class.
plan.Öğrenci, teyemmümün ne zaman ve neden ya: The student explains when and why tayammum is performed. • The student tells which surfaces tayammum can and cannot be performed with. • The student lists the basic steps of tayammum and demonstrates them. • The student tells in their own sentences what the full washing (ghusl) means and how it is done. • The student uses the hadith about the Prophet taking a ghusl on Fridays as an example. • The student recognises the French equivalents of the terms ablution, tayammum and ghusl (les ablutions, le tayammum, les grandes ablutions).
plan.26. ünite, çocuklara iki önemli temizlik: Unit 26 teaches children two important acts of purification: tayammum and the full washing (ghusl). In the first part of the unit a scenario is treated in which Enes and his friends cannot find water while having a picnic in the park; through this example from daily life the question “What is done to perform the prayer when there is no water?” is raised. A friend called Bilal shares what he learnt from his sick father and introduces tayammum. How tayammum is done is explained briefly: it is enough to strike the hands twice, with intention, on a surface of clean earth origin (stone, soil, etc.), and to wipe the face with the first strike and the arms up to the elbows with the second; surfaces such as plastic, iron or wood cannot be used for this purpose.
plan.Piknik senaryosu üzerine sınıf tartışmas: Class discussion on the picnic scenario: the pupils are guided to think with the question ‘What kind of solution do you think Bilal found?’ / An activity of showing how tayammum is done: the pupils give practical demonstrations in turn. / The reasons for the Prophet’s taking a ghusl on Fridays and the benefits of taking a ghusl are discussed and shared in class.
plan.Öğrenci, temel harekelerle yazılmış kısa: The student reads as a whole short words written with the basic short vowels.
plan.Üstün, esre ve ötre bulunan iki ve üç ha: Two- and three-letter words containing fatha, kasra and damma are practised. The students read the word first by spelling it out, then as a whole and rhythmically.
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'dan önce Arabistan'da ceh: The student explains that before Islam bad customs such as ignorance, idol worship and the killing of baby girls were widespread in Arabia, and that for this reason a prophet was needed. • The student tells the lineage of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) (father Abdullah, mother Amina, grandfather Abd al-Muttalib) and that he was born in Mecca in 571. • The student summarises how, before his birth, in the Incident of the Elephant, Allah protected the Kaaba from Abraha’s army. • The student tells of the Prophet Muhammad’s childhood, spent with his wet nurse Halima, through the death of his mother Amina at the age of six and of his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib at the age of eight, and under the protection of his uncle Abu Talib.
plan.İslam'dan önce Arabistan'da cehalet, put: Before Islam, bad customs such as ignorance, idol worship and the killing of baby girls were widespread in Arabia; humanity greatly needed a prophet in order to find the right way. The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) was born in Mecca in 571 to Amina, after the death of his father Abdullah; his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib gave him the name Muhammad. Shortly before his birth, Abraha, the governor of Abyssinia, had tried to destroy the Kaaba with an army equipped with elephants; Allah, with birds that He sent, routed that army and protected the Kaaba (the Incident of the Elephant). The Prophet Muhammad first grew up with his wet nurse Halima; at six he lost his mother, at eight his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, who looked after him, and he came under the protection of his uncle Abu Talib.
plan.Fil Vakası'nı ekrandaki harita/görsel üz: Showing the Incident of the Elephant on the map/picture on the screen and putting the events in order orally.
plan.\"İslam'dan önce insanlar neden doğru yo: Discussing as a class the question “Why had people lost the right way before Islam?”
plan.Hz. Muhammed'in çocukluğundaki kayıpları: Revising the losses in the Prophet Muhammad’s childhood (father, mother, grandfather) by naming them in order on the timeline.
plan.Öğrenci, çevreyi temiz tutmanın bir İslâ: The student explains in their own sentences that keeping the environment clean is an Islamic responsibility (an amana, a trust). • The student lists at least three concrete examples of behaviour that protects the environment in daily life. • The student lists the articles of faith in the Amantu (Allah, the angels, the books, the prophets, the hereafter, destiny) and defines each in a short phrase. • The student names the ulu al-‘azm prophets (Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, Muhammad) and explains the meaning of this concept. • The student correctly matches the four great holy books with the prophet to whom each was sent down. • The student sings the hymn ‘One Night’ together in class and expresses its link with the event of the Mi‘raj.
plan.24. Ünite \"Çevrem bana emanet\" başlığı: Under the title “The Environment Is Entrusted to Me”, Unit 24 treats the theme of environmental awareness and responsibility through religious education. A short story told through the eyes of a child named Enes presents intuitively the reason for noticing environmental pollution and being sensitive to it; the teacher’s saying “If we treat nature well, it will treat us well” is something the child is helped to take to heart as the reflection of the Islamic idea of responsibility in daily life. Then the concrete attitudes of different family members (Enes, Meryem, Mother, Father) towards nature are treated: behaviours such as not wasting water, choosing the bicycle, not picking flowers and saving energy. The unit is completed by revising the topics of the Amantu and the ulu al-‘azm prophets.
plan.Enes, Meryem, Anne ve Baba'nın çevre dav: Compare the note cards that list the environmental behaviours of Enes, Meryem, Mother and Father; answer the question ‘Whose list do you think is better?’ / Match the half sentences in the left column with the completing phrases in the right column (the topics of faith in Allah, the Amantu, the ulu al-‘azm prophets, the holy books, zakat); write how many questions you got right. / Fill in the blanks using the given word pool (Moses, four, peace be upon him, Jesus, counted, of religions, to destiny, to the books, Muhammad, Noah, Amantu, Abraham, to His books, my speaking, messenger, Allah, prayer).
plan.Öğrenci, üstün, esre ve ötreyi karıştırm: The student reads fatha, kasra and damma without confusing them.
plan.Üç hareke karışık kelime listeleriyle te: The three short vowels are revised with mixed word lists. The students read in turn, and the teacher gives short feedback by correcting wrongly read vowels on the spot.
plan.Öğrenci, ahirete iman etmenin öldükten s: The student explains that believing in the hereafter means believing that after people die Allah will raise them to life again. • The student expresses in their own sentences that life in this world is a preparation for the life of the hereafter. • The student explains the meaning of Paradise and Hell and links behaviour in this world with its reward in the hereafter.
plan.31. ünite, İslam'ın altı iman esasından: Unit 31 introduces faith in the hereafter, one of the six articles of faith of Islam, to children over 7. The unit opens with a picture about a cemetery visit and makes the fact of death concrete in the child’s eyes. Then it is explained that believing in the hereafter means believing that after dying Allah will raise people to life again and that what is done in this world will be repaid in the hereafter; the existence of Paradise and Hell is stressed, and that life in this world is a preparation for the hereafter. With questions such as ‘What would happen if people never died?’ and ‘What would happen if there were no Paradise and Hell?’, the unit sets the child’s thinking in motion.
plan.'Ne olurdu?' beyin fırtınası: 'İnsanlar: ‘What would happen?’ brainstorm: we discuss with our classmate the questions ‘What would happen if people never died?’ and ‘What would happen if we were not going to give an account in the hereafter?’
plan.'Cennet ve cehennem olmasaydı ne olurdu?: We talk about the question ‘What would happen if there were no Paradise and Hell?’ as a class and share our views.
plan.Öğrenci, caminin Müslümanlar için taşıdı: The student lists, in at least three points, the religious and social functions the mosque has for Muslims. • The student tells the mosque, the synagogue and the church apart by their basic features (special days, rules, name). • The student names the architectural elements of the mosque (mihrab, minbar, minaret, chandelier) and briefly explains the function of each. • The student matches the people who serve in the mosque (imam, muezzin, caretaker) with their duties. • The student lists the basic stages of the hajj (ihram, the standing at Arafat, stoning the devil, tawaf, sa‘y) in the correct order; and tells that the standing at Arafat and the tawaf of visit are obligatory pillars (rukn) of the hajj, while sa‘y and the stoning are wajib. • The student sings Eshrefoğlu Rumi’s hymn ‘O My Allah’ aloud together with the class.
plan.32. ünite, çocukları \"ibadet yerleri\": Unit 32 takes children on a comprehensive journey around the theme of ‘places of worship’. First, the meaning and functions the mosque has for Muslims are explained concretely: worship together, the spirit of the congregation, the adhan and mutual help. Then the perspective is widened and the places of worship of Islam, Judaism and Christianity (mosque, synagogue, church) are treated in a comparative view; the special days and rules of each religion are introduced. In the third stage the inner world of the mosque is detailed: architectural elements such as the mihrab, minbar and minaret are taught through pictures, and the office-holders such as the imam, muezzin and caretaker are introduced. The unit is completed with the basic pillars of the hajj, such as ihram, the standing at Arafat, stoning the devil, tawaf and sa‘y.
plan.Çok beğenilen bir caminin dış görüntüsün: Draw the outside of a mosque you like very much. / Draw a picture showing the inside of the mosque. / Write a short story about memories lived in the mosque.
plan.Öğrenci, cezmli harfi önceki harfe bağla: The student reads a letter with sukun by joining it to the previous letter.
plan.Cezmin harfi sâkin yaptığı ve önceki har: It is explained that the sukun makes the letter silent and joins it to the previous letter that carries a vowel. The students listen to syllables with sukun from the teacher’s mouth, then repeat them slowly and clearly.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) gençli: The student explains that in his youth the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) earned the title “Muhammad al-Amin” through his honesty and trustworthiness and joined the community called the Hilf al-Fudul (the Alliance of the Virtuous). • The student tells how he managed Khadija’s caravan and won her trust, and how he married her on the strength of that trust. • The student recognises Ali, Zayd ibn Haritha and Umm Ayman, who lived together in the household of the Prophet Muhammad and Khadija. • The student explains by what fair solution the Prophet Muhammad settled the dispute over placing the Black Stone when the Kaaba was damaged by fire and flood and was being rebuilt.
plan.Hz. Muhammed (s.a.s.) amcası Ebû Tâlib'i: Through the trade he had learnt with his uncle Abu Talib, the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) had become the most trustworthy merchant in Mecca, had become known as ‘Muhammad al-Amin’ (Muhammad the Trustworthy) because of his honesty, and had joined the Hilf al-Fudul (the Alliance of the Virtuous), a community founded to protect the rights of the wronged. Khadija, whose caravan he took to Damascus, was impressed by his trustworthiness and good character and proposed marriage to him; they married and had six children. Ali, his uncle’s son, Zayd ibn Haritha, whom Khadija had given him as a gift, and Umm Ayman, his mother’s close friend, also lived in their household. When he was thirty-five, the Kaaba, which had been destroyed by fire and flood, was rebuilt; when the tribes could not agree over the honour of placing the Black Stone, Muhammad, who was chosen as arbitrator, settled the dispute fairly by putting the stone on a cloak and having the leader of each tribe hold it by one edge.
plan.\"Güvenilir olmak\" kavramını günlük hay: Discussing as a class the concept of ‘being trustworthy’ with examples from daily life.
plan.Hacerülesved anlaşmazlığının Hz. Muhamme: Telling orally, in the order of events, how the dispute over the Black Stone was settled by the Prophet Muhammad.
plan.Hz. Muhammed'in ailesinde birlikte yaşay: Matching on the board the names of those who lived in the Prophet Muhammad’s household (Ali, Zayd, Umm Ayman).
plan.Öğrenci, aile içindeki görev paylaşımını: The student explains the sharing of duties within the family with examples and lists the responsibilities they can take on. • The student predicts the consequences that may arise when basic family functions such as cleanliness, livelihood, nutrition and order are not carried out. • The student matches Islam’s teachings on relationships within the family (eating together, speaking respectfully, greeting one another, respect for elders) with the relevant verses and hadiths. • The student expresses in their own sentences the religious basis of respectful behaviour towards parents and relatives. • By drawing up house rules together with their reasons, the student shows in practice the importance of being a responsible and understanding member of the family. • The student recognises Yunus Emre’s hymn ‘Muhammad, Beautiful Is His Name, Beautiful Is He’ and expresses love for the Prophet through this hymn.
plan.27. ünite \"Ailem ve görevlerim\" başlığ: Under the title “My Family and My Responsibilities”, Unit 27 aims to give the child a sense of responsibility within the family and Islam’s teachings on home life.
