The unit opens with a table activity: the child thinks about who does household tasks such as buying bread, taking out the rubbish, tidying the room, cleaning, doing the laundry and earning money, marks them, and asks how they can help the family member who carries the most load. Then, with the question “What would happen?”, critical thinking is developed through the consequences that would appear if responsibility were not taken under the headings of cleanliness, livelihood, nutrition and order. The religious dimension is built through Islam’s teachings on relationships within the family, by way of verses and hadiths.
plan.Evdeki görev paylaşımını gösteren tabloy: Filling in the table showing the sharing of household tasks: marking which family member does which household task (buying bread, taking out the rubbish, tidying the room, cleaning the bathroom/toilet, washing the laundry, earning money). / Identifying the family member with the most tasks and thinking about and sharing how they can be helped. / ‘What would happen?’ questions: what would happen if nobody did the cleaning at home, nobody worked, nobody cooked and the rooms were not tidied? — answering on each topic.
plan.Öğrenci, cezm içeren kelimeleri duraksam: The student works out words containing sukun without hesitation.
plan.Cezmli iki ve üç heceli kelimeler tahtad: Two- and three-syllable words with sukun are read by splitting them on the board. The students follow with a finger and check each other’s reading by listening in pairs.
plan.Öğrenci, Kelime-i Tevhid ve Kelime-i Şeh: The student correctly says the Turkish meaning of the Declaration of Oneness (kalimat at-tawhid) and the Shahadah (kalimat ash-shahadah). • The student tells apart the concepts believer (mu’min), Muslim, hypocrite (munafiq), disbeliever (kafir), polytheist (mushrik) and People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab). • The student defines the concept of the Most Beautiful Names (Asma’ al-Husna) and names at least five of Allah’s names with their meanings. • The student tells apart Allah’s essential attributes (dhati) and affirmative attributes (thubuti) and gives examples from each group.
plan.Bu ünite, Allah'a imanın temel kavramlar: This unit introduces the basic concepts of faith in Allah to children in an age-appropriate way. First the Declaration of Oneness (kalimat at-tawhid) and the Shahadah (kalimat ash-shahadah) are treated, reminding us of the verbal expression of the foundation of Islamic belief; then the concepts of believer, Muslim, hypocrite, disbeliever, polytheist and People of the Book are told apart with their use in the Qur’an. The second dimension of the topic is formed by Allah’s beautiful names (Asma’ al-Husna): with examples from Surah al-A‘raf and Surah al-Hashr, it is treated how Allah’s names help us to know Him. Finally, Allah’s six essential and eight affirmative attributes are introduced; in the younger age group these attributes may be treated not as a full list but limited to examples.
plan.Kelime-i Şehadet ve Kelime-i Tevhid'in a: We repeat the meaning of the Shahadah and the Declaration of Oneness aloud as a class, and write on the board where we say them.
plan.Mümin, Müslüman, kâfir, münafık, müşrik: We tell in class where we have heard the concepts believer, Muslim, disbeliever, hypocrite, polytheist and People of the Book before.
plan.Haşr suresinde geçen Esma-i Hüsna'lardan: We choose five of the Most Beautiful Names that appear in Surah al-Hashr and share their meanings with the class.
plan.Kelime-i Tevhid: 'Lâ ilâhe illallah, Muh: The Declaration of Oneness: ‘Lâ ilâhe illallah, Muhammedün Resûlüllah’ — There is no God but Allah and Muhammad (s.a.s.) is the Messenger of Allah.
plan.Kelime-i Şehadet: 'Eşhedü en lâ ilâhe il: The Shahadah: ‘Eşhedü en lâ ilâhe illallah ve eşhedü enne Muhammeden abdühû ve resûlüh’ — I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) is the slave and the Messenger of Allah.
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'ın beş şartını sıralar ve: The student lists the five pillars of Islam and explains the short meaning of each. • The student names the obligatory and recommended acts of ablution and states in which cases ablution is broken. • The student explains with examples the rules of etiquette to be observed when entering the mosque and during worship. • The student recognises the basic requirements of praying in congregation, such as the order of the rows and following the imam. • The student tells apart the architectural parts of the mosque (mihrab, minbar, pulpit, gallery) on a picture and explains their functions. • The student expresses in their own sentences the importance worship has for the human soul.
plan.Bu ünite, çocukların İslam'ın temel ibad: This unit is designed so that children get to know the basic acts of worship in Islam and correctly grasp the process of preparing for worship. The meaning and importance of the obligatory acts of worship such as the prayer, fasting, zakat and the hajj are conveyed in an appealing and concrete way through characters of the children’s own age (Amira, Bilal, Elif, Parisa). The students discover that worship is not merely an action but the outward expression of love and devotion to Allah. How ablution is performed, in which cases it is broken and when the full washing (ghusl) is needed are treated step by step. The rules of the congregation, such as etiquette on entering the mosque, dress, forming rows and following the imam, are also treated.
plan.Allah rızası için bugüne kadar yapılan i: Let us recall the good deeds we have done so far for the sake of Allah’s pleasure and share them with the class. / Let us recall the five pillars of Islam by listing them and write them in our notebooks. / Let us make a concept/decision map together in class about the meaning and importance of acts of worship.
plan.Öğrenci, şeddeli harfi çift ses değerine: The student reads a letter with shadda, paying attention to its double sound value.
plan.Şeddenin harfi önce sâkin, sonra harekel: It is explained that the shadda makes the letter read first without a vowel and then with its vowel. The students do a rhythm exercise with hand claps to make the stress on the letter with shadda felt.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) on iki: The student recalls the journeys of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) to Busra at the age of twelve, where he met Bahira, and to Yemen at the age of seventeen. • The student explains that Khadija gave him capital and sent the Prophet Muhammad to Syria, and that thanks to his honesty he brought back a large profit. • The student tells that the twenty-five-year-old Prophet Muhammad married the forty-year-old Khadija, and names their seven children (Qasim, Abdullah, Ibrahim; Zaynab, Ruqayya, Umm Kulthum, Fatima). • The student knows that our Prophet’s lineage continued through his daughter Fatima, who married Ali. • The student tells how the dispute over placing the Black Stone was settled through the arbitration of the thirty-five-year-old Prophet Muhammad.
plan.Hz. Muhammed (s.a.s.) on iki yaşında amc: On the journey to Damascus he made with his uncle at the age of twelve, the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) met a monk named Bahira in Busra, and at seventeen he had gone to Yemen with his uncle Zubayr. Khadija, a wealthy widow and merchant, gave him capital and sent him to Syria with a caravan; thanks to his honesty he returned with more profit than expected. On the strength of this trust, the twenty-five-year-old Muhammad married the forty-year-old Khadija; they had seven children, three boys (Qasim, Abdullah, Ibrahim) and four girls (Zaynab, Ruqayya, Umm Kulthum, Fatima). Our Prophet’s lineage continued through his daughter Fatima, who married Ali. At the age of thirty-five, while the Kaaba, which had been destroyed by a flood, was being repaired, he settled through arbitration the dispute that arose among the tribes over the honour of placing the Black Stone, by putting the stone on a cloth and having each tribal leader hold it by an edge.
plan.Hz. Muhammed'in yaşına göre yolculukları: Putting the Prophet Muhammad’s journeys in order by age on the timeline on the screen (age 12 Busra, age 17 Yemen, marriage at age 25, arbitration at age 35).
plan.Yedi çocuğunun adlarını tahtada erkek/kı: Grouping the names of his seven children on the board in two columns, boys and girls.
plan.Hacerülesved olayını \"neden hakem seçil: Discussing the Black Stone episode as a class with the question “Why was he chosen as arbitrator?”
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'ın iki büyük bayramının a: The student correctly says the names of the two great festivals of Islam (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha) and explains in short sentences why each is celebrated. • The student expresses in their own sentences the link between Eid al-Adha and the story that tested Abraham’s obedience to Allah. • The student tells with examples that Eid celebrations are a social joy shared with family, school, friends and neighbours. • The student explains the importance of visiting elders at Eid within the framework of Islamic values. • The student sings Yunus Emre’s hymn ‘Those Rivers of Paradise’ aloud in class and recognises the descriptions of Paradise in the hymn. • The student correctly uses the basic concepts learnt during the term (revelation, Jibril, hadith, ablution, tayammum, ghusl, the names of the two Eids) in matching and fill-in-the-blank questions.
plan.30. Ünite \"Bayramlarımız\" başlığıyla İ: Under the title “Our Eid Festivals”, Unit 30 introduces the two great festivals of Islam, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, in a context that is close and meaningful to children. The unit opens with a dialogue between a child named Elif and her teacher after she asks to take part in Christmas celebrations; in this way the idea that Muslims have their own distinctive festivals settles naturally in the child’s mind. It is stated that this does not prevent them from congratulating their friends on their festivals. The religious and historical background of Eid al-Adha is made concrete by linking it with the story of Abraham, who in unconditional obedience to Allah’s command prepared to sacrifice his son. Eid al-Fitr, on the other hand, is linked with the act of fasting.
plan.Kurban ve Ramazan Bayramlarının neden ku: Making a mind map by finding out why Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr are celebrated. / Telling orally how the pupils spend their Eids with their families, school friends, friends and neighbours. / Matching the sentence beginnings in the left column with the right completions in the right column (assessment questions).
plan.Öğrenci, şeddeli kelimeleri doğru vurgu: The student reads words with shadda with correct stress and fluency.
plan.Şedde bulunan kısa kelimeler önce öğretm: Short words containing shadda are practised first by the teacher’s instruction and then by individual reading. The students tell the stress apart by comparing examples with sukun and with shadda.
plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in Kitab, Furkan: The student names the names of the Holy Qur’an such as Kitab, Furqan, Dhikr and Kalamullah and briefly explains their meanings. • The student lists at least three of the rules of etiquette to be observed while reading the Holy Qur’an. • The student shows the parts of a hadith (the chain of narrators, the text and the source book) on an example hadith. • The student expresses in their own sentences a piece of advice drawn from the example hadiths given.
plan.Bu ünite, Kur'an-ı Kerim ve hadisin İsla: This unit introduces children to the fact that the Holy Qur’an and the hadith are the two basic religious sources of Islam. The names of the Holy Qur’an such as Kitab, Furqan, Dhikr and Kalamullah are explained; it is stressed that this book, whose reading is an act of worship, must be held with respect, used cleanly and listened to in silence. Then the topic of the hadith is treated: with example hadiths it is shown that what the Prophet (s.a.s.) said is called hadith and its practice sunnah, and that hadiths consist of a chain of narrators (isnad), a text and a source book. The unit ends with two example hadiths on mercy and the rights of the neighbour.
plan.Sınıfça 'Kutsal kitabımız Kur'an' başlığ: As a class we prepare a concept map suited to the title ‘Our holy book is the Qur’an’.
plan.Örnek hadisleri okuyup sened ve metin bö: We read the example hadiths and mark the chain-of-narrators and text parts together.
plan.'Komşusu aç olduğu halde tok yatan iyi b: We read the hadith ‘A person who goes to bed full while his neighbour is hungry cannot be a good believer’ and discuss with our classmate why our Prophet may have said it.
plan.Öğrenci, duanın yalnızca dilek sunmak ol: The student explains that supplication is not only making requests; it also has the dimensions of seeking refuge in Allah, praising Him, sharing one’s troubles and confessing sins. • The student recognises Surah al-Fatiha as a complete example of supplication within worship and classifies the elements of meaning in the surah. • Starting from the supplications of Moses (peace be upon him) reported in the Qur’an, the student explains with examples the importance of praying sincerely and from the heart. • The student reads supplication verses chosen from the Qur’an, above all verse 186 of Surah al-Baqara, and links Allah’s closeness to His servants with these verses. • The student thinks about what matters they can pray about in their daily life, expresses it in a few sentences, and practises supplication as a conscious act of worship. • The student lists the basic points to be observed when praying and shows an attitude of supplication that follows these rules.
plan.Bu ünite, duanın ibadet hayatının merkez: This unit aims to help students grasp that supplication stands at the centre of the life of worship and that it is not merely a list of wishes but a deep and sincere communication with Allah. It is explained that supplication includes the heart’s turning to Allah, seeking refuge in Him, gratitude and confessing sins. It is stressed that Surah al-Fatiha, recited in every rak‘a of the prayer, is in this sense a complete example of supplication; students are expected to grasp the elements of meaning of the surah. Moses’ (peace be upon him) turning to his Lord when alone, praying both for himself and for his people, and confessing his sins are conveyed with examples from the Qur’an. Allah’s closeness is stressed with verse 186 of Surah al-Baqara.
plan.Fotoğraflardaki kişileri tanımlayın ve f: Describe the people in the photographs and find what they have in common. / Classify the elements of supplication in Surah al-Fatiha (seeking refuge, praise, asking for help, asking for guidance) in a table and fill in the blanks working in pairs; then discuss the relation of the Fatiha to supplication. / First write your own thoughts about the supplication of Moses (peace be upon him), then share and discuss them with your friend.
plan.Öğrenci, sâkin ve şeddeli okuma örnekler: The student correctly applies the examples of reading letters without a vowel and letters with shadda.
plan.Cezm ve şedde içeren karışık kelimeler k: Mixed words containing sukun and shadda are revised with a short reading test. Each student is given an individual turn at reading, and wrong sounds are corrected on the spot.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed'in (s.a.s.) kırk y: The student tells that, as he approached the age of forty, the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) withdrew to the Cave of Hira to reflect and there received the first revelation through Jibril (peace be upon him). • The student says that the first verses revealed were the first five verses of Surah al-‘Alaq and that they began with the command “Read!”. • The student explains Khadija’s comforting of our Prophet and that Waraqa linked this event with the revelation that came to Moses and Jesus. • The student states that the Prophet Muhammad first began to convey the message secretly, and then openly on the hill of Safa.
plan.Kırk yaşına yaklaşan Hz. Muhammed (s.a.s: Approaching the age of forty, the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) often withdrew to the Cave of Hira on Mount Nur to reflect. In the month of Ramadan of the year 610, while he was in the cave, the angel Jibril (peace be upon him) appeared to him, said ‘Read!’ and had him recite the first five verses of Surah al-‘Alaq; thus the first revelation took place. His wife Khadija comforted our Prophet, who had returned home in fear; her relative Waraqa compared what had happened with the revelation that came to Moses and Jesus, and said that it was a sign of prophethood and that his people might one day drive him out of this land. Our Prophet began conveying the message, first secretly to those close to him, and then by climbing the hill of Safa and calling the Meccans openly to believe in Allah and to keep away from evil.
plan.Alak sûresinin ilk beş ayetinin mealini: Reading the meaning of the first five verses of Surah al-‘Alaq from the screen all together.
plan.\"Oku!\" emrinin Hz. Muhammed'e ne hisse: Sharing orally what the command “Read!” may have made the Prophet Muhammad feel.
plan.Varaka'nın Hz. Mûsâ ve Hz. Îsâ ile yaptı: Discussing Waraqa’s comparison with Moses and Jesus with the question “Why do prophets meet difficulties?”
plan.Öğrenci, güzel sözlerin ve kaba sözlerin: The student explains by comparison the different effects kind words and rude words have on people. • The student recognises the expressions of thanks, apology and greeting used in the Islamic tradition and uses them in daily life. • Starting from the story ‘The Echo’, the student expresses with an example that the words one says are reflected back on the other person. • The student reads the hadith reported from Bukhari and verse 30 of Surah al-Hajj and explains their meaning and message in their own sentences. • By putting the events of the story ‘The Wallet’ in order, the student expresses the harms of lying and the importance of honesty. • The student tells good words and behaviour apart from rude words and behaviour and gives examples.
plan.33. ünite, \"Güzel konuşur ve güzel davr: Under the title “I Speak Kindly and I Act Kindly”, Unit 33 introduces the child to the basics of good conduct in speech and behaviour. Throughout the unit it is stressed that kind words raise a person up, while rude words harm both the speaker and the listener; this truth is made concrete through the story called “The Echo”: Bilal hearing his own shout in the mountains teaches the child that what he says will be reflected back exactly onto the other person. Then expressions specific to the Islamic tradition that strengthen courtesy in daily life, such as thanking, apologising and greeting, are treated; both their religious and their social dimensions are brought forward. The unit is completed by treating the importance of honesty with the story ‘The Wallet’.
plan.Sınıfça 'güzel sözler ağacı' hazırlama:: Preparing a ‘tree of kind words’ as a class: the pupils write their favourite kind words on leaves and add them to the tree. / Preparing a ‘tree of rude words’ as a class: expressions we do not want to be said are identified and hung on the tree. / Preparing, with a classmate, a poster showing how to react to kind and rude words.
plan.Öğrenci, iki üstünlü kelimeleri doğru se: The student reads words with tanwin fatha with the right sound value.
plan.İki üstünün kelime sonunda en veya an se: It is taught with examples that the tanwin fatha gives an -en or -an sound at the end of a word. The students read the letters with tanwin one by one and repeat them without dropping the sound at the end of the word.
plan.Öğrenci, Amentü duasının Türkçe anlamını: The student says the Turkish meaning of the Amantu prayer and names the six articles of faith. • The student recognises, with examples, the unseen beings mentioned in the Qur’an (angels, the spirit, jinn, Satan). • Starting from the story of the ‘clever young man’, the student explains why we can believe in the existence of things that cannot be seen with the eye. • Drawing on Ayça’s story, the student notices that the angels record every action of a person by Allah’s permission. • The student lists at least four of the main duties of the angels (carrying revelation, regulating nature, blowing the Trumpet, taking souls, etc.).
plan.Bu ünite, İslam inanç esaslarından biri: This unit centres on faith in the angels, one of the articles of belief of Islam, and introduces children to the world of unseen beings. The unit, which begins by recalling the Amantu prayer, teaches that, besides the angels, beings that cannot be seen with the eye, such as the spirit, the jinn and Satan, are established by verses of the Qur’an. The story of the ‘clever and believing young man’ makes concrete why we believe in things that cannot be seen; Ayça’s walnut story shows that Allah and the angels are with us everywhere. Finally, the main duties of the angels (carrying revelation, regulating nature, blowing the Trumpet, recording deeds, etc.) are listed.
plan.Amentü duasının Türkçe anlamını sınıfça: We repeat the Turkish meaning of the Amantu prayer aloud as a class.
plan.Görmediğimiz halde var olduğuna inandığı: We share in class things we believe exist although we do not see them (such as the wind, love, reason), and make a concept map on the board.
plan.Meleklerin görevlerinden üçünü sıra arka: With our classmate we act out three of the duties of the angels, each with a movement.
plan.Âmentü: 'Âmentü billâhi ve melâiketihî v: The Amantu: ‘Âmentü billâhi ve melâiketihî ve kütübihî ve rusülihî ve’l-yevmi’l-âhiri ve bi’l-kaderi hayrihî ve şerrihî minallahi teâlâ ve’l-ba‘sü ba‘de’l-mevti hakk. Eşhedü en lâ ilâhe illallah ve eşhedü enne Muhammeden abdühû ve resûlüh’ — I believe in Allah, in His angels, in His books, in His Messengers, in the Last Day (Day of Judgment) and in the fact that everything good or bad is decided by Allah the Almighty, and in the life after death, all of them are true. I witness that there is no god but Allah and I witness that Muhammad (s.a.s.) is His slave and Messenger.
plan.Öğrenci, farz, vacip, sünnet, mekruh ve: The student tells apart the concepts fard, wajib, sunnah, makruh and haram with examples. • The student explains in their own sentences that the prayer is an act of worship performed with body and soul together. • The student classifies the kinds of prayer (fard, wajib, sunnah, nafila) with examples. • The student names the twelve conditions of the prayer (six outside it, six inside it). • The student recognises the basic terms about the prayer of Arabic origin (taharat, qiyam, qira’at, ruku‘, sujud) with their Turkish equivalents.
plan.Bu derste önce farz, vacip, sünnet, mekr: In this lesson the concepts fard, wajib, sunnah, makruh and haram are first recalled. Then it is treated that the prayer is an act of worship performed not only with the body but with heart and body together, through the meanings carried by facing the Kaaba, the takbir, the recitation, bowing and prostration. The hadith of our Prophet (s.a.s.) that likens the five daily prayers to a river that washes away sins is read. The kinds of prayer, fard, wajib, sunnah and nafila, are classified with examples. Finally the twelve conditions of the prayer are introduced: the six conditions outside the prayer (purity from ritual impurity, purity from filth, covering the awra, facing the qibla, the time, the intention) and the six inside it (the opening takbir, standing, recitation, bowing, prostration, the final sitting), and the terms of Arabic origin related to these conditions are learnt.
plan.Tahtaya farz, vacip, sünnet, mekruh ve h: Writing the headings fard, wajib, sunnah, makruh and haram on the board and finding oral examples for each as a class.
plan.Namaz kılarken yapılan hareketleri (Kâbe: Acting out in place, in order, the movements made while praying (facing the Kaaba, takbir, bowing, prostration, greeting) and completing the ‘because’ sentence of each movement.
plan.Namazın on iki şartını defterde iki sütu: Taking notes from the board as a class in the notebook in two columns (conditions outside the prayer / conditions inside the prayer) on the twelve conditions of the prayer.
plan.Öğrenci, iki esreli kelimeleri tenvin se: The student reads words with tanwin kasra keeping the tanwin sound.
plan.İki esrenin in sesini verdiği ve kelime: It is explained that the tanwin kasra gives an -in sound and how it is read at the end of a word. The students reinforce the tanwin sound by reading the examples first slowly and then fluently.
plan.Öğrenci, kırk yaşındaki Hz. Muhammed'e (: The student tells that in the month of Ramadan of the year 610, in the Cave of Hira, the first five verses of Surah al-‘Alaq were revealed through Jibril (peace be upon him) to the forty-year-old Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.). • The student explains the “interval of the revelation” (fatra) and that after this period the revelation began again with Surah al-Muddaththir. • The student names the first Muslims (Khadija, Ali, Zayd ibn Haritha, Abu Bakr) and says that the secret call lasted three years. • The student tells that, because of the pressure of the polytheists, the Muslims migrated to Abyssinia in two groups and that King Negus found them in the right and protected them.
plan.Kırk yaşındaki Hz. Muhammed'e (s.a.s.),: To the forty-year-old Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.), in the month of Ramadan of the year 610 in the Cave of Hira, Jibril (peace be upon him) appeared and conveyed the first five verses of Surah al-‘Alaq; after this first revelation the revelation stopped for a while (the fatra period), and then began again with Surah al-Muddaththir. Our Prophet first invited those he trusted to Islam in secret; the first Muslims were his wife Khadija, Ali, Zayd ibn Haritha and Abu Bakr; the secret call lasted three years and the number of Muslims passed thirty. Because of the polytheists’ growing persecution, a first group made up of eleven men and four women (among them Uthman and his wife Ruqayya) migrated to Abyssinia; a year later a second group of eighty people under the leadership of Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib joined them. The Christian King Negus, despite the request of the Meccan envoys, found the Muslims in the right and gave them his protection.
plan.Fetret devrinin ne anlama geldiğini sözl: Defining orally what the interval of the revelation means and showing on the timeline the waiting between the first revelation and Surah al-Muddaththir.
plan.İlk Müslümanların adlarını ekrana yansıt: Showing the names of the first Muslims on the screen and repeating them in order.
plan.\"Necâşî neden Müslümanları haklı buldu?: Discussing as a class the question “Why did Negus find the Muslims in the right?”
plan.Öğrenci, hadis kavramını 'Hz. Peygamber': The student defines the concept of hadith as ‘the words the Prophet said’. • The student explains with a concrete example that being a means to a good deed earns reward. • The student memorises the hadith ‘The strong man is the one who overcomes his anger’ and expresses its meaning in their own sentences. • The student memorises the Prophet’s advice about serving one’s mother and gives an example of how it can be applied in daily life. • The student explains the consequences of lying and immorality through the relevant hadith. • The student links the principle of making things easy for people and giving good news to a hadith and produces an example from their own life.
plan.34. ünite, Hz. Peygamber'in (s.a.s.) had: Unit 34 aims to give children the basic values of Islamic morality by centring on the hadiths and moral advice of the Prophet (s.a.s.). The unit opens with a story called “Kindness Comes Back to You”: through a child who has fallen out with his family helping a stranger who is elderly on a cold winter day, and that kindness leading in the end back to his own father, the concrete return of kindness and helpfulness is shown. The Prophet, interpreting this event, teaches that even being a means to a good deed earns reward; thus the child grasps that kindness creates a chain effect. Then four basic hadiths are treated. The topics of overcoming anger, serving one’s mother, honesty and ease are dealt with.
plan.'Kim bir hayra vesile olursa, ona o hayr: Memorising the hadith ‘Whoever is the means of a good deed will have a reward like that of the one who does it.’ (Muslim, Imara 133) and drawing a picture that reflects the story. / Memorising the hadith and writing an original story that fits it. / Memorising the hadith and listing in the notebook how kindness can be done to people.
plan.Öğrenci, iki ötreli kelimeleri doğru dud: The student reads words with tanwin damma with the right movement of the lips.
plan.İki ötrenin un sesini verdiği dudak hare: It is shown with a lip movement that the tanwin damma gives an -un sound. The students read the examples with tanwin damma in chorus, and then each pronounces the word the teacher points to.
plan.Öğrenci, meleklerin genel özelliklerinde: The student names at least four of the general characteristics of the angels (created from light, having no gender, never tiring, being free of sin). • The student matches the duties of the four great angels (Jibril, Azrail, Mikail, Israfil) together with the Kiraman Katibin (the honourable recording angels). • The student explains with an example how Satan tries to lead a person to evil and away from worship. • The student expresses in their own sentences the meaning of repentance (tawba) and that regret means making a promise to Allah. • The student defines the concepts of false belief and superstition and notices that they have no connection with our religion.
plan.Bu ünite, önceki dersin devamında melekl: Continuing from the previous lesson, this unit introduces the general characteristics of the angels, the four great angels and the Kiraman Katibin, and then moves on to protection from Satan and repentance. It recalls that the angels are beings created from light, without gender and without sin, and the duties of Jibril, Azrail, Mikail and Israfil. That Satan tries to lead a person to evil and, through whispering in the prayer, away from worship is illustrated with the custom of stoning the devil at the Jamarat. It is explained that repentance means feeling regret for a sin and making a promise to Allah, and that the most beautiful prayer of repentance is the sayyid al-istighfar. The unit ends by reminding us that false beliefs and superstitions have nothing to do with our religion.
plan.Kümelere ayrılıp dört büyük melek ve Kir: Dividing into groups, we present orally in class a poster draft that introduces the four great angels and the Kiraman Katibin.
plan.Şeytandan korunmak için nasıl davranmamı: As a class we list on the board, under the heading ‘What I will do to pray with humility’, how we should behave in order to protect ourselves from Satan.
plan.Çevremizdeki yaygın bâtıl inançları (naz: We discuss the false beliefs common around us (the evil-eye bead, the black cat, an unlucky day, etc.) in class and come up with a shared definition of ‘false belief’.
plan.Öğrenci, beş vakit namaz ile cuma namazı: The student correctly names the numbers of rak‘as of the five daily prayers and the Friday prayer (sunnah – fard – final sunnah). • The student explains that the Eid prayer is wajib, the order in which it is performed and when the takbir of tashriq is recited. • The student tells the definition of the funeral prayer, its character as a collective obligation (fard kifaya) and how it is performed with four takbirs without bowing or prostration. • Starting from the example episode (Enes, Esra, Furkan), the student lists the behaviours that invalidate the prayer (talking, laughing, eating and drinking, turning away from the qibla). • The student explains with examples the personal and social characteristics of a person who prays.
plan.Bu derste önce beş vakit namaz ile cuma: In this lesson the sunnah, fard and final sunnah rak‘as of the five daily prayers and the Friday prayer are first recalled on a table. Then it is explained that the Eids are days of joy, that the Eid prayer is wajib and the order in which it is performed (intention, takbirs, Fatiha, bowing, prostration, greeting, sermon); the takbir of tashriq recited at Eid al-Adha is introduced. It is taught that the funeral prayer is a collective obligation (fard kifaya) performed in congregation for the person who has died, without bowing or prostration, with four takbirs. Through the story of Enes, Esra and Furkan it is made concrete that talking, laughing, eating or drinking something and turning away from the qibla invalidate the prayer. Finally the personal (peace, fear of Allah) and social (mutual help, thinking of others) characteristics of a person who prays are treated with examples.
plan.Beş vakit namazın sünnet-farz-son sünnet: Completing as a class the numbers of sunnah-fard-final sunnah rak‘as of the five daily prayers in the table on the board.
plan.Enes, Esra ve Furkan'ın hikâyesinden har: Starting from the story of Enes, Esra and Furkan, drawing up orally as a class the “list of things that invalidate the prayer” and writing it in the notebooks.
plan.Namaz kılan bir insanın bireysel ve topl: Filling in as a class, with examples, a two-column table in the notebook of the personal and social characteristics of a person who prays.
plan.Teşrik tekbiri: \"Allâhu ekber, Allâhu e: The takbir of tashriq: “Allâhu ekber, Allâhu ekber, lâ ilâhe illallâhu vallâhu ekber, Allâhu ekber ve lillâhi’l-hamd.” (At Eid al-Adha it is recited after the closing greeting of every obligatory prayer, from the morning of the day of Arafa until the afternoon prayer of the fourth day of the Eid.)
plan.Öğrenci, tenvin çeşitlerini kelime içind: The student correctly tells apart the kinds of tanwin within a word.
plan.Üç tenvin çeşidi karışık kısa kelimelerd: The three kinds of tanwin are practised in mixed short words. The students mark the sound at the end of the word, and then read the word as a whole at the right tempo.
plan.Öğrenci, mutluluk, üzüntü, hastalık ve t: The student correctly matches the religious expressions used in different everyday situations such as happiness, sadness, illness and danger (Alhamdulillah, Inna lillah, Mashallah, etc.) with their context. • The student gives examples of Turkish prayers and good wishes said in social situations such as visiting the sick, offering condolences, congratulating on a newborn and wishing good health. • The student defines the concepts of ‘mercy’ and ‘a blessed long life’ and explains their place in Islamic morality. • The student reads the Alhamdulillah prayer with its Arabic and its Turkish meaning and explains the importance of gratitude in religion. • The student answers the assessment questions by drawing on what they have learnt before about basic religious knowledge such as the articles of faith, the mosque, places of worship and the characteristics of hadiths.
plan.36. ünite olan \"Dinim hayatım\", İslam: Unit 36, “My Religion Is My Life”, teaches children through concrete contexts how the religion of Islam gives meaning and direction to every moment of daily life. At the opening of the unit, through the example of children visiting a sick friend, the message is given that religious values make social relationships more beautiful. Then, which religious expressions Muslims use in different life situations such as happiness, sadness, illness, danger and death (remembrances such as Alhamdulillah, Inna lillah and Mashallah) is treated with examples. The students both make sense of these expressions and learn to use them in the right context through practical activities. The prayer wishes said when visiting the sick and offering condolences are also taught.
plan.Beş çocuğun anlattığı günlük yaşam durum: An activity of reading the everyday situations told by five children and finding and matching the suitable religious expression (prayer/remembrance) for each. / Match the cards containing the prayer/congratulation words said to the sick, to the relatives of someone who has died, to families with a newborn baby and to healthy people with the right group. / Join the half sentences in the left and right columns by their meanings with dotted lines; write the number you got right in the box at the bottom of the page.
plan.Öğrenci, tenvinli kelimeleri hatasız ve: The student reads words with tanwin without mistakes and quickly.
plan.Tenvinli kelimeler okuma kartları ve kıs: Words with tanwin are revised with reading cards and a short matching game. The teacher individually checks each student’s reading of tanwin fatha, tanwin kasra and tanwin damma.
plan.Öğrenci, med harflerini tanır ve kelimed: The student recognises the letters of prolongation and notices the lengthening in a word.
plan.Elif, vâv ve ye med harflerinin önceki h: It is shown that the letters of prolongation Elif, Vâv and Ye lengthen according to the preceding vowel. The students follow the difference between short and long reading with a hand sign and repeat the example words.
plan.Öğrenci, üç yıllık gizli davetin ardında: The student tells how, after the three-year secret call, the open call commanded by verses began on the hill of Safa. • The student explains the importance of patience with the examples of Bilal, Ammar ibn Yasir and his mother Sumayya in the face of the persecution the polytheists inflicted on the Muslims. • The student lists the reasons why the Quraysh were hostile to Islam (fear of equality, concern for trade, attachment to the customs inherited from their ancestors). • The student tells the stories of how Hamza and Umar became Muslims as examples of how faith changes hearts.
plan.Üç yıllık gizli davetin ardından inen ây: After the three-year secret call, with the verses that were revealed our Prophet (s.a.s.) invited first his relatives and then all the people of Mecca openly to Islam on the hill of Safa; his uncle Abu Lahab opposed this call. The polytheists inflicted severe persecution on the Muslims; Abu Bakr bought Bilal al-Habashi and set him free, and Ammar ibn Yasir’s mother Sumayya and his father Yasir were martyred under torture and are regarded as the first martyrs of Islam. Enemies such as Abu Jahl and Abu Lahab fuelled the Quraysh’s opposition to Islam out of concern for equality and trade; although the polytheists pressed Abu Talib, he did not give up protecting his nephew. His uncle Hamza, angered by Abu Jahl’s insult to our Prophet, became a Muslim. Umar, who set out to kill our Prophet, listened to Surah Ta-Ha in the house of his sister Fatima, his heart softened and he became a Muslim, and the Muslims performed the prayer openly at the Kaaba for the first time.
plan.Hz. Hamza ve Hz. Ömer'in Müslüman oluş h: Comparing orally the stories of how Hamza and Umar became Muslims: “What brought each of them to Islam?”
plan.\"Zorlukla karşılaşan bir arkadaşımıza n: Discussing the question “How do we support a friend who meets difficulties?” starting from Abu Bakr’s rescue of Bilal.
plan.Açık davetin Safâ tepesinde başlamasını: Showing on the timeline that the open call began on the hill of Safa.
plan.Öğrenci, medli kelimelerde uzatma yerini: The student correctly applies the place of lengthening in words with prolongation.
plan.Med harfleri bulunan kelimeler bir elif: Words that contain letters of prolongation are read with a lengthening of one elif. The students mark the place to be lengthened with a colour, and then pronounce the word in a measured and fluent way.
plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in Allah tarafın: The student says that the Holy Qur’an was revealed in Arabic by Allah to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) over 23 years. • The student states that the Holy Qur’an consists of 114 surahs and 6,236 verses and that not one of its verses has been changed. • The student names at least four of the names given to the Qur’an (Book, Furqan, Light, Healing, Guidance, Dhikr, Word) with their meanings. • Drawing on verses, the student explains with examples the Qur’an’s qualities of giving advice, giving good news, warning and guiding.
plan.10. ünite, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in temel özell: Unit 10 takes up the basic features of the Holy Qur’an again, reinforcing what the children already know. It is recalled that the Qur’an is the word of Allah, that it was sent down by revelation to the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) over 23 years, that it consists of 114 surahs and 6,236 verses and that not one of its verses has been changed. Then the beautiful names given to the Qur’an (Book, Furqan, Light, Healing, Guidance, Dhikr, Word) are introduced. Finally, through four verses, it is shown that the Qur’an gives advice, brings good news, warns and guides; it is stressed that the Qur’an must not only be read but put into practice.
plan.Kümelere ayrılıp Kur'an'ın isimlerinden: Dividing into groups, we each choose one of the names of the Qur’an and tell the class orally what this name reminds us of.
plan.Kur'an-ı Kerim'in dört özelliğini anlata: We read the verses that describe four features of the Holy Qur’an and, in groups of three, find an example from our daily life for each.
plan.Öğrenci, Cuma gününün Müslümanlar için h: The student explains that Friday is regarded as a weekly festival for Muslims, and its virtue. • The student lists the importance of the Eids of Ramadan and of Sacrifice and the behaviours to be carried out at the Eids (visiting, making peace, giving charity). • The student names the five blessed nights (Mawlid, Raghaib, Mi‘raj, Bara’a, Qadr) and says in which month each falls. • The student tells in order the events of the Night of the Mi‘raj (the Isra and Mi‘raj, the gift of the five daily prayers). • The student explains the relation of the Night of Destiny to the revelation of the Qur’an.
plan.Bu derste önce Cuma gününün haftalık bir: In this lesson, first Friday, which is regarded as a weekly festival, and the hadiths about its virtue are recalled. It is explained that the Eids of Ramadan and of Sacrifice are days of joy, that at the Eids the poor are helped with zakat, fitrana and the meat of the sacrifice, that elders are visited and those who have fallen out make peace. The Mawlid night, the birth night of our Prophet (s.a.s.), and Süleyman Çelebi’s mawlid, the Vesiletü’n-Necat, are introduced. Raghaib, the first Friday night of the month of Rajab; the Mi‘raj, on which the Isra and Mi‘raj miracle took place and the five daily prayers were given as a gift; Bara’a, the fifteenth night of the month of Sha‘ban; and the Night of Destiny, on which the Qur’an began to be revealed and which is better than a thousand months, are treated in turn. It is stressed that the blessed nights should be spent with prayer, reading the Qur’an, supplication and giving help.
plan.Sınıfça beş kandil gecesini (Mevlit, Reg: Writing the five blessed nights (Mawlid, Raghaib, Mi‘raj, Bara’a, Qadr) in order on the board as a class and saying which month each falls in.
plan.Miraç Gecesi'nin yaşandığı olayları (İsr: Telling orally, in order, the events of the Night of the Mi‘raj (the Isra, the Mi‘raj, the gift of the five daily prayers).
plan.Hz. Ayşe'nin Kadir Gecesi'nde okunmasını: Repeating together as a class the prayer that Aisha learnt to recite on the Night of Destiny.
plan.Kadir Gecesi duası: \"Ya Rab, sen çok af: The prayer of the Night of Destiny: “O Lord, You are Most Forgiving and You love to forgive, so forgive me.” (The prayer that our Prophet (s.a.s.) taught in answer to Aisha’s question.)
plan.Öğrenci, lafza-i celâli önceki harekeye: The student reads the name of Allah (lafza-i jalala) heavy or light according to the preceding vowel.
plan.Lafza-i celâlin önceki harekeye göre kal: The reading of the name of Allah as heavy or light according to the preceding vowel is introduced with examples. The students repeat the word Allah after the teacher in different word connections.
plan.Öğrenci, müşriklerin işkenceleri yüzünde: The student says that, because of the polytheists’ torture, a group of Muslims migrated to Abyssinia together with the Prophet’s daughter Ruqayya. • The student compares the journey of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) to Ta’if in 620, his ill reception there, and how Muslims should behave in the face of such behaviour. • The student explains the miracle of the Isra (being taken from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque) and the Mi‘raj (being raised to the heavens) and that the five daily prayers were commanded on this journey. • The student tells about the First and Second Pledges of Aqaba and how they opened the way for the Hijra to Medina.
plan.Müşriklerin eziyeti artınca bir grup Müs: When the polytheists’ persecution increased, a group of Muslims migrated to Abyssinia together with the Prophet’s daughter Ruqayya. The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.), however, stayed in Mecca and, in 620, after the deaths of his uncle Abu Talib and his wife Khadija, went to Ta’if to look for support; but the people of Ta’if drove him away and stoned him. After these sad events, Almighty Allah honoured our Prophet with the miracle of the Isra and Mi‘raj: in one night he was raised from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque (the Isra) and from there to the heavens (the Mi‘raj); on this journey the five daily prayers were made obligatory. At the First Pledge of Aqaba in 621, made with six people from Yathrib (Medina), a promise not to do evil was taken; at the Second Pledge of Aqaba in 622, in which a large group promised to protect our Prophet, the Hijra of the Muslims to Medina was decided.
plan.Tâiflilerin davranışını ve \"Müslümanlar: Completing together on the screen the comparison of the behaviour of the people of Ta’if and “how Muslims behave”.
plan.İsrâ ve Mirac yolculuğunun güzergâhını (: Showing the route of the Isra and Mi‘raj journey (Mecca – Jerusalem – the heavens) on the map and telling it orally.
plan.Birinci ve İkinci Akabe Biatlarının fark: Comparing as a class the difference between the First and the Second Pledges of Aqaba.
plan.Öğrenci, İslâm'ın insanlararası ilişkile: The student lists the basic rules of good character that Islam recommends in relations between people (greeting, smiling, helping, patience). • The student recalls the verse of the Qur’an that commands treating one’s parents well (al-Isra 23) and explains its meaning in their own sentences. • The student tells right and wrong behaviour apart in everyday social situations (the family table, time with friends, receiving guests). • The student expresses the religious and moral importance of hosting guests and lists the behaviours to be followed with regard to a guest. • The student explains how virtues such as honesty, generosity and a cheerful face are grounded in the Qur’an and in the examples of the Prophet. • The student puts into practice the values learnt through classroom role-plays (sketches, dialogues, sharing memories).
plan.Bu ünite, İslâm ahlakının insanlararası: This unit aims to teach children, through living them, the principles of good behaviour that Islamic morality brings to relations between people. Virtues such as greeting, smiling, helping one another, patience and kind words are treated on the basis of the religion’s basic recommendations. Centring on the verse of the Holy Qur’an that commands good treatment of mother and father, it is stressed that approaching parents with respect and compassion is both a religious and a moral responsibility. Through stories and dialogues taken from daily life, concrete examples of good behaviour are shown to the children; in this way abstract concepts become something that can be lived.
plan.Bir tanıdıkla karşılaşıldığında ne yapıl: What do you do when you meet an acquaintance? Tell how one behaves with the people met in class and discuss it as a class. / With your classmate, make up short dialogues about good behaviour. / Tell about a moment when you did a kindness to someone in your family: what did you do, how did the other person respond? Share it with the class.
plan.Öğrenci, şemsî lâm ve kamerî lâm örnekle: The student tells apart examples of the sun letter lâm and the moon letter lâm within reading.
plan.Şemsî lâm ve kamerî lâm uygulaması el ta: The application of the sun lâm and the moon lâm is shown with words that carry the definite article. The students mark the examples where the lâm is pronounced and where it is not, and read from the Qur’an page.
plan.Öğrenci, kitaplara imanın imanın altı şa: The student says that faith in the books is the third of the six articles of faith. • Drawing on verses, the student names the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel and the Qur’an. • The student explains how the verses of the Qur’an were preserved both by being memorised and by being put in writing. • Starting from what David, Niko and Emina tell, the student matches the Tanakh, the Gospel and the Qur’an with those to whom they were sent down.
plan.13. ünite, imanın altı şartından üçüncüs: Unit 13 introduces children to faith in the books, the third of the six articles of faith. Drawing on verses, the names of the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the Qur’an, and the Qur’an’s name Furqan, are recalled. It is explained that the verses of the Qur’an were preserved, at a time when paper was still unknown on the Arabian Peninsula, both by being memorised by the Companions and by being written on various materials by the scribes of the revelation. Through what David, Niko and Emina tell, it is shown that the Tanakh was sent down to Moses, the Gospel to Jesus and the Qur’an to Muhammad (s.a.s.), and that each holy book is accepted by the followers of its own religion.
plan.Ayetleri okuyup kutsal kitapların isimle: We read the verses and list the names of the holy books on the board as a class.
plan.Vahiy kâtipliği görevi bize verilseydi y: We talk with our classmate about, and share, what we would pay attention to in order not to make mistakes if we were given the task of scribe of the revelation.
plan.Dört kümeye ayrılıp bir kutsal kitabı (': Dividing into four groups, we introduce one holy book to the class orally (through the questions ‘what is its name, to which prophet was it sent down, which religion’).
plan.Öğrenci, zekâtın İslam'ın beş şartından: The student explains that zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam and that a certain proportion of wealth that has reached the nisab amount must be given. • The student gives examples of verses and hadiths on charity and zakat and states the place of these acts of worship in the Qur’an and the Sunnah. • The student explains with examples that behaviours such as smiling, commanding what is good and showing the way are also counted as charity. • The student expresses in their own sentences that zakat is not a favour but a right of those in need. • Starting from the “Clothes on the Hanger” example, the student develops a proposal for mutual help that can be put into practice in class or in the mosque.
plan.Bu derste önce İslam'ın beş şartı ve iba: In this lesson, first the five pillars of Islam and the fact that acts of worship are done for Allah’s pleasure are recalled. Through verses from Surah al-Baqara and Surah at-Tawba, the importance of spending wealth in the way of Allah and of giving charity in secret is treated. It is explained that zakat is an obligatory act of worship by which a Muslim who has held more than a certain amount (the nisab) of money for a year must give two and a half per cent of it to those in need. Starting from a hadith of our Prophet (s.a.s.), it is exemplified that smiling, commanding what is good and forbidding what is evil, showing the way and removing a stone from the road are also each a charity. It is stressed that zakat is not a favour but a right of the poor. Finally, with the example of the “Clothes on the Hanger” project, it is explained that things that are not used can be shared with those in need.
plan.Peygamberimizin (s.a.s.) hadisinden hare: Starting from a hadith of our Prophet (s.a.s.), finding oral examples as a class to the question “which behaviours are counted as charity”.
plan.Allah rızası için yapılan küçük iyilikle: Filling in as a class on the board a chart that describes small kindnesses done for Allah’s pleasure (to whom, when, why).
plan.\"Askıda Giysi\" örneğinden esinlenerek: Sharing orally with the class an idea for mutual help that could be put into practice in the mosque or at school, inspired by the “Clothes on the Hanger” example.
plan.Öğrenci, vasl ve vakf işaretlerine göre: The student continues reading or stops according to the signs of continuing (wasl) and stopping (waqf).
plan.Vasl ve vakf kavramları kısa satır örnek: The concepts of wasl and waqf are taught through short line examples. The students follow with a finger the places to stop and to pass, and try correct stopping at the ends of verses.
plan.Öğrenci, müşriklerin Müslümanlara ve Hâş: The student tells about the three-year boycott that the polytheists imposed on the Muslims and the Banu Hashim, and the hardships during it, such as hunger and thirst. • The student explains that the boycott agreement was eaten by a moth and the boycott was therefore lifted, and that this was a sign of Allah’s power. • The student says that this year is called the “Year of Sorrow” because his uncle Abu Talib and his wife Khadija died in the same year. • The student explains with examples the increase of the polytheists’ persecution in the Year of Sorrow, Fatima’s compassion towards her father and our Prophet’s trust in Allah.
plan.Hz. Hamza ve Hz. Ömer'in Müslüman olması: The polytheists, frightened by Hamza’s and Umar’s becoming Muslims, took a decision of boycott that cut off all trade and relations with the Banu Hashim and the Muslims, and hung it on the Kaaba; during this three-year boycott the Muslims endured hunger and thirst, and in the end, when a moth ate the text of the agreement, some polytheists tore it up and lifted the boycott. Shortly after the end of the boycott, our Prophet’s uncle Abu Talib and his wife Khadija died one after the other; therefore that year was called the ‘Year of Sorrow’. After these losses the polytheists’ persecution increased even more; one day, as his daughter Fatima, weeping, was cleaning our Prophet, on whose head earth had been thrown, he expressed his trust in Allah by saying, ‘Do not cry, my daughter, Almighty Allah will protect your father.’ After these hard days, as we learnt in the previous lesson, our Prophet went to Ta’if to seek support.
plan.Boykotun üç yılında Müslümanların çektiğ: Sharing orally the hardships the Muslims suffered during the three years of the boycott and how they resisted them.
plan.\"Hüzün Yılı\" adının neden verildiğini: Noting on the board why the name “Year of Sorrow” was given: the two important losses (Abu Talib, Khadija).
plan.Hz. Fâtıma'nın babasına gösterdiği şefka: Discussing the question “How do we support our family on their hard day?” starting from Fatima’s compassion towards her father.
plan.Öğrenci, İslam dininin bireysel ve toplu: The student explains with at least three examples the contributions of the religion of Islam to individual and social life. • The student interprets the Prophet’s hadiths on the protection of nature and the environment and adapts them to their own life. • The student links environment-protecting behaviours such as saving water, planting trees and showing compassion to animals with Islamic values. • The student lists when and how Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha are celebrated and the acts of worship and traditions practised at these Eids. • The student recognises the importance of blessed nights such as the Night of Destiny and the Mi‘raj night and the acts of worship performed on these nights. • The student notices the beauties in nature created by Allah and expresses a feeling of gratitude.
plan.Bu ünite, İslam dininin günlük yaşam, ah: This unit introduces children, with concrete examples, to the transforming effect of the religion of Islam on daily life, morality and culture. Religion is treated as a guide that deeply shapes individual responsibilities, family ties, friendships and attitudes to the environment. In particular, the Prophet’s compassion towards nature and animals is conveyed to the students through hadiths; concrete forms of behaviour such as saving water, planting trees and treating living things with mercy are brought to the fore. In the unit, the religious festivals of Islam, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, and blessed days and nights such as the Night of Destiny and the Mi‘raj night are introduced.
plan.\"Dinimin alfabesi\" oyunu: Her harf içi: The game “The alphabet of my religion”: write a concept from religion for each letter (e.g. A = Adalah/justice, B = Forgiveness...). / Among the actions that can be done every day, mark and list those related to worship, solidarity and the environment. / Read the hadiths of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) on nature and the welfare of animals; find a suitable title and picture for each.
plan.Öğrenci, kelimeleri birleştirerek kısa c: The student reads short sentences as a whole by joining the words together.
plan.Öğrenciler daha önce çözdükleri kelimele: The students read the words they have worked out before within short Qur’anic sentences. The teacher has them follow with the eyes between the words and practises whole reading without going back to the syllable.
plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an ayetlerinin Hz. Peygambe: The student explains that the verses of the Qur’an were revealed to the Prophet (s.a.s.) piece by piece over 23 years. • The student lists the roles of Abu Bakr, Umar and Zayd ibn Thabit in the process of compiling the Qur’an into a mushaf. • The student briefly explains why and how the vowel signs were added to the text of the Qur’an. • The student defines the concept of ‘hafiz’ and expresses the importance of the huffaz in the preservation of the Qur’an.
plan.16. ünite, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in nasıl oluşt: Unit 16 tells children how the Holy Qur’an came into being. It is shown that the revelation, which came verse by verse and surah by surah to the Prophet (s.a.s.) over 23 years, was first memorised and then written down by the scribes of the revelation on materials such as hide, stone and papyrus. On a timeline, the first revelation at Hira, the compiling of the Qur’an into a mushaf under Zayd ibn Thabit in the time of Abu Bakr and its copying in the time of Uthman are listed in order. Abu al-Aswad’s adding of vowel signs to the text of the Qur’an and the concept of ‘hafiz’ are also treated in this unit; the lesson is supported by memorising the supplication of Moses in Surah Ta-Ha.
plan.Hz. Musa'nın duasını ('Rabbi'şrah lî sad: We memorise the supplication of Moses (‘Rabbi’shrah li sadri...’) with its meaning and teach it to the friend on our right.
plan.Zaman çizelgesindeki olayları inceleyip: We study the events on the timeline and match as a class which event took place in which range of dates.
plan.Nebe suresini açıp Arapça harfler dışınd: We open Surah an-Naba’, circle the signs other than the Arabic letters (vowel signs, pause marks, the juz’ rosette, etc.) and talk with our friends about what they are.
plan.Hz. Musa'nın duası (Tâhâ suresi 25-28. a: The supplication of Moses (Surah Ta-Ha, verses 25-28): ‘Rabbi’şrah lî sadrî ve yessir lî emrî vahlül ukdeten min lisânî yefkahû kavlî’ — ‘My Lord! Uplift my heart for me, and make my task easy, and remove the impediment from my tongue so people may understand my speech.’
plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in nasıl vahyedi: The student briefly recalls and tells how the Holy Qur’an was revealed and put into writing. • The student finds a given surah by using the index at the end of the Qur’an (the surah–page list). • The student uses the alphabetical subject index at the end of translations of the meaning to establish the surah and verse number of a verse on a subject. • The student explains what the way of showing surah and verse numbers (e.g. 3/61) means. • The student lists examples of topics in the Qur’an about good and bad behaviour.
plan.Bu derste önce Kur'an-ı Kerim'in Hz. Pey: In this lesson, first how the Holy Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet (s.a.s.) and how it was put into writing thanks to the scribes of the revelation is recalled. Through Ayşe’s story, how to find on which page a wanted surah (for example Ya-Sin) is, by using the index at the end of the Qur’an, is learnt. Through Ali’s story, how to use the alphabetical subject index found at the end of translations of the meaning, and what surah–verse numbers (for example 3/61) mean, are explained. How topics about bad behaviour such as lying, cheating and backbiting, and about good behaviour such as brotherhood, friendship and generosity, are looked up in the Qur’an is exemplified.
plan.Sınıfça belirlenen bir surenin fihristte: Holding a competition of finding the page of a surah chosen by the class in the index; each pupil names a surah and asks their friends to find its page.
plan.Alfabetik konu indeksinden bir konu (örn: Choosing a subject from the alphabetical subject index (e.g. mutual help, brotherhood) and finding orally the surah and verse number of at least one relevant verse.
plan.Sure numarası ile sayfa numarası arasınd: Working out together on the board, as a class, the relation between the surah number and the page number.
plan.Öğrenci, kısa Kur'an cümlelerini doğru s: The student reads short Qur’anic sentences in the right order and at the right tempo.
plan.Kısa ayet parçaları satır satır tahtaya: Short verse fragments are put on the board line by line. The students listen to the sentence from the teacher, then repeat it at the same tempo, in chorus and individually.
plan.Öğrenci, Birinci Akabe Biatı'nda (peygam: The student tells that at the First Pledge of Aqaba (the 12th year of prophethood) twelve people, led by As‘ad ibn Zurara, promised to keep away from evil, and that our Prophet sent Mus‘ab to Medina as a teacher. • The student says that at the Second Pledge of Aqaba (the 13th year) seventy-five people promised to protect our Prophet and twelve representatives were chosen. • The student explains that the Mi‘raj miracle took place one and a half years before the Hijra, on the 27th night of the month of Rajab, and that Abu Bakr at once confirmed this news and received the title “Siddiq” (the Truthful). • The student names the three gifts given to our Prophet at the Mi‘raj (the last two verses of Surah al-Baqara, the good news of Paradise for the ummah, the five daily prayers).
plan.Peygamberliğinin on birinci yılında hac: In the eleventh year of his prophethood, our Prophet met six people from Medina during the pilgrimage season; the next year he met a group of twelve at Aqaba; this group, led by As‘ad ibn Zurara, promised not to associate partners with Allah and to keep away from theft and adultery (the First Pledge of Aqaba), and Mus‘ab was sent to Medina as a teacher. A year later a group of seventy-five (two of them women) promised to protect our Prophet as they would their own families (the Second Pledge of Aqaba), and twelve representatives were chosen from among them; these pledges opened the way for the Hijra to Medina. A year and a half before the Hijra, on the 27th night of the month of Rajab, our Prophet was raised from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque (the Isra) and from there to the heavens (the Mi‘raj); the polytheists did not believe it, but Abu Bakr confirmed it at once and received the title ‘Siddiq’. At the Mi‘raj our Prophet was given as gifts the last two verses of Surah al-Baqara, the good news that the ummah would enter Paradise, and the five daily prayers.
plan.I. ve II. Akabe Biatlarını katılımcı say: Comparing on the board the First and Second Pledges of Aqaba in terms of the number of participants and the promises given.
plan.\"Sıddîk\" unvanının anlamını ve Hz. Ebû: Explaining orally the meaning of the title “Siddiq” and why it was given to Abu Bakr.
plan.Miraç'ın üç hediyesini ekrana yansıtıp s: Showing the three gifts of the Mi‘raj on the screen and repeating them in order.
plan.Öğrenci, bedenin Allah'ın bir emaneti ol: The student explains that the body is a trust (amana) from Allah and tells with an example how this understanding shapes the obligations regarding health and cleanliness. • The student tells apart the concepts of halal and haram in the context of food and drink and expresses the importance of keeping to this limit in daily life. • By assessing, through the story characters, the possible consequences of neglecting responsibilities of worship (especially the dawn prayer and the mosque lesson), the student determines their own attitude. • The student listens to or reads verse 72 of Surah al-Ahzab and explains that the concept of ‘trust’ covers a person’s abilities such as reason, strength and will. • The student notices that choosing what is right without outside pressure requires individual responsibility and gives concrete advice for it. • The student fills in a self-assessment table that evaluates their daily behaviour (prayer, reading the Qur’an, honesty, etc.) in line with the commands of Islam.
plan.Bu ünite, İslam'ın bireye yüklediği soru: This unit treats the responsibilities that Islam places on the individual by relating them to children’s daily life. Starting from the idea that the body is a trust from Allah, it is taught that taking care of health, cleanliness and the limit between halal and haram is a religious duty. The importance of keeping the heart clean, staying away from bad thoughts and earning an honest living by working is stressed. Through the story characters (Mustafa, a sick child; Songül, who goes to sleep late; and Betül, who wants to miss the mosque lesson), the students are guided to question their responsibilities of worship, their understanding of health and their choices of priorities.
plan.Bir hafta boyunca beden sağlığı, temizli: Preparing a self-assessment chart on which you will follow your bodily health, cleanliness and prayer habit for a week. / Dividing halal and haram food and drink into two columns and filling them in with examples. / Reading the paragraphs that explain the commands Islam places on the individual (bodily health, cleanliness of the heart, honest earnings, etc.) and writing the command in each one in the notebook.
plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an-ı Kerim satırını karıştı: The student follows a line of the Holy Qur’an without getting confused.
plan.Mushaf sayfasının satır düzeni, ayet işa: The line layout of a mushaf page, the verse markers and the spaces between words are introduced. The students follow the line with a finger and quickly find the place where the teacher stopped.
plan.Öğrenci, 'nebi' ve 'resul' kavramlarını: The student defines the concepts ‘nabi’ and ‘rasul’ and names the ‘ulu al-‘azm’ prophets. • The student draws the lesson of repentance and obedience to Allah from the story of Adam (peace be upon him). • The student explains with examples Noah’s (peace be upon him) patience in his story. • The student tells how Abraham (peace be upon him) refused to worship idols and how he was saved from the fire. • The student summarises Pharaoh’s oppression in the time Moses (peace be upon him) was born and what was done to the Children of Israel.
plan.19. ünite, peygamberlere imanı ve ilk dö: Unit 19 introduces children to faith in the prophets and to the stories of the first four prophets. First the concepts ‘nabi’, ‘rasul’ and ‘ulu al-‘azm’ are explained. In the story of Adam (peace be upon him), eating from the forbidden fruit, repentance and the title ‘safiyyullah’ (Allah’s chosen one) are told. In the story of Noah (peace be upon him), his patience in the face of his people’s denial and his rescue by the ship are treated. In the story of Abraham (peace be upon him), his breaking of the idols, his answer to Nimrod and his miraculous rescue from the fire are told. The unit ends with the cruel Pharaoh having the male children of the Children of Israel killed in the time Moses (peace be upon him) was born; in this lesson the story of Moses is still at its beginning.
plan.Hz. Âdem'in kıssasında geçen dinî kavram: We identify the religious concepts in the story of Adam (such as safiyyullah and repentance) and write them on the board.
plan.Hz. Nuh'un kıssasını okuyup nerelerde sa: We read the story of Noah and determine orally where he behaved patiently.
plan.Hz. İbrahim'in Nemrut'a verdiği cevabı (: We act out Abraham’s answer to Nimrod (‘Then you bring the sun from the west’) and discuss as a class why it was effective.
plan.Öğrenci, hac ibadetinin mal ve bedenle b: The student states that the hajj is an act of worship done with both wealth and body and that the place one goes to is the Kaaba in Mecca. • The student tells of the building of the Kaaba by linking it with the story of Abraham, Hagar and Ishmael. • The student briefly explains the coming forth of the water of Zamzam and the running between Safa and Marwa. • The student defines the concepts of miqat and ihram and explains that the ihram symbolises equality among people. • The student lists the spiritual preparations a person setting out for the hajj should make (settling accounts and asking forgiveness of others, repentance).
plan.Bu derste önce mal ile yapılan ibadetler: In this lesson, first the acts of worship done with wealth (charity, zakat) and the hajj, an act of worship done with both wealth and body, are recalled. It is told how Abraham left his wife Hagar and his son Ishmael in Mecca, how Hagar ran between Safa and Marwa to find water and how the water of Zamzam came forth during this; and it is treated how Abraham and Ishmael built the Kaaba, the first house of worship, beside this water. With verses from Surah Al Imran and Surah al-Hajj it is stressed that the Kaaba is the first house of worship established for people. It is explained that the hajj is a journey full of symbols from beginning to end, and that a person setting out for the hajj must first pay what is owed to others, settle accounts and repent. Finally the concepts of miqat (the boundary where the hajj begins) and ihram (the dress that shows the equality of all people) are introduced.
plan.Mekke şehrini ve Kâbe'nin yerini sınıfça: Finding the city of Mecca and the position of the Kaaba on the map as a class.
plan.Hz. Hacer'in hikâyesini dinledikten sonr: After listening to the story of Hagar, discussing orally which behaviour pilgrims today repeat as an act of worship.
plan.Mikat ve ihram kavramlarını kendi cümlel: Defining the concepts of miqat and ihram in their own sentences on the board.
plan.Öğrenci, Amme cüzünden kısa satırları yü: The student reads short lines from the last juz’ of the Qur’an from the page.
plan.Amme cüzünün son sayfalarından seçilen k: Short lines chosen from the last pages of the last juz’ are read from the page. The teacher first drills them, and the students, listening in pairs, note the mistakes and read again.
plan.Öğrenci, günlük hayattaki farklı göç seb: The student recognises the different reasons for migration in daily life (war, natural disaster, work, hunger, education) with examples and compares them with the Muslims’ Hijra from Mecca to Medina. • The student tells that after the Second Pledge of Aqaba the Muslims began to migrate secretly to Yathrib, while Umar migrated openly and defiantly. • The student names those who remained in Mecca: our Prophet, Abu Bakr and Ali. • With verse 30 of Surah al-Anfal, the student explains that the Meccans, at the proposal of Abu Jahl, made a plan to kill the Prophet Muhammad but that Allah foiled this plan.
plan.Günümüzde de insanlar savaş, doğal afet,: Today too people migrate for reasons such as war, natural disaster, work, hunger or education; the Muslims’ Hijra from Mecca to Medina was a similar migration. After the Second Pledge of Aqaba the Muslims began to migrate secretly to Yathrib; only Umar set out openly, first circling the Kaaba and praying, defying the Meccans. Left behind were our Prophet, Abu Bakr and his family, Ali, who was still a child, and his mother, and a few people who were not able to migrate. Fearing the Muslims’ growing strength, the Meccans gathered on 9 September 622; at the proposal of Abu Jahl they decided to choose one man from each tribe and kill the Prophet Muhammad. The Holy Qur’an tells this event in verse 30 of Surah al-Anfal, declaring that the disbelievers were making plans but that Allah makes the best of plans.
plan.Beş kişinin (Ahmed, Narisara, Filiz, Rif: Matching orally the reasons for migration of five people (Ahmed, Narisara, Filiz, Rifat, İsmail) with the headings war/natural disaster/work/hunger/education.
plan.Hz. Ömer'in hicret şeklini diğer Müslüma: Comparing the way Umar migrated with that of the other Muslims and discussing the question “why did he behave differently?”
plan.Enfâl sûresi 30. ayetin anlamını (\"Alla: Explaining in their own sentences the meaning of verse 30 of Surah al-Anfal (“Allah too was making plans”).
plan.Öğrenci, Güneş takvimi ile Ay takvimi (H: The student explains the basic differences between the solar calendar and the lunar calendar (the Hijri calendar). • The student lists the twelve months of the Hijri calendar in the correct order and states that this calendar began with the event of the Hijra. • The student recognises the blessed days and nights in Islam (the blessed nights, the Night of Destiny, the Eids) and states in which months of the calendar they fall. • The student tells apart the religious and social meaning of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha and explains the distinctive features of each. • The student briefly tells the story of Abraham’s sacrifice and links it with Eid al-Adha. • The student expresses with examples the importance of showing respect for the festivals of other faith traditions (Christmas, Easter, Passover).
plan.İnsanlar tarih boyunca zamanı düzenlemek: Throughout history people have used calendars to organise time. This unit, treating the basic differences between the solar and lunar calendars, introduces Islam’s own calendar system, the Hijri calendar. The Hijri calendar begins with the Hijra of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) from Mecca to Medina in 622, and because it is based on the movements of the Moon it is about eleven days shorter per year than the solar calendar. The twelve months of the Hijri year (from Muharram to Dhu al-Hijja) are introduced in order, and blessed days such as Ashura, the Mawlid night, the Raghaib night, the Mi‘raj night, the Bara’a night and the Night of Destiny, and the Eids of Ramadan and Sacrifice, are introduced within this calendar framework.
plan.Bilinen dini bayramları, kandilleri ve ö: Making a calendar section showing the religious festivals, blessed nights and important nights that are known. / Sharing in class the memories and experiences about the festivals placed on the concept map. / Researching the different calendars in use today, bringing them to class and comparing them.
plan.Öğrenci, kısa sure satırlarını yüzünden: The student pronounces short surah lines from the page in line with the rules of reading.
plan.Kısa surelerden seçilen satırlar ezber a: Lines chosen from short surahs are used for reading from the page without the aim of memorisation. The students read in turn, paying attention to letters, vowels and pauses.
plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Musa'nın (a.s.) kıssasını K: The student completes the story of Moses (peace be upon him) with the miracle of the parting of the Red Sea. • The student tells the story of Jesus (peace be upon him) with Mary, the miracle of speaking in the cradle and his being raised to heaven. • The student names the five common attributes of the prophets (sidq, amana, tabligh, fatana, isma) with their definitions. • The student gives at least three examples of the miracles given to different prophets. • The student explains with an example that miracles differ according to the needs of societies.
plan.19. ünitenin bu bölümü, önceki derste ba: This part of Unit 19 completes the story of Moses (peace be upon him), begun in the previous lesson, with the miracle of the parting of the Red Sea. Then the story of Jesus (peace be upon him) is told: the good news given to Mary, Jesus’ defending his mother by speaking in the cradle, his healing of the sick and his being raised to heaven by Allah are treated. The unit introduces the five common attributes found in all the prophets (sidq, amana, tabligh, fatana, isma) and presents a list of the miracles given to the prophets from Adam to Muhammad (s.a.s.); it is stressed that different miracles were given according to the needs of each society.
plan.Peygamber kıssalarından çıkarılan öğütle: We match orally the lessons drawn from the stories of the prophets (such as patience, repentance, gratitude) with the relevant prophet.
plan.Peygamberlerin sıfatlarını inceleyip önc: We study the attributes of the prophets and explain with an example which attribute stands out in the stories treated in the previous lesson.
plan.Peygamberlerin mucizelerinden hangisinin: We share with the class, giving reasons, which of the prophets’ miracles we would want to have ourselves.
plan.Öğrenci, telbiye duasının anlamını açıkl: The student explains the meaning of the talbiyah prayer and states when it is said throughout the hajj. • The student tells the order and the symbolic meaning of the tawaf, the sa‘y, the standing at Arafat, the standing at Muzdalifa and the stoning of the devil within the hajj. • The student briefly explains the place of the Black Stone and the Station of Abraham in the act of hajj. • The student expresses how the tawaf of visit and leaving the ihram (cutting the hair) mark the end of the hajj. • The student explains with an example on which story or event the symbols in the hajj are based (Hagar’s running, the struggle against the devil).
plan.Bu derste hac ibadetinin sembolleri sıra: In this lesson the symbols of the hajj are treated in order. The meaning of the talbiyah prayer and the fact that it is repeated continually throughout the hajj are told. The tawaf, done by circling the Kaaba, the story of the Black Stone and the Station of Abraham, and the act of worship of the sa‘y, based on Hagar’s running between Safa and Marwa while looking for water, are treated. The standing at Arafat, where pilgrims who have come from all over the world gather and pray, the second standing at Muzdalifa and the stoning of the devil at Mina, which symbolises the struggle against the devil, are told. Finally the tawaf of visit, which announces the end of the hajj, and leaving the ihram by shaving the hair are treated.
plan.Telbiye duasının anlamını sınıfça birlik: Reading the meaning of the talbiyah prayer together as a class and interpreting it in their own sentences.
plan.Hac ibadetinin sırasını (ihram, tavaf, s: Putting the order of the hajj (ihram, tawaf, sa‘y, Arafat, Muzdalifa, stoning the devil, tawaf of visit) in order orally as a class.
plan.Şeytan taşlama ve sa'y ibadetlerinin han: Discussing with the class on which event the stoning of the devil and the sa‘y are based and briefly noting it in the notebooks.
plan.Telbiye: \"Lebbeyk Allahümme lebbeyk! Le: The talbiyah: “Lebbeyk Allahümme lebbeyk! Lebbeyke lâ şerîke leke lebbeyk! İnne’l-hamde ve’n-ni‘mete leke ve’l-mülk, lâ şerîke lek!” (Meaning: Here I am at Your service, O Allah, here I am! At Your command, here I am!... You have no partner.)
plan.Öğrenci, kısa Kur'an satırlarını hecelem: The student comes close to fluent reading of short Qur’anic lines without spelling them out.
plan.Öğrenciler bildikleri işaretleri içeren: The students read lines containing the signs they know at a slow, a medium and a fluent tempo. The teacher points out unnecessary pauses and gives each student a short goal.
