plan.Öğrenci, Hz. Muhammed (s.a.s.) ile Hz. E: The student tells of the plan of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) and Abu Bakr to hide in the cave on Mount Thawr, and of Ali’s helping him by staying in our Prophet’s bed. • The student explains how the spider’s web at the cave entrance misled the Meccans and how the Prophet Muhammad calmed Abu Bakr with verse 40 of Surah at-Tawba. • The student tells how the journey of the Hijra ended with the arrival at Quba and Medina, and how the name Yathrib turned into Medina. • The student names the importance of the Hijra, such as brotherhood among the Muslims, the spread of Islam and the beginning of the Hijri calendar.
plan.Ebû Cehil'in öldürme planından haberdar: The Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.), who had learnt of Abu Jahl’s plan to kill him, planned to hide in a cave on Mount Thawr with Abu Bakr; he handed over the things entrusted to him to Ali, and Ali stayed in our Prophet’s bed that night and misled the Meccans. The two travelling companions, who set out on 10 September 622, were protected from the Meccans searching for them thanks to a spider’s web woven across the cave entrance; when Abu Bakr became anxious, the Prophet Muhammad calmed him with the verse ‘Do not grieve; surely Allah is with us’ (at-Tawba, 40). Three days later they set out, had a mosque built at Quba, and on 24 September 622 reached Yathrib; after this date the city took the name Medina. The Hijra strengthened brotherhood and mutual help among the Muslims, hastened the spread of Islam and became the beginning of the Hijri calendar.
plan.Hicret yolculuğunun adımlarını (plan, Se: Putting the steps of the journey of the Hijra (the plan, the cave of Thawr, the spider’s web, Quba, Medina) in order on the timeline on the screen.
plan.\"Hicret olmasaydı neler olurdu?\" sorus: Speculating as a class on the question “What would have happened if there had been no Hijra?”
plan.Hicretin önemini anlatan beş maddeyi tah: Reading together on the board and illustrating the five points that describe the importance of the Hijra.
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'ın toplumsal ilişkilerdek: The student explains the basic principles of Islam in social relations (helpfulness, honesty, respect, tolerance). • The student defines the concept of ‘the rights of others’ (huquq al-‘ibad) and expresses the religious and moral consequences of acting unjustly. • The student gives examples of solutions that can be applied in situations of conflict and disagreement met in daily life. • The student conveys in their own words the hadiths of the Prophet (s.a.s.) on social relations. • The student regularly reviews their own social behaviour by the method of self-assessment and identifies the areas that need to be improved. • The student explains the place and importance in Islam of settling accounts and of asking others to forgive what is owed to them.
plan.Bu ünite, Müslümanların toplum içinde üs: This unit treats the duties and responsibilities that Muslims must take on in society around the basic values of Islam. Starting from the principle “The best of people is the one who benefits others most”, the importance of honesty, helpfulness, tolerance and good character in social life is stressed. Centring on the concept of the “rights of others”, it is explained that harming another person’s property, honour or rights brings a great responsibility in Islam, and it is recalled that this responsibility is not limited to life in this world but is carried into the hereafter. The importance of behaving with patience and tolerance in situations of social conflict, of apologising and of settling accounts is stressed.
plan.Hz. Peygamber'in (s.a.s.) tavsiyelerini: The hadith containing the advice of the Prophet (s.a.s.) is read, and thoughts and experiences about this advice are shared in class. / A short text is written and read in class about how to react to unfair attitudes towards friends. / Starting from what has been learnt, a piece of work is prepared on reflecting good behaviour to friends.
plan.Öğrenci, kısa ayet parçalarını nefesini: The student reads short verse fragments by planning their breath.
plan.Uzun cümlelerde nefesin yetmediği yerler: The places where the breath is not enough in long sentences are shown with example lines. The students scan the part they will read with their eyes in advance, and then try to read without breaking the breath.
plan.Öğrenci, mushaf, sure, ayet, cüz, hizb,: The student names the concepts mushaf, surah, verse, juz’, hizb, basmala and pause mark with their definitions. • The student states that the Qur’an consists of 114 surahs, 30 juz’ and 6,236 verses. • The student explains the distinction between Meccan and Medinan surahs by historical period. • The student says what a verse of prostration is and what is done when it is recited.
plan.22. ünite, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in kitap olara: Unit 22 introduces children to the structure of the Holy Qur’an as a book. Concepts such as mushaf, surah, verse, juz’, hizb, basmala and pause mark are shown on a diagram of a Qur’an page. It is told that the Qur’an consists of 114 surahs, 30 juz’ and 6,236 verses; that the surahs revealed before the Hijra are called Meccan and those revealed afterwards Medinan; and that all the surahs except Surah at-Tawba begin with the basmala. The unit ends by recalling that there are fourteen verses of prostration at which a prostration is made when they are recited.
plan.Kur'an sayfası şeması üzerinde sure adı,: On the diagram of a Qur’an page, we try to find with our classmate concepts such as the surah name, the verse, the pause mark and the juz’ rosette.
plan.Mushaftan bir sayfa açıp ayetler dışında: We open a page of the mushaf, circle every sign we see apart from the verses as a class, and talk about what they mean.
plan.Öğrenci, abdestin farzlarını, sünnetleri: The student lists the obligatory and recommended acts of ablution and the things that invalidate it according to the Children’s Guide to Practice (Çocuk İlmihali). • The student tells apart the obligatory acts of tayammum and of the full washing (ghusl). • The student lists the conditions of the prayer (before and within the prayer), its pillars, its wajib acts and its sunnahs. • The student performs, in practice and in the right order, the sunnah and fard of the dawn prayer and the first sunnah, the fard and the final sunnah of the noon prayer. • The student explains the main things that invalidate the prayer with examples.
plan.Bu derste Çocuk İlmihali bölümünden abde: In this lesson, from the Children’s Guide to Practice, the obligatory acts, the sunnahs and the disliked acts of ablution and the things that invalidate it, and the obligatory acts and sunnahs of tayammum and of the full washing (ghusl), are recalled. Then the twelve conditions of the prayer (the conditions outside and inside the prayer), its wajib acts, its sunnahs, its disliked acts and the behaviours that invalidate it are listed. On this basis, the two rak‘as of sunnah and the two rak‘as of fard of the dawn prayer are performed in class in practice, with every movement from the intention to the greeting and the prayers and glorifications recited in every movement. In the same way, the four rak‘as of the first sunnah, the four rak‘as of fard and the two rak‘as of the final sunnah of the noon prayer are practised step by step.
plan.Abdestin farzlarını ve namazı bozan duru: Listing orally as a class the obligatory acts of ablution and the things that invalidate the prayer and writing them point by point on the board.
plan.Sabah namazının sünnet ve farzını sınıft: Performing the sunnah and fard of the dawn prayer in class in practice, step by step; repeating aloud the prayer recited in every movement.
plan.Öğle namazının ilk sünnet, farz ve son s: Telling orally as a class the order of the first sunnah, the fard and the final sunnah of the noon prayer.
plan.Öğrenci, seviyesine uygun Kur'an satırın: The student reads a line of the Qur’an suited to their level under the teacher’s supervision.
plan.Her öğrenci Amme cüzünden kısa bir satır: Each student reads a short line from the last juz’ of the Qur’an from the page to the teacher. Short observation notes are kept under the headings of letter, vowel, prolongation, pause and tempo.
plan.Öğrenci, hicret esnasında Süraka'nın Pey: The student tells of the miracle during the Hijra when Suraqa’s horse sank as he was trying to catch our Prophet, and that he finally became a Muslim. • The student says that our Prophet led the first Friday prayer on the way to Medina and that in Medina he was a guest in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari. • The student explains the building of the Prophet’s Mosque (Masjid an-Nabawi) and that our Prophet himself worked on this construction. • The student defines the concepts “Muhajir” and “Ansar” and tells that our Prophet made them brothers. • The student says that the People of the Suffa (Ashab as-Suffa) were the first school in Islam and that the poor students lodging there learnt knowledge.
plan.Hicret yolunda Peygamberimizi yakalamaya: Suraqa, who was trying to catch our Prophet on the way of the Hijra, had his horse sink into the sand twice; frightened and full of regret, Suraqa asked for forgiveness and later became a Muslim. Our Prophet stayed more than ten days at Quba, had the first mosque (the Quba Mosque) built and led the first Friday prayer on the way to Medina. The people of Medina welcomed him with joy; our Prophet stayed seven months as a guest in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and then on a plot of land he had bought nearby he had the Prophet’s Mosque built, himself carrying mud bricks. The Muslims who migrated from Mecca were called ‘Muhajirun’ and the people of Medina who helped them ‘Ansar’; our Prophet bound each Muhajir to an Ansari in a brotherhood stronger than blood brotherhood. The poor and homeless People of the Suffa, who lodged on the Suffa in one corner of the Prophet’s Mosque, learnt knowledge from our Prophet in the first school of Islam; great scholars such as Abu Hurayra were raised there.
plan.Süraka'nın hicret sırasında yaşadıkların: Telling orally what Suraqa went through during the Hijra and that he finally became a Muslim.
plan.\"Muhacir\" ve \"Ensar\" kelimelerini ta: Defining the words “Muhajir” and “Ansar” on the board and matching them with examples of brotherhood.
plan.Ashâb-ı Suffâ'yı \"İslam'ın ilk okulu\": Introducing the People of the Suffa as “the first school of Islam” and briefly comparing it with today’s school.
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'ın eğitim ve öğrenmeye ve: The student explains the importance Islam gives to education and learning by linking it with the verse ‘Read!’, the first command of the Qur’an. • The student interprets in their own sentences at least two of the Prophet’s hadiths on work and halal earnings. • The student defines the concepts of hard work, productivity and laziness and tells the difference between them with concrete examples. • The student explains that doing good to people and animals is among the behaviours that win Allah’s love. • The student expresses the social importance of solidarity and mutual help with examples from daily life. • The student explains with examples from practice that a good Muslim should try to be useful both to themselves and to those around them.
plan.İslam'ın ilk emri olan \"Oku!\" ayeti, b: The verse “Read!”, the first command of Islam, forms the basic framework of this unit; reading, writing and learning are treated as a religious duty. The unit stresses that working and producing are not merely a worldly necessity but also a way of drawing near to Allah. Through the hadiths of the Prophet, the importance of halal earnings and the virtue of showing mercy to people and animals are treated. Through historical examples such as the Grand Bazaar in Istanbul, the contribution of Islamic civilisation to a culture of work is made concrete. The value of hard work is illustrated by observing the behaviour of hard-working animals such as bees.
plan.Okuma ve yazma bilmeseydin hangi işleri: Marking in a list which jobs you could do and which you could not if you did not know how to read and write, and discussing it in class. / An assessment question on the blessings Allah has given and the responsibilities these blessings bring. / Thinking about and sharing what would be striking if one went to the Grand Bazaar in Istanbul.
plan.Öğrenci, temel med çeşitlerini örnek üze: The student recognises the basic kinds of prolongation on an example and reads with the right lengthening.
plan.Medd-i tabiî, medd-i muttasıl ve medd-i: The natural prolongation (madd tabi‘i), the connected prolongation (madd muttasil) and the separated prolongation (madd munfasil) are introduced at a child’s level with coloured marks. The students find an example for each kind of prolongation and apply the amount of lengthening with the teacher’s hand signs.
plan.Öğrenci, ahiret hayatının aşamalarını (ö: The student says in the correct order the stages of the life of the hereafter (death, the grave, the Day of Resurrection, rising again, the reckoning, the scale, Paradise/Hell). • Drawing on verses, the student explains that everyone will be called to account for what they did in this world. • Starting from Selim’s story, the student lists a Muslim’s duties towards a relative who has died (the prompting of the shahadah, washing, shrouding, the funeral prayer, burial). • The student expresses with examples the behaviours of a person who believes in the hereafter, such as commanding what is good and keeping away from evil.
plan.25. ünite, imanın altı şartından biri ol: Unit 25 introduces children to faith in the Last Day, one of the six articles of faith. The stages of birth, life, death, the grave, the Day of Resurrection, rising again, the reckoning, the scale and Paradise/Hell are listed; with verses it is stressed that everyone will be called to account for what they did in this world and that Allah’s justice is absolute. Through the death of Selim’s grandfather, a Muslim’s duties towards a relative who has died, such as the prompting of the shahadah, washing, shrouding, the funeral prayer and burial, are told. The unit also shows with examples the behaviours of those who believe in the hereafter, such as commanding what is good and avoiding evil.
plan.Doğum, yaşam, ölüm, kabir, kıyamet, diri: We list orally as a class a diagram containing the stages of birth, life, death, the grave, the Day of Resurrection, rising again, the reckoning, the scale and Paradise/Hell.
plan.Verilen ayetlerin hangi ahiret hâline (ö: We match as a class which state of the hereafter (death, the reckoning, the scale, Paradise, Hell) the given verses point to.
plan.'Hiç kimse ve hiçbir canlı ölmeseydi ne: We discuss as a class the question ‘What would happen if no one and no living thing died?’
plan.Öğrenci, ikindi, akşam ve yatsı namazlar: The student performs in practice, in the right order, the sunnah, fard and final sunnah rak‘as of the afternoon, sunset and night prayers. • The student explains the place of the qunut takbir and the qunut supplication recited in the third rak‘a of the witr prayer. • The student tells apart, with examples, the kinds of fasting (fard, wajib, sunnah, mustahab, makruh) and the things that do and do not invalidate the fast. • The student lists the characteristics of a person who is to give zakat and the categories to whom zakat is given, according to the Children’s Guide to Practice. • The student lists the conditions that make the hajj obligatory, and its obligatory acts, wajib acts and sunnahs.
plan.Bu derste Çocuk İlmihali'nden ikindi, ak: In this lesson, from the Children’s Guide to Practice, the way the sunnah, fard and final sunnah of the afternoon, sunset and night prayers are performed, and the qunut takbir and supplication recited in the three-rak‘a witr prayer performed after the night prayer, are treated in practice. Then, in the section on fasting, the kinds of fasting (fard, wajib, sunnah, mustahab and makruh) and the things that do and do not invalidate the fast are listed with examples. In the section on zakat, the conditions a person who gives zakat must meet and the eight categories to whom zakat is given (the poor, the needy, debtors, travellers, etc.) are recalled. Finally, in the section on the hajj, the conditions that make the hajj obligatory, the obligatory acts of the hajj (ihram, the standing at Arafat, tawaf), its wajib acts (sa‘y, the standing at Muzdalifa, stoning the devil, shaving the hair) and its sunnahs are listed.
plan.İkindi, akşam ve yatsı namazlarının sünn: Repeating orally as a class the order of sunnah-fard-final sunnah of the afternoon, sunset and night prayers and, if possible, performing them in practice.
plan.Oruç çeşitlerini ve orucu bozan/bozmayan: Classifying as a class, in a two-column list on the board, the kinds of fasting and the things that do and do not invalidate the fast.
plan.Zekâtın verildiği sekiz sınıfı ve haccın: Holding a competition of naming orally, in order, the eight categories to whom zakat is given and the obligatory acts of the hajj.
plan.Öğrenci, ihfâ örneklerini geniz sesini k: The student reads examples of ikhfa keeping the nasal sound.
plan.Sâkin nûn ve tenvinden sonra ihfâ harfle: It is shown that when the ikhfa letters come after a silent nun or tanwin, the sound is read hidden. The students practise the nasal sound and repeat short examples after the teacher.
plan.Öğrenci, hicret öncesinde Medine'de yaşa: The student recognises the main tribes that lived in Medina before the Hijra (Aws, Khazraj, Banu Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Qurayza) and their different religions and ways of life. • The student explains that before the Hijra there was no central government in Medina, and that after the Hijra order was established through brotherhood among the Muslims and a common agreement. • The student tells how the people of Medina welcomed our Prophet with joy with the hymn “Tala‘a al-badru ‘alayna”. • The student explains how the Prophet’s Mosque was built at the place where his camel knelt, and that the mosque was used not only for worship but also as a centre of education and gathering.
plan.Hicret öncesi Medine'de Evs, Hazrec, Ben: Before the Hijra, tribes such as the Aws, Khazraj, Banu Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Qurayza in Medina lived in their own neighbourhoods by their own rules; the Aws and Khazraj worshipped the idol Manat, while the three Jewish tribes kept their own religion; there was no central government. After the Hijra, brotherhood was first proclaimed among the Muslims, and then common rules were laid down through an agreement made with all the people of Medina. The people of Medina welcomed the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) and Abu Bakr with joy with the hymn ‘Tala‘a al-badru ‘alayna’ (The full moon has risen over us). Our Prophet, whom everyone invited to their home, bought the empty plot where his camel knelt freely and had the Prophet’s Mosque built there; this mosque, made of mud brick and palm trunks, was used not only for worship but also as a centre of consultation, education and hospitality; on the Suffa in one corner of it, young people learnt knowledge.
plan.\"Talea'l-bedru aleynâ\" ilahisini sınıf: Reading the hymn “Tala‘a al-badru ‘alayna” together as a class and finding the comparisons made to our Prophet (the sun, the moon, light).
plan.Medine'nin kabilelerini ve dinlerini ekr: Matching in a table on the screen the tribes of Medina and their religions.
plan.Mescid-i Nebevî'nin niçin sadece ibadet: Discussing as a class why the Prophet’s Mosque was designed not only as a place of worship but as a centre.
plan.Öğrenci, 'Selamün Aleyküm' ifadesinin an: The student explains the meaning of the expression ‘Salamun alaykum’ and its importance in Islam. • The student lists verbal and non-verbal forms of greeting (handshake, hug, kissing the hand, smile) and tells the differences between them. • Giving verse 13 of Surah al-Hujurat as an example, the student explains that Islam embraces the principles of equality, brotherhood and respect among people. • The student gets to know the world of thought of Yunus Emre and expresses in their own sentences the place of love and tolerance in Islamic morality. • The student explains the harm that negative behaviours such as jealousy, backbiting and slander do to the individual and society and lists, with examples, ways of coping with these feelings. • The student briefly summarises the guiding function that the Qur’an offers humanity.
plan.Bu ünite, İslam'ın özünde sevgi, barış v: This unit deals with the fact that love, peace and tolerance lie at the heart of Islam. Greeting is introduced as the basic etiquette of meeting in Islam; it is explained that the expression “Salamun alaykum” is not only a verbal welcome but also carries a deep meaning of wishes for peace and safety. It is stressed that forms of greeting differ from culture to culture and must be treated together with their non-verbal dimensions such as handshakes, hugs, kissing the hand and smiling. It is told that the Prophet encouraged giving the greeting and that the greeting strengthens the bond of love among Muslims.
plan.Sözlü selamlamadan farklı selamlama biçi: Research and compile forms of greeting other than the verbal greeting (handshake, hug, kissing the hand, etc.) and share them in class. / Look at different greeting expressions (goodbye, salam, high five, hello, alaykum salam, ‘I entrust you to Allah’, etc.); compare which ones are used and what they mean. / Take the role of a person visiting a friend and giving a greeting and write a short play scene; use different forms of greeting in the scene.
plan.Öğrenci, izhâr örneklerinde nûn sesini a: The student pronounces the nun sound clearly in examples of izhar.
plan.Sâkin nûn ve tenvinden sonra izhâr harfl: It is explained that when the izhar letters come after a silent nun and tanwin, the nun sound is read clearly. The students separate examples of ikhfa and izhar with cards and read the examples of izhar with a clear sound.
plan.Öğrenci, kader ve kaza kavramlarını Selm: The student defines the concepts of destiny (qadar) and divine decree (qada) in their own sentences, starting from the story of Mrs Selma. • The student explains with an example from the verses that destiny means ‘measure’ and that Allah created everything with a measure. • Starting from Ahmet’s exam story, the student notices that praying alone does not take the place of working. • The student expresses with an example the right meaning of trust in Allah (tawakkul) (working and leaving the result to Allah).
plan.31. ünite, İslam imanının altı esasından: Unit 31 introduces children, with concrete examples from life, to the belief in divine decree and destiny, one of the six foundations of the faith of Islam. Destiny is told as Allah’s knowing everything with His eternal knowledge and determining it according to a measure; divine decree (qada) is the taking place of this determination in life. Through the story of Mrs Selma, the relation of life events such as birth, death and provision to destiny is made concrete. With the story of Ahmet taking an exam without working and failing, it is shown that trust in Allah does not mean expecting a result without working. The unit ends with sayings about destiny from Turkish and world literature.
plan.Selma Hanım'ın hikâyesinde geçen kader,: We discuss as a class what the words destiny, divine decree, the appointed time of death, provision and trust in Allah, which appear in Mrs Selma’s story, mean.
plan.Ahmet'in davranışını inceleyip 'Sadece A: We examine Ahmet’s behaviour and talk with our classmate about the question ‘Is it enough only to pray to Allah?’
plan.Kaderle ilgili Türk ve dünya edebiyatınd: We assess as a class which of the sayings given from Turkish and world literature describes destiny best.
plan.Öğrenci, ibadetin Allah'a saygı gösterme: The student explains in their own sentences that worship means showing respect to Allah and giving thanks for His blessings. • The student gives one example each of worship done with the body, with wealth, and with both wealth and body. • The student states that the most valuable form of worship is worship done only for Allah’s pleasure, without expecting anything in return. • The student gives examples of at least two of the benefits worship brings to the soul and the body.
plan.Bu derste önce ibadetin, Allah'a saygı g: In this lesson it is first told that worship means showing respect to Allah and thanking Him for the countless blessings He has given, and that the purpose of human creation is to know Allah and worship Him. Acts of worship are treated in three groups: those done with the body such as the prayer and fasting, those done with wealth such as zakat and the sacrifice, and those done with both wealth and body such as the hajj. It is stressed that worship can be done with three different thoughts; the most valuable is worship done only for Allah without expecting a reward, worship done with the thought of Paradise and Hell is also valid, but worship done to show off is worthless. Finally the spiritual benefits of worship, which lifts the soul and protects from evil, and its bodily benefits, seen in the example of ablution and fasting, are told.
plan.Beden ile, mal ile ve hem mal hem beden: Placing orally, as a class, the acts of worship done with the body, with wealth, and with both wealth and body in a three-column table on the board.
plan.\"Neden ibadet ederiz?\" sorusuna sınıfç: Finding oral answers as a class to the question “Why do we worship?” and voting for the most beautiful answer.
plan.İbadetin bedene ve ruha sağladığı faydal: Noting in their notebooks in short points the benefits worship brings to the body and the soul.
plan.Öğrenci, iklâb kuralını dudak kapanışına: The student applies the rule of iqlab, paying attention to the closing of the lips.
plan.Sâkin nûn veya tenvinden sonra be harfi: It is shown that when the letter ba comes after a silent nun or tanwin, the sound turns into a mim sound. The students check the closing of the lips with a mirror and repeat the examples of iqlab slowly.
plan.Öğrenci, Mescid-i Nebevî'nin ibadetin ya: The student matches the functions of the Prophet’s Mosque, besides worship, such as meetings, help, education and hospitality, with today’s institutions. • The student tells that the first adhan was called by Bilal al-Habashi, inspired by Abdullah ibn Zayd’s dream. • The student defines the concepts “Muhajir” and “Ansar” and explains that our Prophet declared Meccan and Medinan families brothers so that they would overcome difficulties together. • The student says how the Charter of Medina, accepted in 623, made people of different tribes and religions live together with the principles of justice and freedom of religion.
plan.Mescid-i Nebevî tamamlanınca herkesi iba: When the Prophet’s Mosque was completed, our Prophet consulted his Companions about how to call everyone to worship; he liked the form of the call that Abdullah ibn Zayd had seen in a dream and taught it to Bilal al-Habashi, who had a beautiful voice; this is how the first adhan was called. The Muslims who migrated from Mecca were called ‘Muhajirun’ and the people of Medina who helped them ‘Ansar’; our Prophet declared the Muhajirun, who were in distress, and the Ansar brothers and had them share their earnings; in this way the needs of the Muhajirun were met and peace was established in Medina. Besides the Muslims, tribes such as the Aws and Khazraj and Jewish tribes such as Banu Qurayza, Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Nadir also lived in Medina; to establish an order that included everyone, the Charter of Medina was drawn up and accepted in 623, and with principles such as justice and freedom of religion the foundation of the Islamic state of Medina was laid.

plan.Bu ünitede İslam'ın güzelliğe ve estetiğ: In this unit the importance that Islam gives to beauty and aesthetics is treated. plan.Öğrenci, hadislerin dinin ikinci temel k: The student explains that hadiths are the second basic source of religion and consist of the sayings, actions and approvals of the Prophet (s.a.s.). • Starting from the example of Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him), the student says the order to be followed when looking for an answer to a religious question (the Qur’an, the Sunnah, personal reasoning (ijtihad)). • The student tells apart the concepts of sound (sahih), weak (da‘if) and fabricated (mawdu‘) hadith. • The student chooses at least three of the example hadiths given and explains their meaning in their own sentences.
plan.34. ünite, hadislerin İslam'daki yerini: Unit 34 tells children the place of the hadiths in Islam and the importance of learning them. Through the answer that Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) gave to the Prophet (s.a.s.) when he was being sent as governor to Yemen, the order of answering a religious question is taught: first with the Qur’an, if it is not found, with the Sunnah, and if again not found, with one’s own opinion. It is stated that the hadiths were collected and written down in the centuries after the Prophet’s death, and that during this time sound, weak and fabricated hadiths were distinguished. The unit ends with nine example hadiths on mercy, keeping away from jealousy and good character.

plan.Öğrenci, İslam'ın \"inandığını yaşamak\": The student names the meaning of Islam as “living what one believes” and its five pillars (the Shahadah, prayer, fasting, zakat, hajj). • The student explains the two conditions of being a responsible adult (mukallaf): being of sound mind and reaching the age of maturity. • The student classifies with examples the eight rulings of the acts of the responsible adult (fard, wajib, sunnah, mustahab, mubah, haram, makruh, mufsid). • The student states the difference between the emphasised (mu’akkad) and non-emphasised sunnah, and between the kinds of makruh, tahrimi and tanzihi.
plan.Bu derste önce İslam'ın \"inandığını yaş: In this lesson, first it is recalled that Islam means “living what one believes” and that its five pillars are reciting the Shahadah, performing the prayer, fasting, giving zakat and going on the hajj. Then the two conditions of being a responsible adult are told: being of sound mind and having reached the age of maturity (bulugh). The lesson introduces the eight rulings concerning the responsible adult (Af‘al al-Mukallafin): the fard, which is commanded definitively; the wajib, commanded by strong evidence; the sunnah, which our Prophet (s.a.s.) did (emphasised/non-emphasised); the mustahab, done sometimes; the mubah, which is permitted; the haram, which is definitively forbidden; the makruh, which is asked not to be done (tahrimi/tanzihi); and the mufsid, which invalidates an act of worship that has been begun. The difference of each ruling in terms of reward and responsibility is explained with examples.

plan.Öğrenci, müşriklerin Müslümanlara uygula: The student explains the aims of the boycott the polytheists imposed on the Muslims and its effects on the Muslims.
plan.Öğrenci, 'Hüzün Yılı' kavramını tanır ve: The student recognises the concept of the ‘Year of Sorrow’ and lists the important losses in this period (the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadija).
plan.Öğrenci, Taif yolculuğunun neden gerçekl: The student summarises why the journey to Ta’if took place and its result; the student explains with an example the Prophet’s patience in the face of the difficulties he met.
plan.Hz. Peygamber'in Mekke'deki son yılları,: The Prophet’s last years in Mecca passed under the shadow of the intensifying pressures on the Muslims. The polytheists, in order to stop the spread of Islam, took a decision of boycott aimed at isolating the Muslims socially and economically; with this decision trade, marriage and every kind of social relation were forbidden. After this long and hard period the boycott was finally lifted, but soon afterwards the Prophet was tried by two great sorrows: his uncle Abu Talib, who had supported him in every circumstance, and Khadija, the mother of the believers, died in the same year, and because of this deep grief that year came to be called the Year of Sorrow. In this lesson the boycott and the journey to Ta’if are treated.
plan.Öğrenci, güzel ahlaklı bir insanın temel: The student names, with examples, the basic characteristics of a person of good character (love, humility, helpfulness, avoiding sin). • Drawing on the verses and hadiths given, the student explains the place of doing good and of forgiving in Islamic morality. • The student interprets in their own sentences the commands about the rights of neighbours and relatives in verse 36 of Surah an-Nisa. • Starting from the story ‘The Easiest Charity’, the student explains with an example the importance of being careful about the rights of others. • The student compares and lists the behaviours that their religion asks of them and does not ask of them.
plan.Bu ünitede dinimizin bizden istediği güz: In this unit the characteristics of good character that our religion asks of us are treated. Characteristics of good character such as love, humility, helpfulness and avoiding sin are listed and supported with verses from Surah al-Baqara, al-Ma’ida, ash-Shura, al-A‘raf and Fussilat, and with the relevant hadiths. The commands on neighbourliness, kinship and mutual help in verse 36 of Surah an-Nisa are examined. In the story titled ‘The Easiest Charity’, the importance of being careful about the rights of others is discussed through the incident Hasan experiences in the supermarket. The unit has the behaviours that religion asks of us and does not ask of us listed in a comparative way.
plan.Ekranda gösterilen fotoğraflardaki iyi v: Explaining and discussing orally as a class the good and bad behaviours in the photographs shown on the screen.
plan.'Dinimin benden yapmamı istediği / istem: Filling in orally as a class the table ‘What my religion wants me to do / wants me not to do’ while the teacher writes it on the board.
plan.'En kolay sadaka' hikâyesinin nasıl bitm: Completing and discussing orally as a class how the story ‘The Easiest Charity’ should end.
plan.Öğrenci, Âmentü duasını bölümler hâlinde: The student recites the Amantu prayer in sections in the correct order.
plan.Âmentü duası iman esaslarıyla ilişkilend: The Amantu prayer is divided into short sections by linking it with the articles of faith. The students repeat each section after the teacher and make a first attempt at reading the whole at the end of the lesson.
plan.Öğrenci, din kavramını tanımlar ve dinle: The student defines the concept of religion and divides religions into three kinds: true religion, distorted religion and false religion. • The student divides the rulings of the religion of Islam into belief, practice and morality and briefly explains each. • The student expresses, with reasons, that Islam is the final and universal religion. • The student explains with examples at least three of the features that make Islam universal (a religion of reason and knowledge, a religion of ease, the absence of excess, a religion of peace and love).
plan.TDB'nin birinci ünitesi İslam dininin ne: The first unit of the TDB deals with what the religion of Islam is and its features. Religion is divided into true religion, distorted religion and false religion, and it is told that Islam is the final and uncorrupted true religion. The rulings of Islam are divided into belief, practice and morality. The unit lists the features that make Islam universal: being the final religion, valuing reason and knowledge, aiming at happiness both in this world and in the hereafter, being a religion of ease (with examples such as the traveller shortening the prayer), being free of excess and being a religion of peace and love. The topic is reinforced and simplified for the children with the poem ‘My Religion’.
plan.'Din neye denir?' sorusuna sınıfça cevap: We look for an answer as a class to the question ‘What is religion called?’ and form a shared definition.
plan.İslam'ın kolaylık dini olduğunu gösteren: We list orally the examples that show that Islam is a religion of ease (such as the traveller shortening the prayer, the sick being able to postpone fasting).
plan.'Benim Dinim' şiirini sınıfça birlikte o: We read the poem ‘My Religion’ together as a class and tell the messages in the poem in our own sentences.
plan.Öğrenci, İslam'ın temizliğe verdiği önem: The student grounds the importance Islam gives to cleanliness in verse and hadith. • The student classifies waters according to their purifying quality and tells apart those suitable for worship from those that are not. • The student lists the four obligatory acts of ablution and performs them in the correct order. • The student explains with examples the main sunnahs and etiquette of ablution. • The student states the conditions and the duration for wiping over leather socks (for a non-traveller/a traveller).
plan.Bu derste önce İslam dininin temizlik üz: In this lesson, first it is stressed with the hadith “Cleanliness is half of faith” that the religion of Islam is built on cleanliness. Waters are divided into two kinds, absolute and restricted, and into five kinds according to their purifying quality. After the spiritual and bodily benefits of ablution have been told with hadiths, the four obligatory acts of ablution (washing the face, washing the hands up to and including the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, washing/wiping the feet up to and including the ankles), its sunnahs and its etiquette are listed. Then how to perform ablution step by step is taught in the order of intention, putting water into the mouth and nose, washing the face and arms, wiping the head and ears, and washing the feet. Finally it is told that a person who wears leather socks can wipe over them when performing ablution without taking them off, the conditions necessary for this and the period of wiping (24 hours for a non-traveller, 72 hours for a traveller).
plan.Sınıfça sözlü olarak abdestin dört farzı: Naming orally, in order, the four obligatory acts of ablution as a class and writing them on the board.
plan.Abdestin alınış sırasını (niyet, ağız-bu: Acting out in place, with movements (dry), the order in which ablution is performed (intention, mouth-nose, face, arms, head-ears, feet).
plan.Mest üzerine meshetmenin şartlarını sını: Discussing as a class the conditions for wiping over leather socks and noting them in the notebooks in short points.
plan.Öğrenci, Sübhâneke duasını namazdaki yer: The student recites the Subhanaka prayer from memory, saying its place in the prayer.
plan.Sübhâneke duasının namazın başlangıcında: It is taught that the Subhanaka prayer is recited at the beginning of the prayer. The prayer is drilled word by word, and the students reinforce the memorisation with a repetition circle.
plan.Öğrenci, Bedir Savaşı'nın (624) sebebini: The student explains the cause of the Battle of Badr (624) and the first victory the Muslims won, despite being few in number, through patience and Allah’s help. • The student tells the consequences of the archers leaving their places in the Battle of Uhud (625) and the importance of obeying orders. • The student explains how the trench dug in the Battle of the Trench (627) on Salman al-Farisi’s suggestion protected Medina. • The student says with examples that our Prophet commanded good treatment of prisoners of war and cared about reducing loss of life in the defence of the city.
plan.Mekkeli müşrikler, Medine'ye göç eden Mü: When the Meccan polytheists seized the property of the Muslims who had migrated to Medina and incited the people of Medina, in 624 at Badr the Muslims, who were very few in number, won their first great victory through their patience and Allah’s help; our Prophet commanded that the prisoners be treated well. The Meccans, wanting to avenge the defeat, came to Uhud a year later; the archers’ failure to obey our Prophet’s order and their leaving their places led the Muslims to suffer heavy losses. When the polytheists came again in 627 with a great army of ten thousand, the Muslims, on the suggestion of the Persian Companion Salman al-Farisi, dug a trench of 5.5 km on the open side of Medina; the polytheists could not cross this obstacle and withdrew, and the Battle of the Trench ended with the Muslims winning without any losses. These three battles taught the Muslims the importance of patience, of obeying orders and of a clever defence.
plan.Bedir, Uhud ve Hendek savaşlarını tarih,: Putting the battles of Badr, Uhud and the Trench in order, with their dates, causes and results, on the timeline on the screen.
plan.\"Okçular neden yerlerini terk etti, bun: Discussing as a class the question “Why did the archers leave their places and what was the result?” and drawing out the importance of obeying orders.
plan.Hendek kazma fikrinin nereden geldiğini: Telling orally where the idea of digging a trench came from and how this clever solution won the war.
plan.Öğrenci, medeniyetin insanlığın ortak bi: The student explains that civilisation is the shared accumulation of humanity and gives an example of this. • The student recognises the historical importance of centres of learning such as the House of Wisdom (Bayt al-Hikma) founded in the Abbasid period. • The student lists the contributions of Ibn Sina, al-Biruni, Piri Reis and Ulugh Beg in the fields of medicine, mathematics, geography and astronomy. • Starting from verse 9 of Surah az-Zumar and the hadith ‘The scholars are the heirs of the prophets’, the student expresses the value Islam gives to knowledge. • The student notices that the inventions they use in daily life are the shared labour of humanity.
plan.Bu ünitede Müslümanların dünya medeniyet: In this unit the scientific contributions Muslims made to world civilisation are treated. It is stressed that civilisation is not the product of a single nation but the shared accumulation of all humanity; centres of learning such as the House of Wisdom founded in the Abbasid period are introduced. The pioneering work of Ibn Sina in medicine, al-Biruni in mathematics, Piri Reis in geography and Ulugh Beg in astronomy is told with examples. The value Islam gives to knowledge is reinforced with verse 9 of Surah az-Zumar and the hadith ‘The scholars are the heirs of the prophets’. The students notice that the inventions they use in daily life are the shared labour of humanity.
plan.Verilen buluşlar listesinden (saat, bilg: Choosing orally as a class, and giving reasons for, the five most important inventions from the given list of inventions (clock, computer, compass, farming tools, etc.).
plan.Ekrana yansıtılan görsellerle İbn Sina,: Choosing one of Ibn Sina, al-Biruni, Piri Reis and Ulugh Beg from the pictures shown on the screen and giving the class a short oral introduction.
plan.'Bu buluş olmasaydı hayatımız nasıl deği: Holding an oral brainstorm as a class with the question ‘How would our life have changed if this invention had not existed?’
plan.Öğrenci, Fâtiha suresini namazdaki yerin: The student recites Surah al-Fatiha from memory, knowing its place in the prayer.
plan.Fâtiha suresinin namazın her rekâtında o: It is explained that Surah al-Fatiha is recited in every rak‘a of the prayer. The students listen to the verses in short sections, repeat them and read them to the teacher in turn.
plan.Öğrenci, Kelime-i Tevhid ve Kelime-i Şeh: The student reads the Declaration of Oneness (kalimat at-tawhid) and the Shahadah (kalimat ash-shahadah) correctly and says their Turkish meaning. • The student explains the difference between faith in summary (ijmali) and faith in detail (tafsili) and names the six articles of faith. • The student compares the concepts of believer, hypocrite and disbeliever in terms of belief. • The student explains the relation between faith and worship with the ‘lamp and glass shade’ simile. • The student lists the three conditions for faith to be sound and accepted.
plan.TDB'nin ikinci ünitesi imanı ele alır. K: The second unit of the TDB deals with faith. The Declaration of Oneness and the Shahadah are introduced with their readings and meanings. Faith is divided into two: faith in summary (ijmali; believing in Allah and His Prophet as a whole) and faith in detail (tafsili; believing in each of the six articles of faith separately); the Amantu prayer sums up these six articles. People are classified in terms of belief as believers, hypocrites and disbelievers. The unit is completed by telling the peace that faith gives a person, the relation between faith and worship — through the simile of a lamp protected by a glass shade so that it does not go out — and the three conditions for faith to be sound; the TDB’s language, meant for adults, is simplified here for children.
plan.Kelime-i Tevhid, Kelime-i Şehadet ve Âme: We repeat the Declaration of Oneness, the Shahadah and the Amantu aloud as a class together with their meanings.
plan.Mümin, münafık ve kâfir kavramlarını örn: We match the concepts of believer, hypocrite and disbeliever with example behaviours and discuss them in class.
plan.İman ile ibadet arasındaki ilişkiyi anla: We tell the class the ‘lamp’ simile that explains the relation between faith and worship in our own sentences.
plan.Kelime-i Tevhid: 'Lâ ilâhe illallah, Muh: The Declaration of Oneness: ‘Lâ ilâhe illallah, Muhammedün Resûlüllah’ — There is no God but Allah and Muhammad (s.a.s.) is the Messenger of Allah.
plan.Kelime-i Şehadet: 'Eşhedü en lâ ilâhe il: The Shahadah: ‘Eşhedü en lâ ilâhe illallah ve eşhedü enne Muhammeden abdühû ve resûlüh’ — I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) is the slave and the Messenger of Allah.
plan.Âmentü: 'Âmentü billâhi ve melâiketihî v: The Amantu: ‘Âmentü billâhi ve melâiketihî ve kütübihî ve rusülihî ve’l-yevmi’l-âhiri ve bi’l-kaderi hayrihî ve şerrihî minallahi teâlâ ve’l-ba‘sü ba‘de’l-mevti hakk. Eşhedü en lâ ilâhe illallah ve eşhedü enne Muhammeden abdühû ve resûlüh’ — the prayer that expresses that we believe in the six articles of faith and that rising again after death is true.
plan.Öğrenci, yara veya kırık üzerindeki sarg: The student explains how to wipe over a bandage on a wound or a fracture. • The student names the states that require the full washing (ghusl) (ritual impurity after sexual relations, the end of menstruation, the end of postnatal bleeding) and lists the three obligatory acts of ghusl. • The student explains what it means to have an excuse (‘udhr) and when the ablution of a person with an excuse is invalidated. • The student tells apart women’s special states (menstruation, postnatal bleeding, istihada) and names the acts of worship that cannot be performed in these states. • The student determines in which situations tayammum is to be performed and performs its two obligatory acts in order.
plan.Bu derste önce yara veya kırık üzerindek: In this lesson, first it is told how to wipe over a bandage on a wound or fracture when washing under it would cause harm. Then it is told that washing the whole body, leaving no dry place, is called ghusl, that performing the ghusl is obligatory in the cases of ritual impurity after sexual relations, the end of menstruation and the end of postnatal bleeding, together with the three obligatory acts and the sunnahs of ghusl. It is taught that when a state that invalidates ablution continues without interruption throughout a whole prayer time, it is called an “excuse” and that the person with an excuse performs ablution again for each prayer time. Women’s special states, menstruation, postnatal bleeding and istihada, are told apart; it is stressed that in these states prayer cannot be performed, fasting cannot be kept and the prayers are not made up, but the fasts are made up. Finally the two obligatory acts of tayammum, performed when water cannot be found or used, and how it is performed are told.
plan.Guslün üç farzını sınıfça sözlü olarak s: Naming orally as a class the three obligatory acts of ghusl and writing them on the board.
plan.Kadınların özel hâllerinde (âdet, lohusa: Discussing as a class, in a table, which acts of worship can and cannot be performed in women’s special states (menstruation, postnatal bleeding, istihada).
plan.Teyemmümün hangi durumlarda uygulandığın: Classifying orally, through example situations (no water, illness, travel), in which cases tayammum is performed.
plan.Öğrenci, Ettehiyyâtü duasını oturuştaki: The student recites the Tahiyyat (Ettehiyyatu) prayer, saying its place in the sitting.
plan.Ettehiyyâtü duasının namaz oturuşlarında: It is taught that the Ettehiyyatu prayer is recited in the sittings of the prayer. The long prayer is divided into two parts according to meaning, and the students check their memorisation by listening in pairs.
plan.Öğrenci, Bedir zaferinden sonra esirlere: The student explains that treating prisoners well after the victory of Badr and releasing them in return for teaching reading and writing show the importance our Prophet gave to knowledge. • The student tells how the archer unit’s disobeying the order and leaving its place in the Battle of Uhud (625) changed the result of the battle and that our Prophet prayed even for his enemies in this bitter event. • Under the heading “Lessons to be drawn from the Battle of Uhud”, the student explains the consequences of not listening to elders and leaving one’s post. • The student tells of the digging of a trench around Medina in the Battle of the Trench (627), of the siege lasting 27 days and of the enemy’s dispersing through a violent storm.
plan.Bedir zaferinden sonra Peygamberimiz esi: After the victory of Badr our Prophet commanded that the prisoners be treated well; prisoners who could read and write were released after teaching ten Muslims. The polytheists, who wanted to avenge the defeat of Badr, came to Uhud a year later with an army of 3000; the Muslims first gained the upper hand, but when the archer unit did not obey our Prophet’s order ‘do not leave your places’ and went to gather spoils, the polytheists attacked from behind and even Hamza was martyred. Our Prophet, whose face was wounded, nevertheless prayed ‘O my Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know what they are doing’; the lesson of the importance of obeying orders was drawn from this event. Two years later, when the polytheists came again with an army of ten thousand, the Muslims dug a trench on the open side of Medina; at the end of the siege, which lasted twenty-seven days, a violent storm that came after our Prophet’s prayer scattered the enemy army, and the Meccans never attacked Medina again.
plan.Uhud Savaşı'nda okçuların yaptığı hatayı: Discussing as a class the mistake the archers made in the Battle of Uhud and the lesson drawn from it.
plan.Hendek Savaşı'nın nasıl kazanıldığını (h: Putting how the Battle of the Trench was won (the idea of digging a trench, the siege, the storm) in order on the timeline.
plan.Peygamberimizin Uhud'da yaralanmasına ra: Discussing the question “Why is forgiving important?” starting from our Prophet’s praying for his enemies despite being wounded at Uhud.
plan.Öğrenci, kötü alışkanlıkların (sigara, a: The student defines with examples what bad habits are (smoking, excessive screen/game addiction, small lies, bad words said in anger). • The student explains how bad habits begin and why they are continued. • Starting from verse 4 of Surah at-Tin, the student states that the human being was created as a valuable being. • The student lists the things that are valuable to them and gives reasons for the importance of protecting them. • The student lists the measures that can be taken to protect oneself from bad habits.
plan.Bu ünitede kötü alışkanlıklara yaklaşmam: In this unit the importance of keeping away from bad habits is treated. Negative behaviours such as smoking, excessive screen/game addiction, small lies and bad words said in anger are introduced with examples; how these habits begin and why they are continued is assessed as a class. Starting from verse 4 of Surah at-Tin, it is recalled that the human being was created by Allah in the best form and as a valuable being; it is stressed that everything that is valuable must be protected. The unit is completed by listing the measures that can be taken to protect oneself from bad habits.
plan.Ekranda gösterilen olumsuz davranış görs: Choosing orally as a class, and giving reasons for, the five worst from the pictures of negative behaviour shown on the screen.
plan.'Kötü alışkanlıklardan korunmak için ne: Forming an oral list as a class with the question ‘What can we do to protect ourselves from bad habits?’ (the teacher writes on the board).
plan.Tîn suresi ayetini okuyup 'insan neden d: Reading the verse of Surah at-Tin and answering orally, and discussing, as a class the question ‘Why is the human being valuable?’
plan.Öğrenci, Allâhümme Salli ve Allâhümme Bâ: The student recites the Allahumma salli and Allahumma barik prayers from memory in order.
plan.Allâhümme Salli ve Allâhümme Bârik duala: It is explained that the Allahumma salli and Allahumma barik prayers are recited in the final sitting. So as not to confuse the similar beginnings of the two prayers, the students repeat line by line and listen to one another.
plan.Öğrenci, Allah'ın varlığına ve birliğine: The student explains that believing in Allah’s existence and oneness is the most important duty of faith. • The student names by name the six essential attributes (dhati) and the eight affirmative attributes (thubuti). • The student tells apart the essential and the affirmative attributes with an example. • Starting from Umar’s story of the young girl, the student explains how the belief ‘Allah sees everywhere’ is reflected in behaviour. • The student expresses that love of Allah is shown by following His commands and avoiding what He forbids.
plan.TDB'nin üçüncü ünitesi Allah'a imanı ele: The third unit of the TDB deals with faith in Allah. Starting from the example that every work of art around us has an artist, it is shown that the universe too has a Creator, that is, Allah. Allah’s six essential attributes (existence, eternity without beginning, eternity without end, oneness, being unlike created things, self-subsistence) and eight affirmative attributes (life, knowledge, hearing, sight, will, power, speech, creating) are introduced. It is told that love of Allah is shown by noticing the blessings He gives and by following His commands. The reading passage about Umar and the young girl makes concrete how the belief ‘Allah sees me everywhere’ is reflected in behaviour.
plan.Hz. Ömer'in genç kız hikâyesini okuyup k: We read the story of Umar and the young girl and discuss as a class what the girl’s behaviour teaches us.
plan.Zatî ve sübûtî sıfatları sınıfça iki süt: We list the essential and affirmative attributes on the board as a class in two columns and illustrate the difference between them.
plan.'Allah' şiirini birlikte okuyup şiirde g: We read the poem ‘Allah’ together and try to find the attributes mentioned in the poem (such as seeing, hearing, greatness).
plan.Öğrenci, abdestin niyet ve besmeleyle na: The student shows how ablution begins with the intention and the Basmala. • The student shows in the correct order the sequence in which the limbs are washed and wiped during ablution (hands, mouth-nose, face, arms, head-ears-neck, feet). • The student completes ablution facing the qibla by reciting the Shahadah. • The student explains with examples the details to be paid attention to when performing ablution (between the fingers, under a ring, washing three times each).
plan.Bu ders, abdestin alınışını resimli anla: This lesson repeats how ablution is performed, in practice, through an illustrated explanation. First the rolling up of the sleeves, making the intention and reciting the Ta’awwudh and Basmala; then washing the hands up to the wrists three times, putting water into the mouth and nose and blowing it out, washing the face from where the hair grows down to under the chin, and washing the right and left arms together with the elbows are shown step by step. Then how to wipe the head, the ears and the neck is told; finally the washing of the right and left foot, starting from the tips of the toes and including the ankles. Ablution is completed standing and facing the qibla by reciting the Shahadah.
plan.Öğrenciler tek tek veya küme hâlinde abd: The students act out the movements of performing ablution (dry, without a washbasin) one by one or in groups, in place and in order, and their classmates check the order.
plan.Resimlerdeki adımları sınıfça sözlü olar: A competition is held of telling orally, in the correct order, the steps in the pictures.
plan.Abdestte erkek ve kız öğrencilerin ortak: Repeating orally as a class the movements in ablution that are common to boys and girls.
plan.Abdest niyeti: \"Niyet ettim Allah rızas: The intention for ablution: “I intend to perform ablution for the sake of Allah’s pleasure.”
plan.Öğrenci, Rabbenâ Âtinâ ve Rabbenağfirlî: The student recites the Rabbana atina and Rabbana-ghfir li prayers from memory in the correct order.
plan.Rabbenâ Âtinâ ve Rabbenağfirlî dualarını: It is taught that the Rabbana atina and Rabbana-ghfir li prayers can be recited in the final sitting of the prayer. The students repeat the short prayer formulas with hints of their meaning and recite them individually to the teacher.
plan.Öğrenci, Hudeybiye Antlaşması'nın (H.6/M: The student explains the terms of the Treaty of Hudaybiya (6 AH/628 CE) and that, although it looked heavy at first sight, it brought results beneficial to the Muslims. • The student names the letters inviting to Islam that our Prophet sent to the heads of neighbouring states and the words “Muhammadun Rasulullah” that he had engraved on his seal. • The student tells of the conquest of Khaybar and that our Prophet prayed for good even for his enemies. • The student explains that on the Kaaba visit a year later (the Umrat al-Qada), the good character of the Muslims was a means for people such as Khalid ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn al-As to become Muslims.
plan.Hicretin altıncı yılında Kâbe'yi ziyaret: In the sixth year of the Hijra, when the Muslims who went to visit the Kaaba were stopped by the Meccans, a treaty was made at Hudaybiya; the Muslims would turn back this year and visit the next year, staying three days. Although the terms looked heavy, Surah al-Fath, revealed on the way, announced the good news of victory; the treaty made the Meccans get to know the Muslims for the first time and hastened the spread of Islam. Our Prophet sent letters of invitation with the seal ‘Muhammadun Rasulullah’ to the rulers of Byzantium, Persia, Egypt and Abyssinia; the ruler of Abyssinia became a Muslim, while the ruler of Persia tore up the letter in anger. In the same period the Jews of Khaybar, who were preparing to attack Medina, were conquered; the Jews who asked for peace agreed to stay on their land and give half of the produce. On the Kaaba visit a year later (the Umrat al-Qada), the good character of the Muslims impressed the Meccans, and Khalid ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn al-As became Muslims.
plan.Hudeybiye Antlaşması'nın maddelerinden b: Choosing one of the terms of the Treaty of Hudaybiya and discussing as a class the question “why was this term important?”
plan.Peygamberimizin davet mektubu gönderdiği: Showing on the map the countries to which our Prophet sent letters of invitation and comparing orally the reactions of the rulers.
plan.Kaza Umresi'nde Müslümanların davranışla: Explaining with examples why the behaviour of the Muslims on the Umrat al-Qada impressed the Meccans.
plan.Öğrenci, 'Ben kimim' bilmecelerinden Yun: The student recognises Yunus Emre, Evliya Çelebi, Mimar Sinan, Nasreddin Hodja and Hezarfen Ahmed Çelebi from the ‘Who am I?’ riddles. • The student explains in which art or science these figures stood out. • Starting from verse 48 of Surah al-Ma’ida and verse 32 of Surah Fatir, the student interprets the importance of competing in good deeds. • The student summarises in their own sentences the emergence and importance of the art of calligraphy (Islamic calligraphy). • The student draws a conclusion about the value of learning and of being useful from the hadiths given (Bukhari, Bayhaqi, Tirmidhi).
plan.Bu ünitede İslam sanatı ve edebiyatına k: In this unit Muslim figures who contributed to Islamic art and literature are introduced. With the ‘Who am I?’ riddles the lives and works of Yunus Emre, Evliya Çelebi, Mimar Sinan, Nasreddin Hodja and Hezarfen Ahmed Çelebi are discovered. The importance of competing in good deeds is treated with verse 48 of Surah al-Ma’ida and verse 32 of Surah Fatir; the value of knowledge and of being useful with hadiths reported from Bukhari, Bayhaqi and Tirmidhi. By briefly introducing the emergence and development of the art of calligraphy, the students are helped to love the art and literary heritage of Islamic civilisation.
plan.'Ben kimim' bilmecelerini ekrana yansıtı: Solving and matching orally as a class the ‘Who am I?’ riddles with the pictures shown on the screen.
plan.Mimar Sinan ve Selimiye Camii hakkında b: Sharing orally as a class what is known about Mimar Sinan and the Selimiye Mosque.
plan.Verilen ayet ve hadislerden çıkarılan so: Explaining orally with examples, as a class, the conclusions drawn from the verses and hadiths given.
plan.Öğrenci, Kunut dualarını vitir namazında: The student recites the Qunut prayers, knowing their place in the witr prayer.
plan.Kunut dualarının vitir namazında okunduğ: It is explained that the Qunut prayers are recited in the witr prayer. The students divide the prayers into short pieces and repeat them; difficult words are worked on by spelling them out on the board.
plan.Öğrenci, meleklerin nurdan yaratılmış, c: The student explains that the angels are beings created from light, without gender and without sin. • The student lists the duties of the four great angels (Jibril, Mikail, Israfil, Azrail). • The student matches the duties of the Kiraman Katibin, Munkar and Nakir, Ridwan and Malik. • The student explains with the ‘angel’s voice – Satan’s voice’ example how faith in the angels discourages a person from evil.
plan.TDB'nin dördüncü ünitesi meleklere imanı: The fourth unit of the TDB deals with faith in the angels. It is told that the angels are beings created from light, without gender, who do not eat or drink and who never sin. The duties of the four great angels — Jibril, Mikail, Israfil, Azrail — and of the angels Kiraman Katibin, Munkar and Nakir, Ridwan and Malik are listed. The unit shows the benefits of believing in the angels with an example: the thought of helping a poor person is the angel’s voice, and the thought that tries to talk one out of it is Satan’s voice; a person should follow the voice that calls to good. This belief protects a person from evil even in moments when they think they are alone.
plan.Büyük melekleri ve görevlerini sınıfça s: We match the great angels and their duties orally as a class.
plan.'Fakire yardım et' diyen iç sesle 'yardı: We tell apart the inner voice that says ‘help the poor person’ from the inner voice that says ‘do not help’ and discuss which is the angel’s voice and which is Satan’s voice.
plan.Meleklerin her an yanımızda olduğunu bil: We give examples of how knowing that the angels are with us at every moment can change our behaviour.
plan.Öğrenci, namazın Miraç gecesinde farz kı: The student explains that the prayer was made obligatory on the night of the Mi‘raj and that it is the pillar of religion. • The student names the three conditions for the prayer to be obligatory (being a Muslim, having reached maturity and being of sound mind). • The student tells apart the start and end times of the five daily prayers and the three times at which it is not permissible to pray. • The student classifies the kinds of prayer (fard, wajib, nafila) with example prayers.
plan.Bu derste önce namazın İslam'ın ikinci ş: In this lesson, first it is told that the prayer is the second pillar of Islam, that it was made obligatory on the night of the Mi‘raj and that its importance is shown by the hadith of our Prophet (s.a.s.) “The prayer is the pillar of religion”. It is stated that the prayer is obligatory for a person who is a Muslim, mature and of sound mind. Then the times of the dawn, noon, afternoon, sunset and night prayers, and the times of the Friday, tarawih and Eid prayers are introduced, and it is stressed that prayer cannot be performed at the three times when the sun is rising, at its zenith and setting. Finally the prayers are divided into three kinds, fard (the five daily prayers, Friday, funeral), wajib (witr, the Eid prayers) and nafila (those attached to a fard and those not), and examples are given for each.
plan.Beş vakit namazın vakitlerini ve üç yasa: Naming the times of the five daily prayers and the three forbidden times orally as a class and writing them on the board.
plan.Namaz çeşitlerini (farz, vacip, nafile): Matching the kinds of prayer (fard, wajib, nafila) with example prayers in a three-column table as a class.
plan.\"Namaz dinin direğidir\" hadisini sınıf: Interpreting the hadith “The prayer is the pillar of religion” as a class and discussing orally why it was said so.
plan.Öğrenci, Ezan ve Kâmet metinlerini sıras: The student recites the texts of the adhan and the iqamah from memory, keeping their order.
plan.Ezan ve Kâmet metinleri sıraları ve kull: The texts of the adhan and the iqamah are taught with their order and where they are used. The students repeat the sentences without imitating the melody, with correct pronunciation and in the right order.
plan.Öğrenci, Hudeybiye Antlaşması'nın (628): The student explains the terms of the Treaty of Hudaybiya (628) and the wisdom of our Prophet’s accepting, for the sake of peace, even terms that seemed heavy. • The student tells that after the treaty was broken, Mecca was conquered in 630 without any blood being shed, with a general amnesty proclaimed. • The student summarises the cleansing of the Kaaba of idols and the speech in which our Prophet gave the message “Allah is One, everyone is equal”. • The student names the messages of the Farewell Pilgrimage and the Farewell Sermon of 632, such as the inviolability of life, property and honour and the equality of people. • The student says that our Prophet (s.a.s.) died in Medina in 632 and was buried in Aisha’s house.
plan.628 yılında Hz. Muhammed (s.a.s.) Kâbe'y: In 628 the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) set out to visit the Kaaba; when the Meccans did not allow it, a treaty was made at Hudaybiya: the Muslims would turn back this year, could visit for three days the next year, and there would be no fighting for ten years. When the treaty was broken, our Prophet marched on Mecca with a great army; Abu Sufyan became a Muslim, a general amnesty was proclaimed and Mecca was conquered in 630 without blood being shed. Our Prophet cleansed the Kaaba of idols and gave the people the message ‘Allah is One, no one is superior to anyone else, everyone is from Adam’. In the Farewell Sermon, which he delivered at Arafat during the pilgrimage of 632, he stressed the sanctity of life, property and honour, that everyone will receive the reward of what they do, and the equality of people. After completing his pilgrimage, our Prophet returned to Medina, fell ill two months later, and died on 27 May 632 and was buried in Aisha’s house.
plan.Hudeybiye Antlaşması'nın şartlarını ve M: Putting the terms of the Treaty of Hudaybiya and the conquest of Mecca in order on the timeline.
plan.Veda Hutbesi'nin mesajlarını kendi cümle: Writing the messages of the Farewell Sermon on the board in their own sentences and interpreting them as a class.
plan.\"Mekke fethedilirken neden af ilan edil: Discussing the question “Why was an amnesty proclaimed when Mecca was conquered?” by linking it with our Prophet’s peaceful attitude.
plan.Öğrenci, ahlakın tanımını yapar ve iyi i: The student defines morality (akhlaq) and explains how good and bad habits settle in our soul. • Starting from the hadith of our Prophet (s.a.s.) ‘I was sent to perfect good character’ and Aisha’s saying ‘His character was the Qur’an’, the student explains that the Prophet Muhammad is the most beautiful example of good character. • The student expresses with an example the importance of honesty and halal earnings in work and trade. • With the similes of the ‘perfume shop’ and the ‘blacksmith’s shop’, the student explains the effect of good and bad company on our character. • The student links the value the religion of Islam gives to reason and knowledge with verse 9 of Surah az-Zumar and the relevant hadith.
plan.Bu ünitede ahlakın tanımı ve İslam'da ah: In this unit the definition of morality and its place in Islam are treated. Through the hadith of our Prophet (s.a.s.) ‘I was sent to perfect good character’ and Aisha’s saying ‘His character was the Qur’an’, it is told that the Prophet Muhammad is the most beautiful example of good character. How belief and worship (prayer, fasting, zakat) nourish good character is explained. The importance of honesty and halal earnings in working life is stressed. With the similes of the ‘perfume shop’ and the ‘blacksmith’s shop’, the effect of good and bad company on a person is told. The unit is completed with the high value Islam gives to reason and knowledge.
plan.Peygamberimizin ahlakı hakkındaki hadisl: Reading orally and interpreting as a class the hadiths about our Prophet’s character.
plan.'Güzel koku dükkânı' ve 'demirci dükkânı: Explaining the ‘perfume shop’ and ‘blacksmith’s shop’ simile with oral example situations (a good friend – a bad friend).
plan.'Bir Müslüman nasıl kazanır, nasıl harca: Sharing oral examples and discussing as a class the question ‘How does a Muslim earn and how does a Muslim spend?’
plan.Öğrenci, öğrendiği temel dua ezberlerini: The student has the teacher listen, without mistakes, to the basic prayers they have memorised.
plan.Tevhid ifadeleri, Âmentü ve namaz dualar: The expressions of oneness, the Amantu and the prayers of the prayer are checked with an individual listening list. The students mark what they are missing, and the teacher tells each student their next memorisation goal.
plan.Öğrenci, vahyin tanımını yapar ve dört v: The student defines revelation and names the four kinds of revelation. • The student tells apart the scrolls (suhuf) and the four great books and says which book was sent to which prophet. • The student explains that the first revelation of the Qur’an began in the Cave of Hira with the first five verses of Surah al-‘Alaq. • The student expresses in their own sentences that the Qur’an was revealed over 23 years, verse by verse and surah by surah, and the concept of ‘the occasion of revelation’ (sabab an-nuzul).
plan.TDB'nin beşinci ünitesi kitaplara imanın: The fifth unit of the TDB treats revelation and the sending down of the Qur’an as the first half of faith in the books. It is introduced that revelation is one of the ways in which Allah conveys knowledge to His prophets, in four kinds: the true dream, inspiration, speech from behind a veil and revelation through an angel. It is stated that the Qur’an came through the fourth kind of revelation, by means of Jibril (peace be upon him). It is told that the small books called suhuf were sent down to Adam, Seth, Idris and Abraham, and the four great books as the Torah to Moses, the Psalms to David, the Gospel to Jesus and the Qur’an to Muhammad (s.a.s.). The unit ends with the first revelation at Hira and the 23-year process of revelation.
plan.Dört vahiy çeşidini sınıfça sözlü olarak: We list the four kinds of revelation orally as a class and find a short example for each.
plan.Suhuf ve dört büyük kitabın hangi peygam: We match the scrolls and the four great books with the prophet to whom each was sent and write them on the board.
plan.İlk vahyin Alâk suresinin ilk beş ayeti: We learn that the first revelation was the first five verses of Surah al-‘Alaq and read the meaning of these verses together as a class.
plan.Öğrenci, namazın on iki farzını; namazın: The student distinguishes the twelve obligatory elements of the prayer as six conditions outside the prayer and six pillars inside it. • The student names at least five of the wajib acts of the prayer with examples. • The student gives examples of the sunnahs of the prayer: reciting the adhan and iqamah, raising the hands at the takbirs and the glorifications in bowing and prostration. • The student lists the main things that invalidate the prayer (talking, eating and drinking, laughing, turning away from the qibla). • The student gives examples of the disliked acts (makruh) of the prayer (fidgeting with the body or clothes, yawning).
plan.Bu derste namazın on iki farzı; namazın: In this lesson the twelve obligatory elements of the prayer are recalled as the six conditions outside the prayer (purity from ritual impurity, purity from filth, covering the awra, facing the qibla, the time, the intention) and the six pillars inside it (the opening takbir, standing, recitation, bowing, prostration, the final sitting). Then the wajib acts of the prayer, such as beginning the prayer with “Allahu Akbar”, reciting the Fatiha and performing the prostration of forgetfulness, are listed. The sunnahs of the prayer, such as reciting the adhan and iqamah, raising the hands at the takbirs, reciting the Subhanaka and the Fatiha in order and saying the glorification three times in bowing and prostration, are told. Finally the things that invalidate the prayer, such as talking in the prayer, eating or drinking something and turning away from the qibla, and the disliked acts of the prayer, such as fidgeting with the body or clothes and yawning, are treated with examples.
plan.Namazın on iki farzını sınıfça \"namazın: Grouping the twelve obligatory elements of the prayer on the board as a class in a two-column table: “conditions outside the prayer / pillars inside it”.
plan.Namazı bozan durumları ve namazın mekruh: Distinguishing the things that invalidate the prayer from the disliked acts of the prayer with oral examples and classifying them as “invalidates / is makruh”.
plan.Rükû ve secdede okunan tesbihleri sınıfç: Repeating aloud as a class the glorifications recited in bowing and prostration.
plan.Öğrenci, Nâs ve Felak surelerini doğru s: The student recites Surah an-Nas and Surah al-Falaq from memory in the correct order.
plan.Felak ve Nâs sureleri, mushaftaki sırala: Surah al-Falaq and Surah an-Nas are introduced in their order in the mushaf and in the context of prayers for protection. The students listen to the two surahs verse by verse, repeat them and work in pairs so as not to confuse the similar endings.
plan.Öğrenci, Huneyn Savaşı'nda (630) Müslüma: The student tells that in the Battle of Hunayn (630) the Muslims were first scattered, then rallied through our Prophet’s courage and won the victory. • The student says that the Battle of Awtas completed the victory of Hunayn, that the siege of Ta’if lasted a month and was lifted without the fortress being taken, and that the people of Ta’if later became Muslims. • The student explains that in the Expedition of Tabuk (630) the great army prepared against Byzantium deterred the enemy without entering battle. • The student tells of the help given for the Expedition of Tabuk by Abu Bakr, Uthman and the women as an example of the Companions’ self-sacrifice.
plan.Mekke'nin fethinden sonra putperest Hava: After the conquest of Mecca, the idol-worshipping tribe of Hawazin attacked the Muslims at Hunayn with an army of 20,000; the Muslim army, which was scattered at first, rallied through the courage and voice of our Prophet (s.a.s.) and won the victory. The fleeing enemy was chased as far as Awtas and routed; those who took refuge in the fortress of Ta’if withstood a month-long siege, the Muslims lifted the siege, but the people of Ta’if later became Muslims of their own accord. When news came a year later that Byzantium was preparing to stop the spread of Islam, an army of thirty thousand, equipped with the donations of Abu Bakr, Uthman and the women, marched as far as Tabuk; the enemy did not dare to fight and shut themselves in their fortresses, and the Muslims returned without fighting.
plan.Huneyn Savaşı'nın başında Müslümanların: Telling orally, in the order of events, the scattering of the Muslims at the start of the Battle of Hunayn and then their rallying through our Prophet’s voice.
plan.\"Taifliler kuşatmadan sonra neden kendi: Discussing as a class the question “Why did the people of Ta’if become Muslims of their own accord after the siege?”
plan.Tebük Seferi'nde ashabın yardımlarını (H: Listing on the board the help given by the Companions in the Expedition of Tabuk (Abu Bakr, Uthman, the women).
plan.Öğrenci, Allah'a, Peygamberimize ve Kur': The student lists the duties they must fulfil towards Allah, our Prophet and the Holy Qur’an. • The student explains with examples their duties towards their body (balanced nutrition, protecting health, cleanliness). • Starting from our Prophet’s hadith ‘Cleanliness is half of faith’, the student interprets the place of cleanliness in religion. • The student explains that taking precautions and seeking treatment when ill does not conflict with the belief in trust in Allah (tawakkul). • The student expresses in their own sentences that they should cleanse their soul of bad habits and adorn it with good thoughts and good character.
plan.Bu ünitede kendimize karşı yerine getirm: In this unit the moral duties we must fulfil towards ourselves are treated. First the duties towards Allah, our Prophet and the Holy Qur’an are briefly recalled. Then the duties towards our body are treated, supported with hadiths, under the headings of balanced nutrition, protecting health and seeking treatment when ill, and taking care of cleanliness. The importance of bodily cleanliness is stressed with the hadith ‘Cleanliness is half of faith’ and the example of the miswak. Finally the duties towards our soul are told: that we should cleanse our soul of bad habits and adorn it with good thoughts and good character.
plan.Bedenimize karşı görevler (beslenme, tem: Expanding the list of duties towards our body (nutrition, cleanliness, health) with oral examples as a class.
plan.'Temizlik imanın yarısıdır' hadisini oku: Reading the hadith ‘Cleanliness is half of faith’ and finding oral examples from daily life.
plan.Ruhumuzu süsleyecek güzel huylar ile tem: Saying orally as a class the good habits with which we should adorn our soul and the bad habits we should cleanse it of (the teacher writes on the board).
plan.Öğrenci, İhlâs suresini duraklarına dikk: The student recites Surah al-Ikhlas from memory, paying attention to its pauses.
plan.İhlâs suresi kısa ayetlerle ve tevhid vu: Surah al-Ikhlas is taught with its short verses and its stress on tawhid. The students first follow the surah from the page, then recite it from memory, keeping to the teacher’s pauses.
