plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an'ın mushaf hâline getiril: The student lists the roles of Abu Bakr and Uthman in the process of compiling the Qur’an into a mushaf. • The student explains at least three of the features that distinguish the Holy Qur’an from other holy books (being preserved, being revealed piece by piece, being the last book, universality, being a miracle). • The student lists at least four of our duties towards the Qur’an (reading it in a state of ablution, holding it with respect, keeping silent when listening to it, etc.). • The student chooses five of the hadiths on the virtue of reading the Qur’an and says them with their meaning.
plan.TDB'nin beşinci ünitesinin bu bölümü, Ku: This part of the fifth unit of the TDB deals with the writing down of the Qur’an, its compilation into a mushaf and its features. It is told that the scribes of the revelation wrote the verses down, that a commission set up in the time of Abu Bakr collected the pages of the Qur’an and compiled them into a mushaf, and that Uthman copied it and sent it to various cities. The features that distinguish the Qur’an from other holy books (being preserved without any change, being revealed piece by piece, being the last book, being sent to all humanity, being a miracle) are listed. The unit includes our duties towards the Qur’an and the task of memorising five hadiths on the virtue of reading the Qur’an.
plan.Kur'an'ın mushaf hâline getiriliş süreci: We put the process of compiling the Qur’an into a mushaf (the writing down, Abu Bakr’s commission, Uthman’s copying) in order as a class.
plan.Kur'an'a karşı görevlerimizi maddeler hâ: We write our duties towards the Qur’an point by point on the board and find an example from daily life for each point.
plan.Kur'an okumanın fazileti hakkındaki hadi: We choose five of the hadiths about the virtue of reading the Qur’an, memorise them and say them in turn in class.
plan.Öğrenci, Kur'an okumanın fazileti hakkın: The student chooses five of the hadiths in the book about the virtue of reading the Qur’an and memorises them; example: ‘The best of you are those who learn the Qur’an and teach it.’
plan.Öğrenci, namazın mekruhlarından camide c: The student gives examples of the disliked acts (makruh) of the prayer, such as prostrating towards a picture of a living being in the mosque or standing behind when there is open space in front. • The student performs in practice, in the right order, the two rak‘as of sunnah and two rak‘as of fard of the dawn prayer from the intention to the greeting. • The student performs in practice, in the right order, the four rak‘as of the first sunnah, the four rak‘as of fard and the two rak‘as of the final sunnah of the noon prayer. • The student explains at least two of the differences in posture between men and women in the prayer (the degree of bending in bowing, the way of sitting).
plan.Bu derste önce namazın kalan mekruhları: In this lesson, first the remaining disliked acts of the prayer (such as prostrating towards a picture of a living being, or standing behind in the mosque while leaving the front row open) are completed. Then it is recalled that the prayer must be performed in accordance with its fard, wajib and sunnah acts, avoiding what invalidates it and what is disliked. The two rak‘as of sunnah of the dawn prayer are told in practice with the steps of intention, the opening takbir, standing, recitation, bowing, prostration and greeting, also noting the differences in posture between men and women; then the fard of the dawn prayer is performed in the same order. Finally the four rak‘as of the first sunnah, the four rak‘as of fard and the two rak‘as of the final sunnah of the noon prayer are treated step by step, with the Subhanaka, the Fatiha, the surah, the glorifications and the prayers recited in each rak‘a.
plan.Öğle namazının ilk sünnet, farz ve son s: Naming orally as a class the numbers of rak‘as of the first sunnah, the fard and the final sunnah of the noon prayer and writing them on the board.
plan.Erkek ve kadınların namazdaki duruş fark: Comparing orally the differences in posture between men and women in the prayer (bowing, sitting).
plan.Sabah namazının farzına niyet: \"Niyet e: The intention for the fard of the dawn prayer: “I intend to perform, for the sake of Allah’s pleasure, the fard of today’s dawn prayer.”
plan.Öğle namazının farzına niyet: \"Niyet et: The intention for the fard of the noon prayer: “I intend to perform, for the sake of Allah’s pleasure, the fard of today’s noon prayer.”
plan.Öğrenci, Kevser, Asr ve Nasr surelerini: The student reads Surah al-Kawthar, al-‘Asr and an-Nasr without confusing them with one another.
plan.Kevser, Asr ve Nasr sureleri kısa ayet y: Surah al-Kawthar, al-‘Asr and an-Nasr are practised taking their short verse structures into account. The students repeat each surah with a different rhythm and start the matching memorised text when they hear the surah’s name.
plan.Öğrenci, münafıkların kurduğu Mescid-i D: The student tells the purpose of the Mosque of Dirar, set up by the hypocrites, and how our Prophet had this mosque demolished on his return from Tabuk. • The student explains with the verses in Surah al-Hajj and Surah al-Baqara that our Prophet’s battles did not have the aim of attack but were defensive wars fought to protect religion, life and property. • The student says that in the ninth year of the Hijra Abu Bakr was sent as the leader of the pilgrimage and that this pilgrimage was the first one in line with the principles of Islam. • The student explains that in the tenth year of the Hijra, in the Farewell Pilgrimage made with more than a hundred thousand Muslims, the verse “Today I have perfected your religion for you” was revealed.
plan.Münafıkların Müslümanları bölmek için Me: The Mosque of Dirar, which the hypocrites had built near Medina to divide the Muslims, was revealed by Allah, and our Prophet had the building demolished on his return from the Expedition of Tabuk. The verses in Surah al-Hajj and Surah al-Baqara declare that Muslims were permitted to fight only when they were wronged and without going beyond the limit; therefore our Prophet’s battles were not attacks but defensive wars aimed at protecting religion, life and property. In the ninth year of the Hijra our Prophet sent Abu Bakr to Mecca with three hundred people as the leader of the pilgrimage; Ali announced that idolaters could no longer come to the pilgrimage and that the Kaaba could no longer be circled naked; this became the first pilgrimage in line with the principles of Islam. In the tenth year of the Hijra our Prophet went on the Farewell Pilgrimage with more than a hundred thousand Muslims; after he delivered the Farewell Sermon at Arafat, the verse ‘Today I have perfected your religion for you’ was revealed.
plan.Mescid-i Dırar'ın gerçek amacının ne old: Telling orally what the real aim of the Mosque of Dirar was and how our Prophet responded to it.
plan.\"Savunma savaşı\" ile \"saldırı savaşı\: Discussing as a class the difference between a “defensive war” and an “offensive war”, starting from the verses of Surah al-Hajj and Surah al-Baqara.
plan.Hz. Ebû Bekir'in hac emirliğinde duyurul: Listing on the board the new rules announced during Abu Bakr’s leadership of the pilgrimage.
plan.Öğrenci, yemede ve içmede uyulması gerek: The student names at least five of the rules of conduct to be followed in eating and drinking (saying the Basmala, eating with the right hand, not wasting, etc.). • The student explains with examples the rules to be followed for training the tongue (not lying, not backbiting, keeping secrets). • Starting from our Prophet’s hadith ‘Guard your tongue’, the student interprets the importance of having control over the tongue. • The student expresses with examples what it means to protect the hands, eyes and ears from what is forbidden. • Starting from verse 31 of Surah al-A‘raf and verse 67 of Surah al-Furqan, the student explains the middle way between waste and stinginess.
plan.Bu ünitede yemede ve içmede uyulması ger: In this unit the rules of conduct to be followed in eating and drinking, and the training of the tongue and the other parts of the body, are treated. The etiquette of the table, such as beginning with the Basmala, eating with the right hand and not wasting, is listed point by point. In the section on training the tongue, rules such as not lying, not backbiting and keeping secrets are supported with the hadith ‘Guard your tongue’. It is told that the hands, eyes and ears must be protected from what is forbidden. The unit is completed with a reading text that stresses, with verse 31 of Surah al-A‘raf and verse 67 of Surah al-Furqan, the importance of a balanced and measured life between waste and stinginess.
plan.Yemek adabı kurallarından sınıfça en öne: Choosing orally, and giving reasons for, the five most important rules of table etiquette as a class.
plan.'Dilimizi nasıl koruyabiliriz' sorusuyla: Oral role-play on example situations (moments of speaking and of keeping silent) with the question ‘How can we guard our tongue?’
plan.Ekmek ve su israfı örnekleri üzerinden ': An oral class discussion on ‘the places where we see waste around us’ through examples of wasting bread and water.
plan.Öğrenci, Tebbet suresini mahreç ve durak: The student recites Surah al-Masad from memory, paying attention to points of articulation and pauses.
plan.Tebbet suresi kelime telaffuzlarına dikk: Surah al-Masad is drilled paying attention to the pronunciation of the words. The students memorise the verses with a short chain of repetition and read the places that contain qalqala distinctly.
plan.Öğrenci, peygamberlere neden ihtiyaç old: The student explains why prophets are needed by linking it to the fact that a human being cannot grasp Allah’s attributes alone. • The student names the five common attributes of the prophets (sidq, amana, fatana, isma, tabligh) with their definitions. • The student says the first and the last of the prophets mentioned by name in the Holy Qur’an. • The student lists the three principles (belief, worship, morality) common to the religions that all the prophets conveyed.
plan.TDB'nin altıncı ünitesinin bu bölümü pey: This part of the sixth unit of the TDB deals with the institution of prophethood. It is told that people cannot know Allah’s exalted attributes, the forms of worship and the life of the hereafter by their own reason, and that for this reason Allah sent prophets. The duties of the prophets (making Allah known, teaching the principles of belief and worship, being an example) and their five common attributes (sidq, amana, fatana, isma, tabligh) are introduced. The list of the 25 prophets mentioned by name in the Holy Qur’an is given; it is recalled that the first prophet was Adam and the last prophet is Muhammad (s.a.s.). It is stressed that in the religions that all the prophets conveyed, the principles of belief, worship and morality did not change.
plan.Peygamberlerin beş sıfatını sınıfça taht: We write the five attributes of the prophets on the board as a class and add a short definition to each.
plan.Kur'an-ı Kerim'de ismi geçen 25 peygambe: We read together the list of the 25 prophets mentioned by name in the Holy Qur’an and mark the names we know.
plan.'Peygamberlere neden ihtiyaç vardır?' so: We discuss the question ‘Why are prophets needed?’ as a class and form a shared answer.
plan.Öğrenci, ikindi, akşam ve yatsı namazlar: The student shows in practice the numbers and order of the sunnah, fard and final sunnah of the afternoon, sunset and night prayers. • The student explains the difference between the first sunnah of the noon prayer (emphasised) and the sunnah of the afternoon prayer (non-emphasised). • The student performs saying the qunut takbir and reciting the qunut prayer in the third rak‘a of the witr prayer. • The student recognises the salawat, the glorifications and Ayat al-Kursi recited in order after the fard prayer.
plan.Bu derste ikindi namazının dört rekât sü: In this lesson the four rak‘as of sunnah and four rak‘as of fard of the afternoon prayer, the three rak‘as of fard and two rak‘as of sunnah of the sunset prayer, and the four rak‘as of the first sunnah, four rak‘as of fard and two rak‘as of the final sunnah of the night prayer are performed in order. The small difference in performance between the first sunnah of the noon prayer being emphasised and the sunnah of the afternoon prayer being non-emphasised is explained. It is taught that in the three-rak‘a witr prayer performed after the night prayer, the hands are raised after the Fatiha and the surah in the third rak‘a and the qunut prayer is recited. Finally it is told that after the fard prayer the prayer “Allahumma anta as-salam”, the salawat, the glorifications of Subhanallah-Alhamdulillah-Allahu Akbar thirty-three times each, the Declaration of Oneness and Ayat al-Kursi are recited in order.
plan.Vitir namazının üçüncü rekâtında kunut d: Acting out as a class where the qunut prayer is recited in the third rak‘a of the witr prayer.
plan.Namazdan sonra okunan salavat, tesbihler: Repeating orally the order of the salawat, the glorifications and Ayat al-Kursi recited after the prayer.
plan.Namazdan sonra otuz üçer kere: \"Sübhâna: After the prayer, thirty-three times each is said: “Sübhânallah”, “Elhamdülillah”, “Allâhu Ekber”.
plan.Ardından: \"Lâ ilâhe illallâhu vahdehû l: Then: “Lâ ilâhe illallâhu vahdehû lâ şerike leh, lehü’l-mülkü ve lehü’l-hamdü ve hüve alâ külli şey’in kadîr.”
plan.Öğrenci, Kâfirûn suresini ayet sırasını: The student recites Surah al-Kafirun from memory without disturbing the order of the verses.
plan.Kâfirûn suresindeki tekrar eden ayet yap: The repeating verse structures in Surah al-Kafirun are shown with coloured marks. The students rehearse their memorisation with order cards so as not to confuse the similar verses.
plan.Öğrenci, Veda Hutbesi'nin insan hakları: The student says that the Farewell Sermon brought provisions protecting human rights long before the universal declaration of human rights. • The student names the nine basic principles announced in the Farewell Sermon (equality, the inviolability of life, property and honour, keeping trusts, the prohibition of interest, the abolition of blood feuds, the rights of women and men, brotherhood, treating servants well). • The student explains in their own sentences our Prophet’s advice “look after the rights of women” and “a Muslim is the brother of a Muslim”. • The student says that our Prophet left the Qur’an as a trust and advised holding fast to it.
plan.Peygamberimizin Arafat'ta okuduğu Veda H: In the Farewell Sermon that our Prophet delivered at Arafat, every sentence was repeated aloud and conveyed to the whole congregation; this sermon brought provisions protecting human rights long before the universal declaration of human rights. In the sermon it was announced that all people are equal, that superiority is measured only by respect for Allah, that life, property and honour are sacred and inviolable, that trusts must be returned to their owners, and that interest and blood feuds are abolished. It was stressed that men must respect the rights of women and women the rights of men, that servants must be treated well, that all Muslims are brothers and that the right of a brother in faith cannot be violated. So that they would not lose their way, our Prophet left the Holy Qur’an to the Muslims as a trust.
plan.Veda Hutbesi'nin dokuz ilkesini tahtaya: Writing the nine principles of the Farewell Sermon point by point on the board and finding an example from daily life for each.
plan.\"Faizin ve kan davalarının kaldırılması: Discussing as a class the question “Why was the abolition of interest and blood feuds important?”
plan.Peygamberimizin kadın hakları ve kardeşl: Expressing orally, in their own sentences, our Prophet’s words about the rights of women and about brotherhood.
plan.Öğrenci, ailenin toplumdaki önemini ve a: The student explains in their own sentences the importance of the family in society and the principle that a nation is formed by the joining of families. • The student lists the duties of children towards their parents (kindness, having a cheerful face, obedience, praying for them). • The student expresses the lesson drawn from the story of the young man who was disobedient to his parents (the reading text). • The student explains with examples the importance of love, respect and visiting among brothers, sisters and relatives. • The student names their duties towards neighbours (kindness, not disturbing, visiting the sick) and realises that one must also treat a neighbour of a different religion well.
plan.Bu ünitede ailemize karşı görevlerimiz e: In this unit our duties towards our family are treated. That the family is the foundation of society, the duties of husband and wife towards each other, and the duties of parents towards their children and of children towards their parents are told, supported with hadiths. Through the reading text on the distress that a young man who was disobedient to his parents suffered at his last breath, the importance of the rights of parents is stressed. Love and unity among brothers and sisters, love, respect and visiting for relatives, kindness to neighbours, not disturbing them and the duty to treat even a neighbour of a different religion well are treated with examples.
plan.'Anne-babama karşı görevlerim' başlığınd: Forming an oral list as a class under the heading ‘My duties towards my parents’ (the teacher writes on the board).
plan.Anne-babasına asi olan genç hikâyesini d: Listening to the story of the young man who was disobedient to his parents and interpreting it orally as a class.
plan.Fatih Sultan Mehmet'in çarşı hikâyesini: Acting out orally as a class the story of Mehmed the Conqueror and the market, and drawing out the principles of neighbourliness.
plan.Öğrenci, Mâûn suresini doğru telaffuz ve: The student recites Surah al-Ma‘un from memory with correct pronunciation and pauses.
plan.Mâûn suresi sosyal sorumluluk vurgusu kı: Surah al-Ma‘un is taught with its stress on social responsibility briefly pointed out. The students repeat the surah verse by verse and identify the letters of prolongation and the silent letters together with the teacher.
plan.Öğrenci, mucize ile keramet arasındaki f: The student explains the difference between a miracle (mu‘jiza) and a saintly wonder (karama). • The student tells at least three of the miracles of our Prophet (s.a.s.) (water gushing from his fingers, the date-palm trunk moaning, the Isra and Mi‘raj). • The student names at least three of our Prophet’s superior features among the other prophets. • The student expresses, grounding it in the Qur’an, that the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.s.) is the last prophet and that no prophet will come after him.
plan.TDB'nin altıncı ünitesinin bu bölümü muc: This part of the sixth unit of the TDB deals with the concepts of miracle and saintly wonder, our Prophet’s miracles and his being the last prophet. It is explained that a miracle is peculiar to prophets, an extraordinary event shown by Allah’s permission, while a saintly wonder is a similar event that takes place for servants who are friends of Allah. As examples are given the water gushing from our Prophet’s (s.a.s.) fingers, the date-palm trunk moaning, the Isra and Mi‘raj, and the Holy Qur’an, which is his greatest and everlasting miracle. Our Prophet’s superior features over the other prophets and his being the last prophet are told by likening the earlier prophets to a lamp and him to the sun.
plan.Peygamberimizin mucizelerinden birini se: We choose one of our Prophet’s miracles and tell it to the class in our own sentences.
plan.'Önceki peygamberler kandil gibiydi, Pey: We explain the simile ‘The earlier prophets were like lamps, our Prophet is like the sun’ in our own sentences.
plan.Okuma bölümünde geçen batılı düşünürleri: We choose one of the sayings of Western thinkers about our Prophet that appear in the reading section and discuss why it may have been said.
plan.Öğrenci, sehiv secdesinin ne zaman ve na: The student explains when and how the prostration of forgetfulness is made. • The student grounds the virtue of praying in congregation in a hadith and recognises the parts of the mosque (mihrab, minbar, pulpit, minaret, balcony, finial). • The student explains how a person who catches up with the imam in different rak‘as completes their prayer. • The student names how many rak‘as the Friday prayer has and for whom it is obligatory (six conditions). • The student lists the conditions for the Friday prayer to be valid (the sermon, the congregation, the place, an authorised imam).
plan.Bu derste önce namazda unutarak bir farz: In this lesson, first it is taught when and how the prostration of forgetfulness is made when, in the prayer, an obligatory or wajib act has been forgotten, delayed or left out. Hadiths stating that praying in congregation is twenty-seven times more rewarding than praying alone, mosque etiquette and the parts of the mosque (mihrab, minbar, pulpit, minaret, balcony, finial) are introduced. How a person following the imam completes the prayer if they catch up in the bowing of the first rak‘a, in the second rak‘a or in a later rak‘a is told step by step. Finally it is treated that the Friday prayer is ten rak‘as, that it takes the place of the noon prayer, for whom it is obligatory (six conditions such as being male, free, resident and healthy) and the conditions necessary for it to be valid (being performed at noon time, a sermon being delivered, at least three in the congregation being present).
plan.Sehiv secdesinin ne zaman ve nasıl yapıl: Naming orally as a class when and how the prostration of forgetfulness is made and, if possible, showing it in practice.
plan.Caminin bölümlerini (mihrab, minber, kür: Defining orally as a class the parts of the mosque (mihrab, minbar, pulpit, minaret, balcony, finial) and matching them on the board.
plan.Cuma namazının kimlere farz olduğunu ve: Dividing into two lists as a class, and classifying on the board, for whom the Friday prayer is obligatory and the conditions for its validity.
plan.Öğrenci, Kureyş ve Fîl surelerini ayrı s: The student recites Surah Quraysh and Surah al-Fil from memory as separate surahs.
plan.Fîl ve Kureyş sureleri, mushaftaki sıral: Surah al-Fil and Surah Quraysh are introduced in their order in the mushaf and with their links of meaning around the Kaaba. The students work on the two surahs separately with verse cards and recite from memory, saying the surah’s name.
plan.Öğrenci, Peygamberimizin (s.a.s.) hastal: The student tells that during his illness our Prophet (s.a.s.) had Abu Bakr lead the prayers and tells of the advice he gave his daughter Fatima. • Taking as an example our Prophet’s going up to the minbar two days before his death to settle accounts with his Companions, the student explains the concepts of ‘the rights of others’ and ‘settling accounts’. • The student says that our Prophet (s.a.s.) died on 8 June 632 (10 AH) at the age of 63 and was buried in the Rawda al-Mutahhara. • The student tells of the grief of the Companions at our Prophet’s death and how Abu Bakr consoled them.
plan.Veda Haccı'ndan sonra hastalanan Peygamb: Our Prophet (s.a.s.), who fell ill after the Farewell Pilgrimage, appointed Abu Bakr to lead the prayers; he advised his daughter Fatima to do good deeds and told his Companions that they would meet again at the edge of the Kawthar pool. Two days before his death he went up to the minbar and settled accounts with his Companions, asking that whoever he had wronged take their right. On Monday, 8 June 632 (12 Rabi‘ al-Awwal, the 10th year of the Hijra), at noon, with his last words being ‘Refîk-i A‘lâ’, he died at the age of sixty-three, and the place where he was buried is known in Medina as the Rawda al-Mutahhara; of his 23 years of prophethood he had spent 13 years in Mecca and 10 years in Medina. His death plunged the Muslims into great grief; some of the Companions did not want to believe it, and Abu Bakr came and consoled them.
plan.Peygamberimizin vefatından önce ashabıyl: Discussing as a class, with the question “why is it important?”, our Prophet’s settling accounts with his Companions before his death.
plan.Hz. Fâtıma'ya yapılan nasihati kendi cüm: Repeating orally, in their own sentences, the advice given to Fatima.
plan.Peygamberimizin hayatını (doğum-vefat) z: Completing our Prophet’s life (birth–death) on the timeline and showing the length of the Meccan and Medinan periods.
plan.Öğrenci, yaşadığımız ülkeye ve topluma k: The student explains the importance of unity, brotherhood and tolerance within the framework of duties towards the country and society we live in. • The student links verse 103 of Surah Al Imran (‘Hold fast to the rope of Allah all together and do not be divided’) and our Prophet’s hadith ‘The believers are like a building whose parts are bound to one another’ with the principle of unity. • Starting from verse 10 of Surah al-Hujurat, the student explains the bond of brotherhood among Muslims and the importance of reconciling those who have fallen out. • Starting from the examples of tolerance that our Prophet (s.a.s.) showed to people, the student interprets how people of different beliefs and views should be treated. • The student explains, with an example from the environment they live in, how unity and tolerance, rather than division, bring peace to society.
plan.Bu ünite, Temel Dinî Bilgiler'deki 'Vata: This unit has been adapted, in a way suited to our students living in Belgium, from the unit ‘Our Duties Towards Our Country and Our People (I)’ in Basic Religious Knowledge (Temel Dinî Bilgiler); only the universal principles of unity, brotherhood and tolerance have been used, and the parts about Turkish history, the flag and the national anthem have not been included in the lesson. The importance of being united is told with verse 103 of Surah Al Imran and our Prophet’s hadith ‘The believers are like a building whose parts are bound to one another’. Starting from verse 10 of Surah al-Hujurat, the brotherhood of Muslims and the duty of reconciling those who have fallen out are treated. Through our Prophet’s (s.a.s.) examples of tolerance, how we should treat people of different views in the society we live in is told.
plan.Sınıfta yaşanmış küçük bir dargınlık örn: Oral role-play, with the question ‘How do we reconcile them?’, on an example of a small quarrel that has happened in class.
plan.Peygamberimizin hoşgörü örneklerini dinl: Listening to our Prophet’s examples of tolerance and answering orally as a class the question ‘How can we too be tolerant?’
plan.'Birlikte yaşadığımız arkadaşlarımızla n: Holding an oral brainstorm as a class on ‘How do we live in unity with the friends we live together with?’ (the teacher writes on the board).
plan.Öğrenci, öğrendiği kısa sureleri adları: The student recites from memory the short surahs they have learnt when their names are called.
plan.Fâtiha ile birlikte Asr, Fîl, Kureyş, Mâ: Together with the Fatiha, the surahs al-‘Asr, al-Fil, Quraysh, al-Ma‘un, al-Kawthar, al-Kafirun, an-Nasr, al-Masad, al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas are checked with individual listening and group repetition. The students write the surahs they started wrongly or confused on a revision list.
plan.Öğrenci, ahiret gününe imanın imanın alt: The student says that faith in the Last Day is the fifth of the six articles of faith. • The student explains with examples three of the benefits of faith in the hereafter (a sense of responsibility, preparation for the hereafter, consolation). • The student defines the concepts of death, the grave and the Day of Resurrection in the correct order. • The student expresses, grounding it in verses, for whom reward and punishment, Paradise and Hell, are prepared.
plan.TDB'nin yedinci ünitesi ahiret gününe im: The seventh unit of the TDB deals with faith in the Last Day. The Day of Resurrection that will begin with Israfil’s blowing the Trumpet, the gathering at the place of assembly, the Kiraman Katibin angels’ handing over the records of deeds and the weighing on the scale of justice are told. The benefits of faith in the hereafter — giving a sense of responsibility, preparing a person for the hereafter and consoling those who have been wronged — are treated under three separate headings. The concepts of death, the grave (with the questioning by Munkar and Nakir) and the Day of Resurrection are defined in turn. The unit ends by explaining, grounding it in verses, for whom reward and punishment, Paradise and Hell, are prepared.
plan.Ahirete imanın üç faydasını (sorumluluk,: We explain the three benefits of faith in the hereafter (responsibility, preparation, consolation) with examples as a class.
plan.Ölüm, kabir ve kıyamet kavramlarını doğr: We match the concepts of death, the grave and the Day of Resurrection in the correct order and write them on the board.
plan.'Kıyamet gününde insan dört şeyden sorgu: We read the hadith ‘On the Day of Resurrection a person will be questioned about four things’ and discuss how these four questions relate to our lives.
plan.Öğrenci haccın İslam'ın beş şartından bi: The student names the hajj as one of the five pillars of Islam and lists the conditions needed for it to become obligatory (reason, maturity, freedom, being a Muslim, ability (istita‘a)). • The student recognises by name the three obligatory acts of the hajj (ihram, the standing at Arafat, the tawaf of visit) and briefly explains each. • The student tells apart the basic differences between Ifrad, Tamattu‘ and Qiran hajj and states the ruling on slaughtering a sacrifice for each. • The student puts the order of performing the hajj (ihram → tawaf/sa‘y → Mina → the standing at Arafat → Muzdalifa → Eid practices) in the correct order. • The student defines the umrah, explains the steps of performing it and expresses how it differs from the hajj. • The student defines basic hajj concepts such as the talbiyah, tawaf, sa‘y, the standing and the miqat and gives concrete examples.
plan.Hac, İslam'ın beş şartından biri olup be: The hajj is one of the five pillars of Islam and a comprehensive act of worship performed at certain times and in certain places. Being of sound mind, mature, free and a Muslim, and having financial and physical ability (istita‘a), are among the basic conditions for the hajj to become obligatory; for every Muslim who meets these conditions, performing the hajj once in a lifetime is obligatory. The obligatory acts of the hajj are entering the ihram, making the standing at Arafat and performing the tawaf of visit. The hajj can be performed in three kinds: Ifrad hajj, in which the ihram is entered for the hajj alone; Tamattu‘ hajj, in which in the hajj season of the same year the umrah is performed first and then the hajj, and which makes the slaughter of a sacrifice wajib; and Qiran hajj, performed with the intention for the hajj and the umrah together.
plan.Öğrenci, Hümeze suresini mahreç hataları: The student recites Surah al-Humaza from memory, reducing mistakes in points of articulation.
plan.Hümeze suresi zor kelimeleri hecelenerek: Surah al-Humaza is practised with the difficult words spelled out and their points of articulation stressed. The students repeat the verses in small sections and recite them to the teacher one by one.
plan.Öğrenci, Peygamberimizin (s.a.s.) vefatı: The student says that after the death of our Prophet (s.a.s.) Abu Bakr was chosen as caliph and that our Prophet left no worldly property as inheritance, his greatest legacy being the light of Islam and the principles of good character. • The student names our Prophet’s seven children (Qasim, Abdullah, Ibrahim; Zaynab, Ruqayya, Umm Kulthum, Fatima) and tells how our Prophet corrected the wrong belief about the solar eclipse at the death of his son Ibrahim. • The student names the concept of the “Ashara al-Mubashshara” and the ten Companions who were given the good news of Paradise. • The student defines the concepts of “the Companions (Ashab)”, “Muhajir” and “Ansar”.
plan.Peygamberimizin (s.a.s.) vefatından sonr: After the death of our Prophet (s.a.s.), Abu Bakr was chosen as caliph; our Prophet left nothing as worldly property, his greatest legacy being the light of Islam and the principles of good character. Of his seven children, Qasim and Abdullah died young, and Ibrahim, born in Medina after the Hijra, also died at a young age; when the sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim died, some linked it with his death, and our Prophet corrected this wrong belief by saying that the sun and the moon are not eclipsed for anyone’s death or life. All his daughters married, and except for Fatima they died before our Prophet; his lineage continued through Fatima, who married Ali. The ten Companions whom our Prophet gave the good news of Paradise are called the ‘Ashara al-Mubashshara’ (Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali and six other Companions). Those who saw our Prophet and died as Muslims are called the ‘Companions (Ashab)’; they are divided into two: the ‘Muhajirun’, who migrated from Mecca, and the ‘Ansar’, the people of Medina who helped them.
plan.Peygamberimizin yedi çocuğunun adlarını: Grouping the names of our Prophet’s seven children on the board as boys/girls.
plan.Aşere-i Mübeşşere'nin on ismini ekrana y: Showing the ten names of the Ashara al-Mubashshara on the screen and repeating them in order.
plan.\"Muhacir\" ve \"Ensar\" kavramlarını ör: Explaining orally, with examples, the concepts “Muhajir” and “Ansar”.
plan.Öğrenci, 'birlikten kuvvet doğar, ayrılı: The student explains with an example the principle ‘strength is born of unity, division leads to disaster’. • The student expresses in their own sentences the lesson drawn from the story ‘A Father’s Advice’ (the bundle of sticks). • Starting from our Prophet’s (s.a.s.) hadith ‘Allah’s help is with the community’, the student explains the strength of acting in unity. • The student links the fact that being respectful of the laws and public order of the country one lives in is a religious responsibility with verse 59 of Surah an-Nisa. • The student explains the social importance of paying taxes and contributing to shared services.
plan.Bu ünite de, Temel Dinî Bilgiler'deki 'V: This unit too has been adapted from the unit ‘Our Duties Towards Our Country and Our People (II)’ in Basic Religious Knowledge (Temel Dinî Bilgiler); the parts on martyrdom, veterans, military service and national holidays have been left out and only the principles of being united and respecting the law have been used. The strength of being united is told with the hadith ‘In togetherness there is mercy, in division there is punishment’ and the story of the bundle of sticks that a father told his sons. Our Prophet’s hadith ‘Allah’s help is with the community’ is treated. Starting from verse 59 of Surah an-Nisa, it is told that being respectful of the laws and public order of the country we live in and contributing to shared services (such as taxes) is a religious responsibility.
plan.'Bir baba nasihatı' hikâyesini dinleyip: Listening to the story ‘A Father’s Advice’ and acting it out orally as a class (telling the simile of breaking a single stick and sticks in a bundle).
plan.Kanunlara ve kamu düzenine uymanın günlü: Listing orally as a class examples from daily life of obeying the laws and public order (queuing, not dropping litter, a traffic rule, etc.).
plan.'Birlik olursak ne kazanırız, ayrılırsak: An oral class discussion with the question ‘What do we gain if we are united, and what do we lose if we are divided?’
plan.Öğrenci, Kevser suresini doğru okur ve k: The student reads Surah al-Kawthar correctly and explains its relation to the sacrifice. · Illustrating the meaning of the surah.
plan.Kevser suresi okunur ve meali işlenir; ': Surah al-Kawthar is read and its meaning is treated; the verse ‘So pray and sacrifice to your Lord ˹alone˺.’ (al-Kawthar 108/2) is dwelt on.
Illustrating the meaning of the surah.
plan.Öğrenci, kurbanın dayandığı kıssayı ve t: The student tells the story on which the sacrifice is based and the meaning of submission. · Telling the story in their own sentences.
plan.Kurban ibadetinin dayandığı teslimiyet k: The story of submission on which the act of worship of the sacrifice is based is told by reading verses 102-107 of Surah as-Saffat; the concepts of trust in Allah and obedience are treated.
Telling the story in their own sentences.
plan.Öğrenci, kurban etinin nasıl paylaşılaca: The student tells how the meat of the sacrifice is shared and says the takbir of tashriq. · Drawing a diagram of sharing the sacrifice.
plan.Kurbanın hükmü, kimlere vacip olduğu, et: The ruling on the sacrifice, for whom it is wajib, and the sharing of its meat; the Eid prayer and the takbirs of tashriq are taught. It is stated that the takbirs of tashriq are recited at 23 prayer times, from the dawn prayer of the day of Arafa (15 May 2027) until the afternoon prayer of the fourth day of the Eid (19 May 2027), and that the sacrifice can be slaughtered on the first, second and third days of the Eid.
Drawing a diagram of sharing the sacrifice.
plan.Öğrenci, Tekâsür suresini duraklara dikk: The student recites Surah at-Takathur from memory, paying attention to the pauses.
plan.Tekâsür suresi tekrar eden sesler ve dur: Surah at-Takathur is taught dwelling on its repeating sounds and pauses. The students move from chorus repetition to individual reading by reading the ends of the verses distinctly.
plan.Öğrenci, Peygamberimizin (s.a.s.) insanl: The student tells with examples the compassion our Prophet (s.a.s.) showed to people and animals (giving water to a thirsty cat, loving children, his tolerance towards Hasan and Husayn). • The student explains our Prophet’s humility, simplicity and gentle nature that never scolded anyone (Enes’s testimony). • The student says with examples that because of his honesty our Prophet was known as “Muhammad al-Amin” (Muhammad the Trustworthy), and his generosity and forgiveness. • The student links the importance our Prophet gave to cleanliness, to treating women well and to hard work with an example from their own life.
plan.Peygamberimiz (s.a.s.) insanlara ve hayv: Our Prophet (s.a.s.) was very compassionate towards people and animals; he had given a thirsty cat water to drink with his own hand, he loved children, and he showed tolerance to his grandsons Hasan and Husayn when they climbed on his shoulders during the prayer. Without distinguishing between rich and poor he would accept even a servant’s invitation; according to Enes, who served him for ten years, he never scolded anyone for any of his work and never said a bad word to anyone. Because of his honesty and trustworthiness he was called ‘Muhammad al-Amin’ (Muhammad the Trustworthy); he was the most generous of people and forgave even those who did evil to him. He mended his clothes with his own hands, gave great importance to cleanliness and told his Companions to come clean; he advised treating women well, did not like laziness, and even on a journey divided the work with his companions and worked himself.
plan.Peygamberimizin merhamet, doğruluk, cöme: Choosing one of our Prophet’s examples of compassion, honesty, generosity, cleanliness and hard work and finding a similar behaviour from our daily life.
plan.Enes'in Peygamberimiz hakkındaki tanıklı: Reading Enes’s testimony about our Prophet as a class and discussing what “not scolding anyone” means.
plan.\"Muhammedü'l-Emin\" unvanının anlamını: Explaining orally the meaning of the title “Muhammad al-Amin” and why this title was given.
plan.Öğrenci, 'kimseye zarar vermemek' ilkesi: The student explains the principle ‘do not harm anyone’ within the framework of respect for people’s life, property, honour and dignity. • The student names with examples social duties such as greeting one another, reconciling those who have fallen out, and visiting the sick and friends. • The student links the importance of respecting elders and showing mercy to the young with the relevant hadith. • The student explains with examples from hadiths about a cat and a dog that tormenting animals is a sin. • The student expresses with examples the etiquette of hosting guests and of going to an invitation.
plan.Bu ünitede bütün insanlara ve hayvanlara: In this unit our duties towards all people and animals are treated. Duties such as not harming anyone, helping, respecting elders and showing mercy to the young, greeting one another, reconciling those who have fallen out, visiting the sick and hosting a guest well are listed, supported with hadiths. Then our duties towards animals are treated; through the stories in the hadiths of the woman who let a cat die of hunger and the man who gave water to a thirsty dog, it is told that tormenting animals is a sin and showing mercy is rewarded.
plan.İnsanlara karşı görevler listesinden (se: Choosing orally, and giving reasons for, the five most important from the list of duties towards people (greeting, reconciling, visiting, hosting) as a class.
plan.Kedi ve köpekle ilgili hadisleri dinleyi: Listening to the hadiths about a cat and a dog and giving oral examples as a class to the question ‘How can we treat animals well?’
plan.Sınıfta iki arkadaşın dargın olduğu bir: Acting out a situation in which two friends in class have fallen out and analysing orally the question ‘How do we reconcile them?’
plan.Öğrenci, Kâria suresini bölümleri birleş: The student recites Surah al-Qari‘a from memory by joining the sections.
plan.Kâria suresi iki kısa bölüm hâlinde tali: Surah al-Qari‘a is drilled in two short sections. The students repeat first the first section and then the second, and at the end of the lesson join the surah from beginning to end.
plan.Öğrenci, kader ve kaza kavramlarını dinî: The student defines the concepts of destiny (qadar) and divine decree (qada) as religious terms. • The student explains with an example the difference between things outside a person’s own will and things that depend on their will. • The student expresses that believing in destiny gives a person the strength to work and a sense of responsibility. • The student defines the concepts of provision (rizq) and the appointed time of death (ajal) and links them with destiny.
plan.TDB'nin sekizinci ünitesi kader ve kazay: The eighth unit of the TDB deals with faith in destiny and divine decree. Destiny is defined as Allah’s knowing from eternity and determining what will happen; divine decree (qada) as the taking place of this determination when its time comes. A person’s actions are divided into two: a person is not responsible for things that happen outside their will, such as the working of the heart, but is responsible for what they do with their own will, such as walking and speaking. It is told that the belief in destiny gives a person the determination to work and a sense of responsibility, and does not make them fall into pessimism in the face of disasters. The unit ends with the definitions of provision and the appointed time of death and their relation to a person’s working.
plan.İnsanın istemsiz işleri (kalp atışı, boy: We separate in two columns, as a class, a person’s involuntary actions (such as the heartbeat and height) and voluntary actions (such as walking and speaking).
plan.'Kader inancı insanı çalışmaktan alıkoya: We discuss the question ‘Does the belief in destiny keep a person from working?’ as a class and reach a shared conclusion.
plan.Rızık ve ecel kavramlarını kendi cümlele: We define the concepts of provision and the appointed time of death in our own sentences and give examples.
plan.Öğrenci, oturarak veya ima ile namaz kıl: The student explains in which situations the prayer is performed sitting or by gesture. • The student lists the conditions for being counted as a traveller (musafir) and the prayer concessions granted to a traveller (such as shortening four rak‘as to two). • The student explains the difference between performing a prayer on time (ada’) and making it up (qada’) and states which prayers can be made up. • The student tells when the prostration of recitation becomes wajib and how it is performed inside and outside the prayer. • The student explains the conditions of the funeral prayer, how it is performed with four takbirs and its character as a collective obligation (fard kifaya).
plan.Bu derste önce namazı ayakta kılamayan b: In this lesson, first it is told that a person who cannot pray standing can pray sitting or by pointing with the head (by gesture). Then the concessions granted to a traveller (musafir) on a journey of 90 kilometres are treated with examples such as performing the four-rak‘a fard prayers as two rak‘as and being able to wipe over leather socks for three days and three nights. It is told that performing a prayer in its time is called ada’ and performing it after its time has passed qada’; that the fard prayers and the witr can be made up while the sunnahs are not made up. How the prostration of recitation, which is wajib for whoever reads or hears the verse of prostration in the fourteen surahs of the Qur’an that contain one, is performed inside and outside the prayer is taught. Finally it is told that the funeral prayer is a collective obligation (fard kifaya), performed with four takbirs and without bowing or prostration, with the six conditions necessary for it to be performed and the order of its performance.
plan.Yolcu (misafir) sayılmanın şartlarını ve: Listing with oral examples as a class the conditions for being counted as a traveller (musafir) and the prayer concessions granted to a traveller.
plan.Eda ile kaza arasındaki farkı sınıfça ör: Discussing as a class the difference between ada’ and qada’ through example situations (oversleeping, forgetting).
plan.Cenaze namazının dört tekbirini ve arala: Repeating orally, in order, as a class the four takbirs of the funeral prayer and what is recited between them.
plan.Cenaze duasını bilmeyenler şu âyeti dua: Those who do not know the funeral prayer recite this verse with the intention of a prayer: “Rabbenâ âtinâ fi’d-dünyâ haseneten ve fi’l-âhireti haseneten ve kınâ azâbe’n-nâr.” (Meaning: “Our Lord! Grant us the good of this world and the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”)
plan.Öğrenci, Âdiyât suresini ayet sırasını k: The student recites Surah al-‘Adiyat from memory, keeping the order of the verses.
plan.Âdiyât suresi hızlı akışa kapılmadan açı: Surah al-‘Adiyat is practised with clear pronunciation, without being carried away by a fast flow. The students repeat the short verses rhythmically and bring out the places of qalqala together with the teacher.
plan.Sahabenin Peygamberimize bağlılığı; Muha: The Companions’ devotion to our Prophet; the Muhajirun and the Ansar; the Rightly Guided Caliphs (Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali); the Ashara al-Mubashshara: the four caliphs together with Talha ibn Ubaydullah, Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, Abd ar-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, Sa‘id ibn Zayd and Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah.
plan.Sahabi isim kartlarıyla eşleştirme oyunu: A matching game with Companion name cards. / Each student tells one good quality of a Companion.
plan.Dört halifenin isimleri: The names of the four caliphs
plan.Öğrenci, İslam ahlakına uygun yaşayan bi: The student names at least five of the characteristics of a Muslim who lives by Islamic morality (honesty, trustworthiness, forgiveness, helpfulness). • The student defines the concept of ‘haram’ in our religion and gives examples of forbidden behaviours. • The student explains the harm that alcoholic drinks and drugs do to human health and to the order of society. • Starting from our Prophet’s hadith ‘Every intoxicating drink is haram’, the student interprets the reason for this prohibition. • The student expresses in their own sentences the importance of being able to say ‘no’ to bad habits and harmful friendships.
plan.Bu ünitede İslam ahlakına uygun yaşayan: In this unit the characteristics of a Muslim who lives by Islamic morality are introduced point by point; qualities such as honesty, trustworthiness, forgiveness, helpfulness and patience are listed. Then the concept of ‘haram’ is defined in our religion and examples of forbidden behaviours such as lying, cheating and gambling are given. The unit is completed with a reading text that tells of the harm that alcoholic drinks and drugs do to human health, reason and the order of society; together with our Prophet’s hadith ‘Every intoxicating drink is haram’, the importance of keeping away from these substances and of being able to say ‘no’ to bad friendships is stressed.
plan.İyi Müslümanın özellikleri listesinden s: Choosing orally, and giving reasons for, the five most important from the list of the characteristics of a good Muslim as a class.
plan.Haram listesinden günlük hayatta karşıla: Discussing orally as a class examples from the list of haram things that can be met in daily life.
plan.'Arkadaşımız bize kötü bir şey teklif et: Acting out orally as a class an example situation with the question ‘What do we do if a friend suggests something bad to us?’ (practice in saying ‘no’).
plan.Öğrenci, Zilzâl suresini durak ve uzatma: The student recites Surah az-Zalzala from memory, paying attention to pauses and lengthening.
plan.Zilzâl suresi ayet sonlarındaki duraklar: Surah az-Zalzala is taught paying attention to the pauses at the ends of the verses. The students repeat the surah in two sections and read slowly together with the teacher over the long words.
plan.Öğrenci, tevekkülün 'elinden geleni yapı: The student explains with the farmer example that trust in Allah (tawakkul) means ‘doing what one can and leaving the result to Allah’. • The student expresses in their own sentences the lesson drawn from the hadith ‘First tie your camel, then trust in Allah’. • The student explains with an example that working for halal earnings has the value of worship in Islam. • Starting from the story of the man who cut wood, the student states that working is better than begging.
plan.TDB'nin sekizinci ünitesinin bu bölümü t: This part of the eighth unit of the TDB deals with trust in Allah and the importance of work. Trust in Allah is defined, with the example of a farmer who ploughs and sows his field and then leaves the result to Allah, as ‘doing what one can and expecting the result from Allah’; it is recalled that to a person who said he trusted in Allah without tying his camel, our Prophet said ‘First tie your camel, then trust in Allah’. It is told that working for halal earnings has the value of worship, and that our Prophet had a Companion who asked for help sell his belongings and buy an axe to cut wood, and said that this was better than begging. The unit ends with a reading passage telling how planting a tree is counted as charity.
plan.Çiftçi örneğini dinleyip 'gerçek tevekkü: We listen to the farmer example and discuss as a class the difference between ‘true trust in Allah’ and ‘waiting without working at all’.
plan.Odun kesen adamın hikâyesini okuyup Peyg: We read the story of the man who cut wood and explain orally why our Prophet helped him in this way.
plan.'Ağaç dikelim' okuma parçasını okuyup ağ: We read the passage ‘Let Us Plant Trees’ and share with the class why planting a tree is counted as charity.
plan.Öğrenci, sabah namazının iki rekât farzı: The student performs in practice, in the right order, the two rak‘as of fard of the dawn prayer from the intention to the greeting. • The student shows with examples the differences in posture between men and women in every movement of the prayer (takbir, standing, bowing, prostration, sitting, greeting). • The student practises how the hands are opened and held when praying at the end of the prayer.
plan.Bu ders, sabah namazının iki rekât farzı: This lesson has the two rak‘as of fard of the dawn prayer repeated in practice from beginning to end through an illustrated explanation. The intention, the opening takbir, folding the hands in standing, reciting the Subhanaka, the Fatiha and a surah, bowing, rising from bowing, prostration, sitting between the two prostrations, rising to the second rak‘a, the prayers recited in the final sitting and giving the greeting to the right and left are shown step by step. At each step the small differences in the posture of the hands, arms, feet and sitting of boys and girls (for example the degree of bending in bowing and the position of the feet in sitting) are treated separately. Finally it is taught that when praying at the end of the prayer, the hands are held at chest level, palms turned towards the face and slightly apart.
plan.Sınıf, sabah namazının iki rekât farzını: The class performs together, in practice, the two rak‘as of fard of the dawn prayer in the order in the pictures (dry, on the prayer mat).
plan.Öğrenciler ikişerli eşleşip birbirinin n: The students pair up and check one another’s posture in the prayer (takbir, bowing, prostration, sitting) by comparing it with the pictures.
plan.Namaz sonunda dua ederken ellerin doğru: Practising together as a class the correct way of holding the hands when praying at the end of the prayer.
plan.Öğrenci, Beyyine suresini bölümler hâlin: The student follows Surah al-Bayyina in sections and begins reading from memory.
plan.Beyyine suresi yıl sonuna hazırlık için: Surah al-Bayyina is drilled divided into sections in preparation for the end of the year. The students follow the difficult verses from the page and give the teacher their first reading of the section to be memorised, to complete it with revision at home.
plan.Siyer alanında dönem boyunca işlenen kon: In the area of the life of the Prophet (sira), the topics covered during the term are revised in chronological order and an assessment is made; in the second semester the boycott and the Year of Sorrow, the Hijra and the first years in Medina, the battles of Badr, Uhud and the Trench, the Treaty of Hudaybiya, the conquest of Mecca and the Farewell Sermon had been treated.
plan.Ahlak alanında dönem boyunca işlenen kon: In the area of good character, the topics covered during the term are revised and an assessment is made; in the second semester Islam and aesthetics, good character, the contribution of Muslims to civilisation, bad habits, our moral duties, and our duties towards the family, the country and all people had been treated.
plan.Öğrenci, yıl sonunda Kur'an-ı Kerim okum: At the end of the year the student shows the teacher their achievements in reading and memorising the Holy Qur’an.
plan.Yıl boyunca öğrenilen elifbâ, yüzünden o: The achievements in the alphabet (elifba), reading from the page, tajwid and memorisation learnt during the year are assessed with an individual reading file. Each student does a short Qur’an reading, has the teacher listen to texts chosen from the memorisation list and receives their goal for the new year.
plan.İtikat alanında dönem boyunca işlenen ko: In the area of creed, the topics covered during the term are revised and an assessment is made; in the second semester divine decree and destiny, learning the hadiths, the features of the religion of Islam, faith and the six articles of faith (faith in Allah, the angels, the books, the prophets, the hereafter, and divine decree and destiny) had been treated.
plan.İbadet alanında dönem boyunca işlenen ko: In the area of worship, the topics covered during the term are revised and an assessment is made; in the second semester the prayer (I–II), fasting, zakat, the hajj, the sacrifice and blessed days and nights had been treated.
